headline: Rahul, Akhilesh, Mamata to participate in ‘Constitution Protection March’ in Bhopal
content: Bhopal Senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and Mamata Banerjee, will attend a ‘Constitution Protection March’ in Bhopal on December 12, 2026. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/indian-national-congress/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/Rahul_Gandhi/ The march is expected to draw between 1 lakh and 1.5 lakh people, according to the Madhya Pradesh Congress Committee (MPCC), which has sought the Lal Parade Ground in Bhopal as the venue for the rally, MPCC media coordinator Abhinav Barolia told PTI. Congress to hold ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches across States on Constitution Day, Kharge to join programme in Lucknow Congress to hold ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches across States on Constitution Day, Kharge to join programme in Lucknow The marches will begin at statues of Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi, followed by a reading of the Preamble and an oath to protect the Constitution Congress to hold ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches across States on Constitution Day, Kharge to join programme in Lucknow storyline 1 The Congress had earlier announced plans to launch a nationwide campaign in December against what it calls “vote theft” and to protect the Constitution, with Mr. Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra expected to lead the movement. Madhya Pradesh Congress president Jitu Patwari had said that safeguarding democracy and every citizen’s right to vote remained the party’s top priority. Mr. Barolia said the march will begin from Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s statue, where Mr. Gandhi will pay a floral tribute to the architect of the Constitution. It will pass in front of the district court, the old jail and the control room before reaching Lal Parade Ground, where a rally will be held. Former West Bengal Chief Minister Ms. Banerjee is also scheduled to attend, he said. Congress media department chairman Mukesh Nayak said the party was awaiting the administration’s decision on the venue. He expressed apprehension that obstacles could be created for the Bhopal event, as allegedly happened in Indore in connection with Mr. Gandhi’s function, and said repeated uncertainty over the venue would affect preparations. Take constitutional patriotism to the people Take constitutional patriotism to the people Waving pocket editions of the Constitutions is an empty ritual if the Opposition and civil society fail to champion constitutional patriotism CONSTITUTION DAY, NOVEMBER 26 Take constitutional patriotism to the people opinion 1 Mr. Nayak said the Congress needed the ground at least seven days before the rally to make arrangements for domes, sound systems, barricades and other infrastructure, and has urged the administration to make the venue available in advance. A Congress delegation, including Mr. Nayak and other office-bearers, met Additional Commissioner of Police Monika Shukla on Friday (November 27, 2026) and submitted a memorandum seeking permission for the venue. Mr. Nayak said Ms. Shukla informed the delegation that the permission process involved coordination with the traffic department and the Seventh Battalion. He said the application would be forwarded to the battalion through police headquarters as per procedure, and the delegation would be informed about the decision on Saturday (November 28, 2026) or Sunday (November 29, 2026).

headline: Tamil Nadu library scam: Every reader of a spurious book becomes an invisible victim of an unpardonable crime, says Special Court
content: CHENNAI Filling the shelves of a library with fake books containing misleading contents by fictitious authors is a grave offence against civilisation and culture, with every reader of such spurious books becoming an invisible victim of the unpardonable crime, the Special Court for Prevention of Corruption Act cases in Chennai said on Saturday (November 28, 2026). Special Judge L.S. Sathiyamurthy wrote: “A library is a symbol of civilisation and culture. It is a think tank that promotes learning among the children and youth, besides assisting research scholars who seek authentic reference materials. Its shelves are a sanctuary of wisdom, archives of human thoughts, heaven of learning, and a wardrobe of history, literature, and science.” The impact of fraudulent books on the moral rights of authors The impact of fraudulent books on the moral rights of authors The alleged purchase of fraudulent books, some with phantom authors, by a public library in Coimbatore using crores of public money raises concerns over authorship and moral rights, and underscores the need for a framework for stakeholders to verify authorship and address complaints The impact of fraudulent books on the moral rights of authors storyline 1 He went on to state: “If such shelves are filled with fake books by fictitious authors, plagiarised pages, and spurious books with misleading contents, it is a grave offence against civilisation and culture. These types of worst books will soon destroy the public libraries of Tamil Nadu and meet the fate of the Library of Alexandria (which suffered destruction in Egypt).” The judge also said that every reader of a spurious book would be an invisible victim of a crime whose magnitude could not be measured in numbers. He said that the loss or damage caused to thesociety due to the circulation of such fake books would be irreparable and unpardonable. The observations were made while permitting the custodial interrogation of the prime accused in the public libraries book purchase scam in Tamil Nadu. Tamil Nadu public libraries book purchase scam: Madras High Court nominates DGP Venkataraman to monitor DVAC probe Tamil Nadu public libraries book purchase scam: Madras High Court nominates DGP Venkataraman to monitor DVAC probe Justice V. Lakshminarayanan empowers the nominated officer to suggest measures to the investigating officer and directs the Director of Vigilance and Anti Corruption to coordinate with him Tamil Nadu public libraries book purchase scam: Madras High Court nominates DGP Venkataraman to monitor DVAC probe storyline 1 What is the scam about? Mr. Sathiyamurthy permitted the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) sleuths to subject R. Mohan, 63, to custodial interrogation. He had been operating Agal Vilakku Pathipagam and Phoenix Publications from the same address at Madipakkam in Chennai and was accused of supplying AI-generated, substandard, and misleading books to various public libraries in the State after receiving ₹1.74 crore from the public exchequer. Stating that the DVAC could subject the accused to custodial interrogation for three days between November 28, 2026, and November 30, 2026, the judge said: “The custodial interrogation may be helpful in ascertaining the quantum of fake books procured for the libraries and the ‘experts’ who suggested such dubious publications for public libraries and all other materials and incidental facts necessary to comprehensively approach this crime.” Books from Periyar Arivulagam sent to DVAC headquarters for investigation into purchase scam Books from Periyar Arivulagam sent to DVAC headquarters for investigation into purchase scam Books from Periyar Arivulagam sent to DVAC headquarters for investigation into purchase scam storyline 1 Special Public Prosecutor K. Usharani told the court that the magnitude of the crime had been increasing day by day ever since the presence of fake books in a library at the Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore came to light recently. She said that a Government Order (G.O.) was issued on September 9, 2024, sanctioning ₹50 crore for the procurement of books for the Periyar Arivulagam library. Thereafter, the School Education Department issued another G.O. on November 5, 2025, for procuring the books, and one more G.O. was issued on February 27, 2026, for the advance release of ₹30 crore from the Consolidated Fund. The prime accused, Mohan, had sent an e-mail to the Director of Libraries and submitted a list of 2,339 titles under Agal Vilakku Pathipagam and 99 titles under Phoenix Publications. Release White Paper on books procured for libraries in the last 20 years, High Court tells T.N. government Release White Paper on books procured for libraries in the last 20 years, High Court tells T.N. government Hearing a case pertaining to the alleged ‘scam’ in the procurement of books for public libraries, the court says the revelations has shaken the conscience of the people of Tamil Nadu and the faith in the system must be restored Release White Paper on books procured for libraries in the last 20 years, High Court tells T.N. government storyline 1 Subsequently, purchase orders for 1,857 books were issued to these two publishers on February 13 and 14, 2026. The investigation revealed that Agal Vilakku Pathipagam had made bulk registrations of its books on the International Standard Book Number (ISBN) portal on February 4 and 5, 2026, coinciding with a meeting of a high-level committee constituted to approve the list of books to be purchased for public libraries. “Six authors were credited with 745 books across unrelated subjects, including 48 books each by Thamarai Murali and Lakshmi Mohan, both receiving ISBNs on February 5, 2026, raising serious concerns regarding the authenticity of the authorship... Phoenix Publications had registered 2,923 books under various languages in the ISBN portal with 74 authors common to both publishing concerns,” the SPP said. DVAC registers criminal case over alleged irregularities in the purchase of books DVAC registers criminal case over alleged irregularities in the purchase of books The criminal case has been registered against a Chennai-based publisher and “unidentified officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai, and Periyar Arivulagam, Coimbatore. On Monday (November 16, 2026), DVAC officials launched a search at seven places and seized receipt vouchers for book procurement and other documents. Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers, was arrested DVAC registers criminal case over alleged irregularities in the purchase of books storyline 1 She also said: “The enquiry revealed that the prime accused had created books using fictitious author names and content sourced from websites and online applications, including ChatGPT. The books were found to contain vague, irrelevant, misleading, and substandard content, lacking educational or informational value for public libraries.”

headline: Mumbai Customs team seizes drugs, gold worth ₹39.8 crore at airport; nine arrested
content: Mumbai “Customs officials at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai have seized narcotic substances and gold collectively valued at around ₹39.8 crore in multiple operations, leading to the arrest of nine passengers and suspected cartel members,” sources said. In one of the biggest seizures, officers of the Air Intelligence Unit (AIU), Customs Zone-III, recovered around 12 kg of ketamine, valued at approximately ₹36 crore, in an operation conducted on November 27. headline: Economy to sustain growth momentum in Dec quarter, but near-term inflation risks persist: finance ministry review
content: India's economic activity continued its strong momentum midway into the December quarter, buoyed by consumption demand, a “gradual broadening of private investment”, and continued policy support for manufacturing, the finance ministry said on Saturday.Near-term inflation, however, is likely to remain under pressure due to an unfavourable base effect and weather-related uncertainties, including the possibility of a strong El Niño, the ministry said in its economic review for November.A moderation in crude oil prices to below $100 a barrel and a strengthening rupee could help contain imported inflation, if sustained, it added.“Nevertheless, the evolving geopolitical situation, alongside uncertainty surrounding global trade policies, could weigh on the outlook,” the ministry said.The continuing West Asia conflict and risks to the Strait of Hormuz – a vital global energy chokepoint – may keep the oil import bill and maritime freight rates volatile. “These supply-side shocks threaten to feed into broader wholesale and retail price indices in the coming months,” it said.Still, domestic economic fundamentals and macroeconomic buffers provide India the capacity to navigate emerging challenges, the review added.The economy is expected to have grown 7.35% in the September quarter, the ministry had said earlier, citing its nowcasting model, after a strong provisional expansion rate of 7.8% in the three months through June. India remains the world's fastest-expanding major economy, with global agencies, including the International Monetary Fund, projecting FY27 growth at 7% or higher.The provisional September quarter growth data will be released on Monday.Retail inflation, however, scaled a two-year peak of 6.09% in October, breaching the upper limit of the central bank's 2% to 6% inflation tolerance band. A little more than half the items in the consumer price basket saw inflation less than 4%.Strong demandBusiness activity will likely remain firm, with new orders gaining traction and input cost pressures easing, according to the review. “Domestic demand should stay supportive, with sequential momentum in vehicle sales and continued strength in rural consumption,” it said.Meanwhile, high-frequency gauges across goods movement, tax collections, energy consumption, and freight continue to expand.While winter crop sowing and water reserves are trailing from the levels a year before, adequate fertiliser supply bodes well for the rabi season, the ministry said.Industrial production grew 6.7% in September. Manufacturing activity expanded in October, bank credit to industry strengthened. The output of core infrastructure industries grew 10.9% in October from a year before, while cumulative growth between April and October stood at 6%, compared with 2.3% in the corresponding period last fiscal, the review highlighted, indicating persistence of growth momentum.The overall balance of payments remained in surplus during the April-October period this fiscal, supported by higher net foreign direct investment and net banking capital inflows. Foreign exchange reserves remained strong at $705.3 billion as of 13 November, providing an import cover for 10 months.The labour market remained robust in the first half of FY27, with rising labour force participation and easing unemployment, alongside a modest shift towards regular wage/salaried employment and the secondary sector.

headline: Musi Jan Andolan Boycotts MRDCL’s Consultation After Tenders Already Issued
content: Hyderabad: The Musi Jan Andolan (MJA) has demanded the govt to place all the Detailed Project Report (DPRs) of Musi riverfront development project in public including hydrological studies, and certified boundary maps. The MJA, which boycotted the stakeholder consultation meeting organised by the Musi Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (MRDCL) on Musi project, termed the exercise a deceptive, post-facto farce, The leaders said that the state govt is staging closed-door token consultations only after already issuing tenders for project works and advertising the controversial Musi riverfront project to investors at the upcoming Global Investment Summit.Addressing a press conference at Somajguda press club on Saturday, the MJA activists and affected people including Sajaya K, Sandhya V, Syed Bilal, Vishali, Ruchith Asha Kamal, Sanjeev, Lissy Joseph, Shailendra, Subbalakshmi, Kondal Rao and Sudha Goparaju, alleged that the cabinet sub-committee, chaired by the deputy CM constituted for this purpose has completely abdicated its political responsibility of hearing people’s voices to a mere implementing agency, which is a vested interest party.“The MRDCL issued a sudden invitation to MJA on November 25 for a 90-minute consultation scheduled for November 28. The MJA demanded that before any such meeting, the Detailed Project Report (DPR), comprehensive environmental and social assessments, and river boundary maps be proactively placed in the public domain in English, Telugu, and Urdu. Genuine civic consultation requires stakeholders to have access to full project documentation, adequate time to review impacts on displacement and livelihoods, and an institutional dialogue led by the cabinet sub-committee. It is shocking and conniving that the MRDCL had already issued tenders for Zone-IA and Zone-IB of the riverfront project in October itself,” the leaders said.The final bidding submission deadline for these tenders as it is listed on the Asian Development Bank (ADB) website was set for 5:00 PM on 27th November 2026: the exact same deadline given to civil society to confirm attendance for the consultation, they said.The MJA leaders alleged that calling for stakeholder consultations after closing the tenders for project works completely strips the consultation of any integrity or material consequence. They asserted that presenting an already finalized, tendered commercial design to the stakeholders after decisions have already been sealed is not dialogue; it is an undemocratic attempt to manufacture rubber-stamp legitimacy for an anti-people, anti-river project.The leaders demanded abolition of the corporate Special Purpose Vehicle (MRDCL), which operates without democratic oversight, and establish a statutory, participatory Musi River Basin Authority comprising elected local representatives, riparian community members, independent hydrologists, environmentalists and civil society. The leaders said while the ADB claims project loan Rs 4,5000 crore is in conceptual stage, the MRDCL has already issued tenders and is in the process of finalisation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Care leave provision for parents of kids with disabilities needed: Kiran Bedi
content: Mysuru: Former Puducherry Lieutenant Governor and IPS officer Kiran Bedi urged the government to introduce a dedicated care leave provision for parents of children with disabilities, which enables them to balance professional commitments with the special care and attention their children require.“Just as maternity and paternity leave are provided, the government should consider introducing care leave for parents of children with special abilities,” she said. She was speaking after inaugurating the two-day 32nd National Parents’ Meet, organised by PARIVAAR, the National Confederation of Parent Organisations, in association with Maulana Azad National Urdu University, Hyderabad, and the All India Institute of Speech and Hearing (AIISH), at the AIISH premises in Mysuru on Saturday..India's maternity rights framework needs a paternity leave rethink.The meet is hosted with the theme of ‘From Care to Empowerment: Building Inclusive Communities Through Strong Families and Collective Action’. She said that families must become active participants in shaping policies and securing the rights of persons with disabilities. Suggesting the formation of separate awareness, advocacy and activism groups, she called for mobilising parents, professionals, lawyers and corporate leaders to identify gaps in policy implementation and pursue collective action. Bedi also stressed the need for measurable outcomes from such initiatives, urging families to move beyond discussions and demonstrate concrete progress. She called for greater involvement of fathers in caregiving, observing that the responsibility of raising children with disabilities should not fall entirely on mothers. Advocating a change in societal attitudes, she said persons with disabilities must be treated with dignity and provided opportunities for independence, empowerment and inclusion..Breastfeeding beyond 10 months statistically linked to higher blood pressure in children: Report.Highlighting the need for long-term financial security for children with intellectual and developmental disabilities, Bedi expressed concern over the reported absence of a chairman for a welfare trust established for their benefit. She called upon the trust to immediately address the issue, strengthen the trust’s corpus and ensure that it fulfilled its intended purpose of supporting children beyond their parents’ lifetime.PARIVAAR President Dr Pankaj Maru said that the organisation represented more than 300 parent and non-parent organisations across the country. AIISH Director Dr Pushpavathi highlighted the institute’s contributions for rehabilitation and early intervention for such kids. NIEPID Director BV Ramkumar emphasised the importance of family-centred rehabilitation of such kids.Dr D K Menon and B Elangovan, Deputy Director, Technical Education, JSS, were present.

headline: JD(U) fully supports delimitation, women's reservation-linked Constitution amendment bills: Sanjay Jha
content: New Delhi, The Janata Dal on Saturday extended its full support to the Constitution amendment bills related to delimitation and women's reservation, describing those as an important initiative towards expanding Indian democracy.In a post on X, JD working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said the proposal provides for a 50-per cent increase in the existing strength of the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, besides paving the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in these legislatures."The Janata Dal fully supports this proposal," Jha said, describing it as an "important initiative" towards expanding Indian democracy. "The most important aspect of this proposal is that it provides for a 50 per cent increase in the existing number of seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies," he said.Jha said the proposal will expand the scope of people's representation and ensure women's participation in the decision-making process.He appealed to all political parties to "rise above partisan differences" and support the bills, urging them to play a positive role in ensuring their passage in Parliament with broad consensus.The Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre is set to introduce a fresh Constitution amendment bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday to roll out one-third reservation for women by increasing the seat allocation for each state and Union Territory in the House and the strength of their legislative assemblies by 50 per cent, and freeze the revised allocations and boundaries until 2051.The Constitution Bill, 2026, seeks to raise the House's maximum strength to 850, with up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories.It also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a state Assembly from 500 to 650.The objective of the Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes , in the House of the People and the legislative assemblies of the states and Union territories through a delimitation exercise, its Statement of Objects and Reasons says.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: NITI Aayog to assess 49 national missions for impact, spending efficiency
content: NITI Aayog will undertake a comprehensive assessment of 49 national missions, including those focused on energy security, healthcare, and artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities, to evaluate their relevance and effectiveness, and will recommend changes in implementation, according to an Economic Times report. The exercise will examine whether the missions should continue in their existing form, undergo restructuring, be consolidated, or merged where necessary. It will also seek to identify operational, institutional, financial, and coordination-related bottlenecks affecting their implementation. The missions under review include the National Critical Mission, National Energy Mission, National Health Mission, Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, India Semiconductor Mission, Skill India Mission, National Food Security Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission, among others. A senior government official told the Economic Times that the missions have been divided into five thematic groups to facilitate the assessment. These cover urban development, water, sanitation and environment; agriculture, allied activities and rural development; digital technology, innovation, education and skills; health, biotechnology, AYUSH and culture; and energy, strategic resources, science and emerging industries.NITI Aayog to invite bids for assessmentThe first group, covering urban development, water and sanitation, comprises 10 missions, while the agriculture, allied activities, and rural development category has 13. The third and fourth groups have eight missions each, while the fifth group has 10. NITI Aayog will soon invite bids to conduct the assessment and plans to submit its recommendations to the respective ministries by the end of the current financial year. The proposed exercise aims to enable evidence-based decisions on the future of the missions, optimise public expenditure and eliminate duplication, the official said. It will also examine overlapping mandates and identify opportunities for convergence between programmes, restructuring or mergers to improve administrative efficiency and effectiveness.Focus on implementation bottlenecks and outcomesThe assessment is expected to help the government identify gaps in implementation and introduce corrective measures, including changes to implementation frameworks and measures to address ground-level constraints. The exercise comes amid the government's focus on ensuring that public resources are directed towards initiatives delivering tangible developmental outcomes. According to the report, the Aayog believes a critical assessment of the missions will help establish accountability, facilitate informed policy decisions and ensure that government initiatives remain aligned with India's evolving developmental priorities and the vision of Viksit Bharat.

headline: CM Shivakumar warns of 'Delhi Chalo' stir if Centre continues to withhold drought aid
content: NEW DELHI: Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar on Saturday warned of a 'Delhi Chalo' agitation after the Belagavi winter session if the Centre failed to release drought relief funds to the state before the session concludes. He also announced a meeting with the chief ministers of Kerala and Telangana in Delhi on Sunday to discuss the proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies, alleging that the exercise could disadvantage southern states.Addressing a press conference at the Sangama conference hall in Vidhana Soudha, Shivakumar said Karnataka had not received any drought relief from the Centre so far, news agency IANS reported."We have discussed this issue in the Cabinet and will launch all forms of protest. If the Centre does not release compensation before the conclusion of the Belagavi session, we will launch a Delhi Chalo agitation after the session," he said.Asked whether the state would approach the Supreme Court if the Centre failed to release the funds, Shivakumar said the government would move the court. He added that it had also sought an appointment with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss the matter through an all-party delegation.To meet Kerala, Telangana CMs over delimitationOn his Delhi visit, Shivakumar said he would leave Bengaluru on Saturday night and meet the chief ministers of Kerala and Telangana on Sunday to discuss the Centre's proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies."We will discuss the injustice being done to our state, the likely increase in the number of seats in northern states, and the implications for southern states. We have only the information available through media reports about the decision taken by the Union Cabinet. We will fight to protect our interests," he said.Accusing the BJP of pursuing delimitation to suit its political interests, Shivakumar said southern states could become minorities in terms of parliamentary representation despite their contribution to the country's development."We support women's reservation, but oppose delimitation. The BJP is doing this according to its convenience. We will fight to protect our sovereignty and interests. They cannot suppress our voice," he said.He also questioned why the Centre had not convened an all-party meeting to discuss the proposed exerciseGet the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Himachal HC upholds ST status for Sirmaur’s Hatti community, dismisses pleas
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh high court on Saturday upheld the Scheduled Tribe (ST) status for the Hatti community in the Trans-Giri (Giripar) area of Sirmaur district, dismissing petitions challenging the move.Directing authorities to take consequential steps—including issuing ST certificates to Hatti applicants in accordance with the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950—the court held that courts and tribunals lack jurisdiction to adjudicate inclusions or exclusions in SC or ST lists notified by Presidential Order under Articles 341 or 342 of the Constitution.Quoting the Supreme Court precedent, the bench observed: “…the mandate of the Apex Court is that the Courts or tribunals have no authority, power, or jurisdiction to hold inquiry, to collect evidence, or appreciate evidence for adjudicating the inclusion or exclusion by the Presidential Order in the list of SC or ST under Article 341 or 342 of the Constitution.”It cited State of Orissa vs. Dasarathi Meher ((2018) 18 SCC 176), noting that courts or tribunals have no power to examine the correctness of including or excluding any class, category, or group in the schedules attached to the SC or ST orders of 1950.The high court dismissed petitions challenging the status filed by the Giripar Anusuchit Jaati Adhikari Sanrakshan Samiti, Gujjar Samaj Kalyan Parishad, and Kinnaur Students Welfare Association.Senior advocates Shravan Dogra and Ashok Sharma, representing the Hatti community, said the court made clear it could not stay or amend a law passed by Parliament, which holds sole authority over inclusions in the ST list.Calling the ruling historic, Dogra said the court reaffirmed settled Supreme Court law and found no scope for intervention after Parliament enacted the inclusion. On a potential appeal to the Supreme Court, he said while no party is barred from approaching the top court, established Supreme Court jurisprudence leaves little room for success.Case chronologyThe Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Third Amendment) Bill, 2022, proposing to add “Hatti” to the state’s ST list, was cleared by the Union Cabinet in October 2022, passed by the Lok Sabha in December 2022, and passed by the Rajya Sabha in July 2023.In October 2023, Himachal Pradesh’s tribal development department sought clarification from the Union ministry of tribal affairs on the identity of Hattis and whether Scheduled Caste (SC) members fell under the category. Following a ministry clarification in November 2023, the state government issued a notification on January 1, 2024, granting ST status to Hattis in the Trans-Giri area while excluding those eligible for SC reservation.In January 2024, a division bench of then-Chief Justice MS Ramachandra Rao and Justice Jyotsna Rewal Dua stayed the implementation of the law while hearing pleas by the Giripar Anusuchit Jaati Adhikar Sanrakshan Samiti and the Gujjar Kalyan Parishad. At the time, the bench remarked prima facie that there appeared to be “manifest arbitrariness and glaring unconstitutionality in the impugned law.”Questioning the exclusion of SCs in its January 2024 interim order, the court had said it was baffled by the ministry’s advice without Parliament making an exclusion under Article 341(2) of the Constitution. It had also noted that the Centre had rejected requests for ST status to Hattis in 1995, 2006, and 2017—including in 2017, when it described “Hatti” as a blanket or generic term covering all Trans-Giri residents.Six-decade struggleLeader of the Opposition and former chief minister Jai Ram Thakur welcomed the dismissal of the petitions, saying the Hatti community would finally receive its due after a six-decade struggle. “Whatever I could do in the struggle for the rights of the Hatti community, I did. I am satisfied that I could contribute to this cause,” he said, congratulating the community.Anil Kumar Manget, counsel for the SC petitioners, also welcomed the outcome, saying the Centre informed the court that communities already on the SC list would not be removed. “If the rights of the SC community remain intact as they were, then it is a victory for us as well,” he said. He added that a newly formed SC committee headed by Surender Dharma will decide whether to move the Supreme Court.

headline: Odisha to host National conference on AI in litigation on December 12-13
content: The Odisha government is preparing to host a two-day conference on the use of artificial intelligence in litigation, which is expected to be attended by the chief justice of India and judges from several high courts, officials said on Saturday.The participation of senior judicial officials is expected to make the conference an important platform for discussing technology's growing role in the Indian justice system, reported by PTI.The conference, titled ‘Artificial Intelligence in Litigation - Issues and Challenges’, will be held on December 12 and 13 and is likely to bring together around 300 delegates included senior members of the judiciary, legal experts and other stakeholders to discuss how artificial intelligence can be used in India's justice delivery system, chief secretary Anu Garg said.Garg said the event would serve as an important platform to discuss the growing role of artificial intelligence in the justice delivery system and the challenges associated with its use.She also directed the departments concerned to coordinate closely to ensure the smooth and successful organisation of the conference.The conference is significant because AI is increasingly influencing legal research, case management, documentation, evidence analysis and court administration. At the same time, its use raises questions about accuracy, accountability, data privacy and judicial independence.Why is this conference important for India's judicial system?India's judicial system is increasingly exploring technology to improve access to justice and court administration.Some important areas of technological development include:Digital courts: Technology is being used to manage case records, filings and court proceedings.AI-assisted translation: Language technology can help make judgments accessible to people who do not understand English.Legal research: AI tools can assist legal professionals in searching and analysing large collections of judgments.Virtual hearings: Digital platforms have expanded access to court proceedings beyond physical courtrooms.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 7 killed as vehicle falls into gorge in Lansdowne area of Uttarakhand’s Pauri district
content: At least seven people were killed after a vehicle fell into a gorge in the Lansdowne area of Uttarakhand's Pauri district, news agency PTI reported, citing officials.Further details about the accident are awaited.Also Read | 6 killed after vehicle falls into deep gorge on Banswada-Mohankhal road in Uttarakhand's RudraprayagCM Dhami expresses condolencesFollowing the tragic accident, Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed condolences.In a post on X, he said, "I have received the deeply distressing news of a horrific road accident in Rikhnikhal, Kalwadi, Pauri Garhwal.""I express my deepest condolences to the grieving families of those who lost their lives in this heart-wrenching accident," the CM stated.Dhami also noted that he had directed the district administration to reach the accident site immediately, expedite rescue and relief operations, and ensure proper medical treatment for the injured.He added, "I have also directed that seriously injured individuals be airlifted to advanced medical centres. I pray to God for the speedy recovery of all those injured." (with inputs from PTI)

headline: ED raids 3 private companies in Punjab grain contract scam probe
content: Chandigarh: The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Chandigarh, has intensified its probe into alleged corruption and irregularities in Punjab’s foodgrain procurement, storage and preservation contracts, conducting searches at residential and commercial premises linked to three private companies on November 25 and 26.The searches were carried out by the ED’s Chandigarh zonal office under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, in connection with Origo Commodities India Pvt Ltd, Greymarble Infra Pvt Ltd (GMI) and Shivalik Agro Poly Products Ltd.Locations identified in the searches include GMI’s office at GMI (IT) Tower in Sector 83, Mohali, the residence of the company’s owner in Sector 21, Chandigarh, and Shivalik Agro Poly Products Ltd’s corporate office at B-45, Phase III, Industrial Area, Mohali.The operation is linked to allegations that private companies were extended undue favours in government contracts in return for illegal gratification, causing substantial losses to the Punjab exchequer.The ED also searched the residence of Shiromani Akali Dal’s Kharar constituency in-charge, Ravinder Singh Khera, in Khera village near New Chandigarh. Khera owns Guru Kripa Rice and Agro Industries, and the agency reportedly sought documents relating to its rice-milling operations.Probe into alleged ₹100-cr lossThe investigation stems from a CBI FIR against officials of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) and others over alleged irregularities in foodgrain procurement, storage and quality inspection. The ED is examining the suspected nexus between private companies and senior officials associated with the Punjab State Grains Procurement Corporation (PUNGRAIN) and the state’s department of food and civil supplies.According to earlier reports, discrepancies in contracts awarded for the preservation and security of wheat stocks are suspected to have caused a loss of nearly ₹100 crore to the state exchequer.The probe is also examining the award and subsequent extensions of contracts to Origo Commodities and its associated entities. The company was reportedly awarded work for the preservation and security of 30 lakh metric tonnes of foodgrains at ₹27.50 per metric tonne, compared with ₹18.10 per metric tonne offered to some other firms—a rate gap that allegedly translated into about ₹32 crore in extra annual expenditure.In a statement issued on Saturday, the ED confirmed that searches had been conducted on November 25 and 26 at premises linked to the three companies in connection with the alleged corruption and irregularities.

headline: 'Did not prioritise family planning': Javed Akhtar questions seat distribution under delimitation
content: NEW DELHI: Lyricist and former MP, Javed Akhtar, on Saturday questioned the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, raising concerns over the allocation of Lok Sabha seats and the potential disadvantage to states that prioritised family planning.Speaking to the media at an event, Akhtar said the final plan was yet to be made public and several aspects of the exercise remained unclear.“First, the final plan has not yet been revealed, how it will be executed, whether new constituencies will be created, what criteria will be considered, and how the country will be divided into various constituencies,” he said, as per ANI.He also questioned the proposed allocation of seats, arguing that states which had not prioritised family planning could benefit at the expense of those that had.“Second, I find it somewhat strange that regions that did not prioritise family planning are being granted more seats, while those that followed family planning are being allocated fewer seats… How does this create any balance? We will examine the details once they are released… We will also observe which members of the opposition, beyond our own government, come forward to endorse or reject this…” he said.The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations to facilitate the proposed delimitation exercise and implementation of women's reservation. These include the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and a proposed amendment to laws governing Union Territories. The Bills are scheduled to be taken up during the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.The proposed legislative package provides for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to every state and Union Territory, alongside a corresponding increase in the strength of state legislative assemblies. It proposes raising the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, with up to 815 members representing states and 35 representing Union Territories.The package also seeks to facilitate the implementation of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provides for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.While the Opposition has backed women's reservation, it has objected to linking its implementation with delimitation and demanded that the exercise be based on the latest Census data.The Centre has proposed using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies and determining seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while retaining the 1971 population basis for state-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats until 2051.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Mortgaging self-respect': Raut takes aim at Sharad Pawar's NCP over delimitation bill
content: NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Saturday accused the BJP of engineering a split in the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and the Pawar family, saying any move by the NCP (SP) to support the Centre's proposed delimitation bill would amount to mortgaging its self-respect.Raut said the BJP had divided the NCP and the Pawar family, and alleged that aligning with the saffron party would mean surrendering one's self-respect.Speaking to reporters, the Rajya Sabha MP said the NCP (SP) should reconsider its reported decision to back the legislation, calling it an unfortunate and unilateral move that would not go down well with people in Maharashtra."If you are taking unilateral decisions and backing the government on the bill, then the people of Maharashtra will not tolerate it," he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.Raut questions NCP (SP)'s standQuestioning the party's reported willingness to support the bill, Raut said its eight MPs had won the Lok Sabha election as part of the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), and not with the BJP's support."Your eight MPs won as Maha Vikas Aghadi. BJP did not help them win," he said.He also asked the NCP (SP) to apologise to leaders such as Anil Deshmukh and Nawab Malik, who, he claimed, had faced jail while fighting the BJP.Raut said backing the legislation would be contrary to the ideology of the NCP (SP) and Maharashtra's political legacy. He added that parties should not invoke the ideals of Mahatma Phule, Shahu Maharaj and Dr BR Ambedkar while supporting the bill.Calls delimitation a threat to democracyRaut alleged that the proposed delimitation exercise was intended to weaken democratic institutions and strengthen the BJP ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections."By raising the number of 543 to 806 MPs and then doing delimitation as per your whim...this is snatching people's rights forever. This is a conspiracy of the BJP," he said.He also accused the BJP of not winning all its elections on merit, alleging that it had misled voters in 2014 and resorted to an EVM "scam" and "vote chori and seat chori" in 2024. He claimed the government was now pushing delimitation after the Opposition had exposed these alleged irregularities."This (the delimitation process) is detrimental for the country and its federal system," Raut said, warning that the passage of the bill would leave no room for the Constitution, freedom or democracy.What the proposed bill seeks to doThe Union Cabinet on Friday cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill ahead of the special Parliament sitting beginning November 30.The proposal seeks to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent across all states, taking the House's proposed upper limit to 850 from the existing 543. The increased seats would be redrawn using the 2011 Census, while each state's percentage share of parliamentary representation would remain unchanged, sources said.The government is seeking support from parties including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the NCP (SP) to secure the numbers needed to pass the legislation.The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) could secure 319 votes with the support of 20 Trinamool Congress rebels and the lone Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MP, whose party returned to the NDA on November 24.The tally could increase to 353 if the DMK's 22 MPs, the NCP (SP)'s eight MPs and the YSR Congress Party's four MPs also support the bill.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Modi is not going anywhere': Rajnath hits back at Congress, says only people can remove PM
content: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday hit back at the Congress, declaring that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was “not going anywhere”, asserting that only the people of India could decide when he should leave office.Addressing a rally after leading the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, End Anarchy) foot march, Singh accused the Congress and its allies of attempting to destabilise the country and create an atmosphere of uncertainty in a bid to dislodge Modi from power.Invoking PM Modi's description of himself as a 'faqir', Singh said the prime minister had repeatedly made it clear that he had no personal attachment to power and would leave office whenever the people wanted him to."You must have heard our Prime Minister Modi say on several occasions, 'I am a faqir. When the people say so, I will pick up my bag and leave'," he said.Singh said PM Modi had been entrusted with the responsibility of leading the country by the people and that only they had the authority to take it away."He did not become the Prime Minister because of anyone's inheritance. The people of India gave him this responsibility. And if anyone can take it back, it is only and only the people of India. No one else can do so," he said.Questioning the Congress's attempts to target a prime minister who had secured his position through public support, Singh asked, "Are you trying to remove such a person from power? Are you trying to impose baseless allegations on him?"Issuing a direct challenge to the opposition, Singh said PM Modi would continue in office despite attempts to discredit his leadership."Let the Congress leaders listen carefully. Modi Ji is not going anywhere. I want to convey this message to Congress leaders across the country: Modi Ji is not going anywhere," he said.Taking a further swipe at the Congress, Singh said the party, rather than PM Modi, should prepare to exit the political scene. "The time has come for the Congress to pack up and leave. If anyone has to go, it is the Congress, not Modi," he said, drawing applause from the gathering.The defence minister also contrasted PM Modi's political journey with that of Congress leaders, alleging that political inheritance had shaped the careers of several opposition leaders, while the prime minister had risen through his own journey and public support.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Toyota to study feasibility of Karnataka’s invite to adapt hybrid taxis for Indian market in State
content: Bengaluru Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has invited Toyota Motor Corporation to explore manufacturing in Karnataka a compact hybrid version of a taxi model it had developed around the time of the Tokyo Olympics, with a view to making it affordable for common people. During his three-day visit to Japan from November 23 to 25, Mr. Shivakumar discussed the proposal with Toyota’s leadership, suggesting that the vehicle be adapted for the Indian market with lower pollution, lower maintenance costs and an affordable price. Karnataka Chief Minister to lead delegation to Japan for investment talks, urban-planning study storyline 1 Karnataka CM’s Japan visit: D.K. Shivakumar promises support for Toyota’s vehicle manufacturing expansion plans in State Karnataka CM’s Japan visit: D.K. Shivakumar promises support for Toyota’s vehicle manufacturing expansion plans in State Toyota looks at scaling its vehicle production capacity to one million in the near future; D.K. Shivakumar and M.B. Patil invite company leadership to Global Investors’ Meet in Karnataka in 2027 Karnataka CM’s Japan visit: D.K. Shivakumar promises support for Toyota’s vehicle manufacturing expansion plans in State storyline 1 No competition to autos The Chief Minister said the vehicle should not be positioned as a competitor to autorickshaws, which play an important role in last-mile connectivity and provide livelihoods to drivers. “We must protect the jobs of auto drivers,” he said, pointing out that the proposed model should complement the existing transport system. Toyota had agreed to examine the proposal, including the vehicle’s height and floor height, and undertake research before responding. Mr. Shivakumar said estimates of a possible price ranged from ₹7 lakh to ₹10 lakh, but no price had been finalised. Development beyond Bengaluru The delegation’s visit was aimed at attracting fresh investments, strengthening industrial partnerships and taking development beyond Bengaluru. More than 525 Japanese establishments are already operating in Karnataka, and the State has attracted 101 Japanese greenfield projects since 2016, he said. A major outcome was an agreement with Kawasaki Heavy Industries for an investment of up to ₹800 crore over 10 years to expand its facility at Harohalli, with the potential to create around 600 jobs. The delegation also held discussions with Panasonic Automotive, JFE Engineering, JFE Steel and JSW Steel. Industries Minister M.B. Patil held separate meetings with several Japanese companies, including Sumitomo Corporation, JX Metals, Neturen, Takeda and Mitsubishi Chemical. Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years storyline 1 The Chief Minister said the government had assured companies of support in land, infrastructure, approvals and investment facilitation, and would work to reduce delays in clearances. Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years Expansion of Harohalli plant to create 600 jobs; Chief Minister-led delegation also holds talks with Panasonic Automotive Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years storyline 1 Urban planning and waste management The delegation studied Japanese models of urban development, public transport and waste management in Nagoya, Osaka and Tokyo. Mr. Shivakumar said he had asked officials to examine the possibility of developing commercial spaces around Metro stations, improving pedestrian infrastructure and adopting transit-oriented development. He referred to integrated developments such as Azabudai Hills, Tokyo Midtown and Oasis 21, and said the Urban Development Department would examine their feasibility for Bengaluru, including the possibility of pilot projects. Karnataka Chief Minister-led delegation visits Osaka waste-to-energy plant Karnataka Chief Minister-led delegation visits Osaka waste-to-energy plant The delegation examined the plant’s technology, which processes up to 900 tonnes of municipal solid waste a day and has a power generation capacity of 32 MW. Karnataka Chief Minister-led delegation visits Osaka waste-to-energy plant storyline 1 In Osaka, the delegation visited the Maishima waste-to-energy plant, which processes around 900 tonnes of waste a day and generates 32 MW of power. He also interacted with Karnataka youth undergoing training and working in Japan. The delegation met Japan’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Yasutaka Nakasone, and India’s Ambassador to Japan, Nagma Mohamed Mallick. Mr. Shivakumar invited Japanese companies to participate in the Global Investors Meet, Invest Karnataka 2027, in Bengaluru, from April 20 to 22.

headline: Sonia Gandhi was not an Indian citizen in 1980 but name on voter list: Delhi Police tells court
content: NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police on Saturday told a Delhi court that Sonia Gandhi was not an Indian citizen in 1980, despite her name appearing on the electoral roll that year, news agency ANI reported.The submission came after the Rouse Avenue Court sought an action taken report (ATR) from the Station House Officer (SHO) of IP Estate Police Station on a complaint alleging that the Congress leader's name was included in the voter list nearly three years before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983.The complaint questions how Sonia Gandhi's name could have featured in the electoral roll in 1980, when she was not an Indian citizen. It seeks a police investigation into what it describes as a possible case of forgery.On Saturday, the Delhi Police told the court that Sonia Gandhi acquired Indian citizenship only in 1983. It added that the facts had been verified by the district magistrate and the ministry of home affairs.The court granted the Delhi Police more time to complete its inquiry and scheduled the next hearing for December 14. It also summoned the SHO of Tughlak Road Police Station.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Former High Court judges review arrangements at Thirupparankundram ahead of ‘deepathoon’ lamp lighting
content: MADURAI Two former High Court judges, Justices S. Vaidyanathan and V. Parthiban, appointed by the Supreme Court as receivers, have begun climbing the Thirupparankundram hillock on Saturday (November 28, 2026), where the top court has ordered the lighting of the lamp on the contested ‘deepathoon’. While visiting the Sri Subramaniaswamy Temple, they assessed the prevailing situation on the ground and reviewed administrative arrangements for the hillock. Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit at ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice storyline 1 The former judges said that only 50 identified devotees would be allowed atop the Thirupparankundram hillock, along with security personnel and temple employees, to light the Karthigai Deepam on the ‘deepathoon’ on Saturday evening. #Thiruparankundram | The two former #MadrasHC judges, Justices S. Vaidyanathan & V. Parthiban, who were appointed by #SupremeCourt as receivers to oversee affairs of Thirupparankundram temple, have arrived at the site. They’ll climb atop the deepathoon site shortly. @rajanjourno https://t.co/p71AOjlXVO— The Hindu - Chennai (@THChennai) November 28, 2026 They would be allowed to climb the hillock between 2.30 p.m. and 3 p.m. for the ceremony to be conducted at 5 p.m. No other members of the public or devotees would be allowed to climb the hillock. The former judges appealed to the devotees to respect the Supreme Court order and cooperate with the administration in maintaining law and order. Steep flights of steps made of stone, along with the rocky terrain, have posed challenges to those climbing up. Additionally, some stretches of the pathway do not have any steps at all. Wooden scaffolding has been placed around the tall stone pillar, or the ‘deepathoon’, to help the workers set up the lamp for Karthigai Deepam. headline: Akhtar rues lack of education opportunities for poor; takes 'poison' jibe at gurukuls, madrasas | Education
content: Pune, India is a talented and intelligent country, but opportunities for education are becoming increasingly inaccessible to children from poor families, legendary writer-poet Javed Akhtar said on Saturday.Akhtar also took a swipe at the education imparted in madrasas and gurukuls, claiming children emerging from such institutions would have minds filled with poison.He was speaking after receiving the Mahatma Phule Samata Award 2026 from Maharashtra minister and NCP leader Chhagan Bhujbal at a ceremony organised by the Akhil Bharatiya Mahatma Phule Samata Parishad here to mark the death anniversary of social reformer Mahatma Jyotiba Phule."India is a talented and intelligent country, but opportunities for education are becoming increasingly inaccessible to children from poor families. An ordinary person can achieve a great deal if given an opportunity, but even basic educational opportunities are being denied to many," he said at the event.Education has become expensive, and only a certain class can afford it, he added."If there are no public schools, where will a rickshaw puller's child study? If the child goes to a school with poor education, there won't be good teachers, a proper system or a good curriculum," he said."When a child comes out of a madrasa or a gurukul, his mind will be filled with poison. This is what is happening," Akhtar further claimed.Asserting that education was the government's responsibility under the Constitution, he asked why the government, which claims to provide food to 80-85 crore people, cannot give education to the same number of people."Is education less important than food? The stomach may be full, but the head will remain empty. Why do you want the head to remain empty? Education is as important as two meals a day. If you educate a person, he will not have to ask you for two meals a day," Akhtar emphasised.He also slammed the scenario in which those raising complaints about irregularities in examinations are being branded as anti-national."If you care about the country, let anyone call you anti-national. Consider it another Padma Bhushan," he advised the youth.India might take some time to move forward, but nobody could stop it from progressing, he said, citing the country's history and its significant contributions to astronomy, mathematics, philosophy, languages, scripts and music.He described the Sanskrit script as one of the most logical and scientific writing systems.India fell behind in technology after the Industrial Revolution, he said."This was due to the caste system, which denied education to people engaged in physical labour. This prevented the country from developing basic technologies such as vacuum cleaners, washing machines and tractors, despite its achievements in mathematics and other fields," he claimed.Innovations from blacksmiths, potters and farmers could not emerge as these segments were denied access to education, he said, adding that caste discrimination continued to exist despite the passage of several centuries.The closure of government schools, established to provide education to poor children, was once again pushing education into the hands of privileged sections, Akhtar said.Paying tribute to Mahatma Jyotiba Phule and Savitribai Phule for their contribution to education and social reform, Akhtar told the gathering that he did not consider himself worthy of the Mahatma Phule Samata Award."Their work was extraordinary. Educating people from disadvantaged sections of society was considered against religious practices at the time. The place associated with the Phules is a great temple where people should bow their heads and learn from their work," he said.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.
