headline: Delimitation is about gerrymandering, nothing to do with women’s reservation: Arundhati Roy
content: New Delhi Ahead of the special Parliament session, called from November 30, 2026 where the Centre is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill, author Arundhati Roy said delimitation will do to democracy what demonetisation did to the economy. Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051 storyline 1 Editorial | Fair play: on a hurried delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/fair-play-on-a-hurried-delimitation-of-lok-sabha-constituencies/article71751034.ece Ms. Roy was speaking at the National Conclave of Writers & Artists at Jawahar Bhawan in New Delhi on November 28, 2026. Below is the full text of the speech delivered by Ms. Roy: There is so much else that I wanted to speak about other than what I am going to say today. That is how the world works these days, every crisis is replaced by another more urgent one. This meeting was planned before we learned of the govt’s latest ambush. I wanted to speak about Artificial Intelligence and its impact on the world of literature and publishing. But now, suddenly we are informed that a parliament session has been called. Reports suggest that the Modi government may have managed to bully and buy itself enough MPs to pass its ‘Delimitation Bill’ under the pretence of creating more constituencies to implement women’s reservation in parliament. Constitution Amendment Bill: April to November what changed Constitution Amendment Bill: April to November what changed The revised Constitution amendment Bill closes legal loopholes, extends the population freeze to 2051 and narrows Parliament’s discretion on delimitation Constitution Amendment Bill: April to November what changed storyline 1 This is a government that loves to ambush its citizens. In 2016 PM Modi appeared on TV and announced demonetisation. With no warning, more than 80 percent of Indian currency became non-legal tender. In 2019 his government locked down all of Kashmir and cut the internet in the valley for months together. In 2020 the Prime Minister ambushed us with the COVID lockdown, shutting down a country of more than a billion people with less than four hours’ notice, leaving tens of million with no option but to walk thousands of miles home to their villages. And now this, the latest ambush. If it passes in parliament, Delimitation will do to democracy what demonetisation did to the economy. Demonetisation broke the back of India’s poor and made millions dependent on government charity. Together with electoral bonds it made the BJP the richest political party in the world. The BJP has used its money and influence to undermine the Constitution and capture every single institution that is meant to oversee checks and balances in a functional democracy. This includes, as we now know, the Election Commission. The Special Intensive Review (SIR) of electoral rolls has struck 130 million voters off the electoral lists. That is almost one-tenth of the population, a scale of disenfranchisement that is unprecedented in history. The people who have been struck off are now no longer eligible for the meagre government benefits that have helped them survive. Centre’s delimitation fix steadies Yogi Adityanath’s nerves ahead of polls Centre’s delimitation fix steadies Yogi Adityanath’s nerves ahead of polls By raising the constitutional ceiling on State assemblies from 500 to 650 seats, the Union Cabinet’s revised delimitation bill allows U.P. assembly to expand to 605 members without dividing the State Centre’s delimitation fix steadies Yogi Adityanath’s nerves ahead of polls storyline 1 The SIR curates electoral rolls to benefit the ruling party. An exercise in which a government elects its people instead of the other way around. Delimitation seeks to curate political constituencies towards the same end. If the bill passes it will break the back of India’s democracy. Do not let them fool you into believing that it is just about increasing the number of constituencies and the number of parliamentarians. Do not believe that the Women’s Bill had anything to do with women’s rights. It’s about gerrymandering, plain and simple. This bill is about maps, not numbers. It has to do with redrawing the map of constituencies to geographically consolidate the divisions of caste, religion, and community—to institutionalise divisiveness in a way that benefits a rotten ideology and attempts to entrench it in our society forever. If you have any doubts about their intentions, please study the way redrawn constituencies have served the BJP in Assam and Kashmir. https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/gerrymandering-meaning-explained-parliament-delimitation-politics-definition-usage-america-political-definition/article70872921.ece The Nazis—Germany’s fascists—called themselves National Socialists. By doing this they tried to murder the very meaning of socialism. What shall we call what is going on in India today— Democratic Fascism? In which the very meaning of democracy is being gutted? And the machinery of democracy is being re-purposed towards that end. Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026 Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026 Why the Delimitation Bill failed in Parliament in April 2026 and how the political arithmetic changed since then; here’s what to know Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026 storyline 1 It took many of our writers, artists, intellectuals and commentators a very long time—decades in fact—to understand what has been happening in our country and call it by its name. Fascism. Perhaps this is because it’s easy for a society that practises caste and considers some humans ‘purer’ and more ‘godly’ than others to shuffle sideways into fascism. Despite the mass slaughter, daylight lynching and routine killing of Muslims, despite church burnings and attacks on Christian missionaries in the wake of the 2014 general election, many respected and self-styled ‘liberal’ intellectuals and artists, actually welcomed and applauded Modi when he was sworn in as Prime Minister. They mocked those of us who had raised the alarm years ago because we could see what was coming. Even today, many artists who think of themselves as liberal and secular continue to normalise fascism by participating in government-sponsored festivals and shows at home and abroad. It is shameful. It will not be forgotten. Or forgiven. Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation The distribution of seats based on 1971 Census continued for 50 years for the reason that a readjustment would adversely affect the proportion of States that stabilised population. Population stability was a stated objective of the government. That link between population stability and Lok Sabha share has been removed in the 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill NEWS ANALYSIS Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation storyline 1 Today we live in one of the most unequal societies in the world. A society in which the Rule of Law is implemented according to caste, class, religion, and ethnicity. A society in which dissent is crushed in a million ways. Our country, once a friend of Palestine now unforgivably calls Israel a friend even though it continues to commit genocide in Gaza on a daily basis. Our government buys weapons and illegal surveillance software like Pegasus and Cellebrite from Israel—that is being used on protestors and activists here at home. The Delimitation Bill is a way of consolidating all of this. It’s a long-term plan for Forever Democratic Fascism. As someone who grew up in South India, I am heart-broken to see a party like the DMK, rooted in anti-Hindutva, and anti-caste political ideology, even consider supporting this Bill. I really want to believe they will step back from the brink. Its decision will affect all of India. It shoulders a huge responsibility. Every Member of Parliament that votes for the Delimitation Bill is betraying the promise of India’s Democracy. I’m just a writer. An ordinary citizen. I represent no one but myself. I have no claims to power or sainthood. But here’s this ordinary citizen’s curse upon every MP that conveniently goes missing and every hand that goes up in Parliament next week to support that Delimitation Bill.

headline: Groww's AI assistant can now place trades in more than 20 Indian languages
content: Groww has expanded its in-house artificial intelligence (AI) investing assistant GR-1 to help users research stocks, understand company results and move from investment insights to buy or sell orders, subject to their explicit approval, in more than 20 Indian languages. GR-1 was the highlight of Groww Next 2026, the investment platform's flagship technology event held in Bengaluru on Saturday, where it showcased a new range of AI-led products and investment features. Other launches included family accounts, daily and weekly systematic investment plans (SIPs) starting at ₹100, minor accounts and an option allowing investors to sell bonds before maturity. The company is positioning these offerings around the need to make investment research and financial guidance more accessible as India's retail investor base expands.AI and the investment advice gapIndia has around 1,000 Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)-registered investment advisers, according to the regulator's chairman. It also has roughly one mutual fund distributor for every 4,000 Indians, according to an AMFI and Crisil study. Groww believes AI could help bridge this gap by combining technology-led research with human oversight. “AI brings the speed, our people bring the scrutiny, and the customer always makes the decision,” said Neeraj Singh, co-founder and chief technology officer of Groww. GR-1 understands the screen a user is viewing, allowing it to provide contextual information without requiring the investor to repeatedly enter details. The assistant operates on Groww's internal systems, which the company says allows tighter control over security and customer data. Since the introduction of multilingual chat, around 15 per cent of daily queries have come in regional languages, the company said. Its speak-to-chat feature, being rolled out in phases, already accounts for nearly 20 per cent of daily queries, with a significant share coming from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.MF Prime adds research-backed portfolio guidanceGroww is also expanding MF Prime, its opt-in mutual fund offering launched six months ago. The service helps investors assess which mutual funds to buy, hold, rebalance or exit, addressing three common questions: where to invest, how a portfolio is performing and when to exit. The platform combines AI-led analysis with checks by Groww's in-house research team before recommendations reach investors.AI accelerates product developmentThe company said AI has also changed the pace at which it develops and launches products. Around 70-80 per cent of the code behind its recently launched US stocks offering was written using AI, according to Groww. Among the new features showcased at the event were minor accounts that parents or legal guardians can open and manage entirely online, and fully digital Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) accounts for families investing together. The platform has also introduced daily and weekly SIP options starting at ₹100, aimed at gig workers, shopkeepers, freelancers and other investors who prefer smaller, more frequent investments rather than a single monthly instalment. For active traders, its AI Insights feature identifies chart patterns as they emerge. Groww has also begun rolling out a facility allowing customers to sell their bond holdings before maturity at prevailing market prices, expanding access to secondary-market liquidity.From IPO investments to US stocksInitial public offerings (IPOs) remain an important entry point for first-time investors on the platform. Groww customers accounted for nearly 30 per cent of all IPO allocations in India in 2026 as of October, according to the company. During the Jio Platforms IPO, around 36 lakh customers applied through Groww. For more than 2.5 lakh of them, it was their first investment in the financial markets, the company said. Groww has also made US stocks available on its platform, allowing customers to access more than 10,000 US-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs). During the November correction in Nvidia, orders for the stock on Groww increased more than 15 times from the beginning of the month, the company said. Ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq listing on November 19, Groww introduced a pre-order facility for the stock. More than one lakh users showed interest on the product page within hours, according to the company. Encouraged by the response, Groww plans to extend pre-order facilities to other prominent international listings. “Our customers have grown up with us. The young professional who started a SIP with us years ago is now investing for a child, a family and the future,” said Lalit Keshre, co-founder and chief executive officer of Groww. “Honestly, we feel we haven't covered even 1 per cent of our journey,” he added.

headline: Tirumala temple to release Vaikunta Dwara Darshan tickets from November 28; TTD cancels VIP Break Darshan
content: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) is preparing to release tickets for the much-awaited Vaikunta Dwara Darshan at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala. The special darshan facility will be available to devotees for 10 days, from December 20 to 29. TTD officials have finalised the online booking schedule for different categories of darshan tickets and tokens to help devotees plan their pilgrimage, according to Times of India (TOI) report. Vaikunta Dwara Darshan 2026: Ticket booking schedule According to the schedule announced by TTD, Srivani Darshan tickets will be released first, followed by tickets for special entry darshan. The booking schedule is as follows: - Srivani Darshan tickets: November 28 at 10 am - ₹300 Special Entry Darshan tickets: November 30 at 10 am - Online registration for Slotted Sarva Darshan (SSD) tokens through the electronic dip (e-Dip) system: December 1, from 10 am, to December 5, until 5 pm - e-Dip allocation of SSD tokens: December 7 at 3 pm - Darshan quota for donors: December 8 at 10 am The e-Dip system will be used to allot SSD tokens for the first two days of the festival, December 20 and 21, which coincide with Vaikunta Ekadasi and Vaikunta Dwadasi.TTD cancels VIP Break Darshan, ₹300 tickets on December 20 and 21In view of the expected heavy rush during the festival, TTD has decided to cancel VIP Break Darshan, except for protocol dignitaries, and ₹300 Special Entry Darshan tickets on December 20 and 21, TOI reported.During these two days, devotees will be allowed to have darshan only through the online e-Dip Slotted Sarva Darshan tokens.The decision has been taken to ensure that a larger number of ordinary devotees can participate in the special darshan during the peak festival period.TTD has advised devotees to book tickets and register for tokens only through its official website: (https://ttdevasthanams.ap.gov.in).Tirumala temple adorns Lord Balaji with jewellery donated by Chennai couple A day after a Chennai-based couple donated gold ornaments to Lord Venkateswara, arrangements were made to adorn Lord Balaji with the newly donated jewellery at the Tirumala temple on Friday. Chennai-based donors Vardhaman Jain and Radhika Jain presented 46 different gold ornaments to the temple on Thursday. The jewellery, weighing a total of 121 kg and valued at approximately ₹208 crore, was donated to Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams. The temple authorities made arrangements to adorn the deity with the newly donated ornaments on Friday. According to TTD sources, this would be the largest offering ever made by an individual devotee to Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala.

headline: Govt plans road safety councils at local body level: Minister John
content: Thrissur , The Keralam government is planning to set up road safety councils in local bodies and promote road clubs at the grassroots level as part of efforts to reduce accidents in the state, Transport Minister C P John said on Saturday.Speaking to reporters, John said the government was not approaching road safety merely as a matter of identifying offenders and punishing them, but was seeking to raise awareness while ensuring strict enforcement of rules.Under the Jeeva-Suyathra Mission, the government was pursuing a two-pronged approach of "enlighten and enforce" - educating people about road safety and taking strict action against those who violate traffic rules, he said.The Kerala Road Safety Act and the Road Safety Authority were already in place, with the minister serving as its chairman.However, the authority had not been sufficiently active earlier and had now been revived, he said.District Road Safety Councils were also functioning, but the government wanted to make them more active and was considering setting up similar councils at the level of block panchayats, municipalities and corporations.The government also wanted to establish road safety clubs across the state, preferably at every junction, as part of the mission, he said.With the support of the Union government and IIT Madras, accident-prone locations were now being identified and monitored using a grid system that divides the country into one-km-by-one-km squares, he said.The data would be used to create awareness among people, particularly children. Around six to seven lakh volunteers from organisations such as the National Cadet Corps, police cadets, Scouts and Guides, the National Service Scheme, and the Red Cross were available to support the initiative, he said.The district-level launch of the Road Safety Mission would be held shortly, and the government expected to take the campaign to every nook and corner of the state within six months, he said.John said speed limits would continue to vary depending on the type of road and there was no need for a blanket revision of the limits fixed by the previous government."It is not right to restrict vehicles to 70 kmph on a six-lane highway. The speed limit for highways was fixed during the previous term and I do not think there is any major problem with it. However, speed limits on smaller roads, including district roads that are around eight metres wide, should remain low and must not be increased," he said.On reports of cyber fraudsters using fake traffic challans to siphon money from the public, John said he had taken note of the issue and informed the police to initiate legal action.The incidents were not widespread, he said, adding that one or two cases had initially been reported but no such incidents had occurred subsequently.On Kerala State Road Transport Corporation operations during the Sabarimala pilgrimage season, the minister said 461 buses were currently operating exclusively for pilgrims, and services were running satisfactorily and exceeding expectations.He said 110 old and damaged buses had been refurbished and converted into buses fit for service.The initiative to provide buses to KSRTC was gaining support, with MLAs having contributed 110 buses and the mayor expected to provide one more. Individuals and organisations in several districts had also come forward to donate buses, he said.A cooperative society in Kozhikode, the City Cooperative Society, was the first to contribute a bus, he said, describing the initiative as a new beginning for KSRTC.The corporation had also received a major boost in public support following the launch of the Priyadarshini initiative, he said, adding that people had begun showing greater affection towards KSRTC.On the delay in appointing chairpersons and office-bearers to boards and corporations, John said he had himself experienced a long wait before taking charge as a board and corporation chairman in the past."I took charge as a board and corporation chairman for the first time only after nearly two years," he said.He said it was the right time to make the appointments and expressed hope that the process would be completed soon, as discussions were underway within the UDF.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: INDIA bloc decides to oppose Delimitation Bill, says it is against SCs/STs, will end democracy
content: New Delhi INDIA bloc leaders on Saturday (November 28, 2026) decided to jointly oppose the Constitution Amendment Bill on delimitation-linked women quota in Parliament, terming the move a bid by the BJP-RSS to permanently remain in power and end democracy in the country. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/union-cabinet-clears-delimitation-bill/article71750210.ece Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026 storyline 1 https://www.thehindu.com/visual-story/ Also Read: Delimitation Bill LIVE https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/delimitation-bill-special-parliament-session-india-bloc-meeting-opposition-bjp-live-updates-november-28-2026/article71753535.ece Addressing reporters after the two-hour meeting with floor leaders of Opposition parties, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge claimed that the Delimitation Bill is against the interests of Scheduled Castes (SC) and the Scheduled Tribes (ST) as they will not get increased seats according to their increased numbers and the bill threatens to "finish democracy". INDIA bloc leaders meet at Kharge’s residence to discuss joint strategy ahead of Parliament’s special sitting INDIA bloc leaders meet at Kharge’s residence to discuss joint strategy ahead of Parliament’s special sitting Kapil Sibal alleged that the government’s delimitation Bill is aimed at keeping the BJP in power for 30-40 years, as the Centre is set to introduce a fresh constitutional amendment Bill on Monday (November 30, 2026) INDIA bloc leaders meet at Kharge’s residence to discuss joint strategy ahead of Parliament’s special sitting storyline 1 He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had earlier given the slogan '400-paar' during the last general elections, but by getting this bill passed, he intends to achieve the '800-paar' figure to permanently remain in power and alter the Constitution. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/modi-virtually-addressed-the-viksit-bharat-viksit-madhya-pradesh-programme/article67900724.ece "Once the power goes into their hands, they will do anything to use this bill as a weapon to remain in power permanently. We will oppose this bill," Mr. Kharge told reporters. Also Read: Delimitation redraw brings DMK and BJP together, deepens rift with Congress https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/delimitation-redraw-brings-dmk-and-bjp-together-deepens-rift-with-congress/article71752138.ece The Congress chief claimed that India will become like China, where they raise hands in thousands to get a majority. "They want to end democracy and give the government in the hands of the BJP/RSS forever. Manusmriti will be implemented, this is certain," he claimed. Mr. Kharge also said that earlier too, the BJP planned to get this bill through, but failed due to the opposition's joint efforts. "They are indulging in this 'natak'. We decided to together oppose this bill, as it is not in favour of SC/ST and they intend to finish democracy in the country," he asserted. INDIA bloc to chalk out Parliament strategy as Opposition rallies against delimitation Bills INDIA bloc to chalk out Parliament strategy as Opposition rallies against delimitation Bills Floor leaders to discuss a joint response ahead of special session; parties warn the move could distort representation, weaken federalism and politically benefit the BJP INDIA bloc to chalk out Parliament strategy as Opposition rallies against delimitation Bills storyline 1 The Delimitation Bill was discussed at the meeting of floor leaders of the Opposition, with the clear demands that the current strength of the Lok Sabha should be maintained, women's reservation should be provided based on the current strength of the Lok Sabha and the current allocation of seats among States in the Lok Sabha should be maintained for the next 25 years. The Opposition leaders met at the Leader of the Opposition's residence here and deliberated on a joint strategy in view of the government's imminent move to reintroduce a Constitutional Amendment Bill in Parliament, involving delimitation. Also Read: Union Cabinet clears Delimitation Bill https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/union-cabinet-clears-delimitation-bill/article71750210.ece Besides Congress president Kharge, former party chief Rahul Gandhi, TMC's Abhishek Banerjee, Independent Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, RJD's Abhay Kumar Singh and Manoj Jha, CPI's P Sandosh Kumar, IUML's ET Mohammed Basheer, RSP's NK Premchandran, among others, participated in the meeting. Congress general secretaries Jairam Ramesh, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K.C. Venugopal, among others, also attended the meeting. While non-INDIA bloc parties such as the DMK, AAP and BJD were also invited for the meeting, they chose to stay away. DMK to support Delimitation Bill as there is no loss for Tamil Nadu: A. Raja DMK to support Delimitation Bill as there is no loss for Tamil Nadu: A. Raja Asked why the DMK, which had consistently opposed the BJP, had decided to support the Bill, Mr. Raja said there was nothing wrong with supporting a measure if its provisions were consistent with the party’s position DMK to support Delimitation Bill as there is no loss for Tamil Nadu: A. Raja storyline 1 "Look, we need to examine this from the perspective of what is going to happen at the national level and what lies ahead. At the national level, if this Bill is passed, the number of Lok Sabha seats could increase to around 850. The first question is whether a House of 850 members can function properly," Mr. Sibal said ahead of the meeting. "But the most serious issue is that their objective is not merely women's reservation. We are ready for women's reservation. They can implement it immediately within the existing 543 seats. So that is not their real objective. Their real objective is to remain in power for the next 30-40 years. And for that, what matters most to them is the Delimitation Bill," he said. "They will make appointments to the delimitation body in the same way they appointed Gyanesh Kumar to the Election Commission. In other words, another Gyanesh Kumar will be placed in this position. They will decide the boundaries of constituencies in states such as Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Maharashtra according to their own preferences," he said. A special sitting of Parliament has been convened from November 30. The Lok Sabha has been reconvened on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2. The sittings will conclude on December 3, subject to exigencies of government business. The Centre is set to introduce a fresh constitutional amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday (November 30) to roll out one-third reservation for women by increasing each State and Union territory's seat allocation in the House and the strength of their legislative assemblies by 50%, and freeze the revised allocations and boundaries until 2051. The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, slated for introduction in the Lok Sabha on Monday (November 30), seeks to raise the House's maximum strength to 850, with up to 815 members from States and 35 from Union Territories. It also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a State Assembly from 500 to 650. The objective of the present Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States and the Union territories, through a delimitation exercise, the Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons says. It says the exercise shall provide for an increase of 50% in the number of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union Territories, over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation. On April 17, the earlier Constitutional Amendment Bill fell 54 votes short of the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha, with 298 MPs voting in favour and 230 against. The government did not proceed with the accompanying bills. Delimitation Bill a bid to reduce political representation of south Indian States: Chennithala Delimitation Bill a bid to reduce political representation of south Indian States: Chennithala Delimitation Bill a bid to reduce political representation of south Indian States: Chennithala storyline 1 The Opposition has undergone a churn since then. Twenty Trinamool Congress MPs broke away in June and announced their merger with the NDA-supporting Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI). Disqualification proceedings against them are pending before Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. The NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), which has eight MPs and opposed the April Bill, said on Friday (November 27) that it would back the fresh proposal if it provided for a uniform 50% increase. The DMK, with 22 MPs, has also backed the bill. The BJP is confident of securing the required two-thirds majority, banking on the Trinamool rebels and support from some other parties that opposed the Bill in April. The Lok Sabha has 540 sitting members and three vacancies. If Trinamool MP Kalyan Banerjee's suspension remains in force, 539 members, including the Speaker, can attend the proceedings. The Bill would need 359 votes if all 538 members other than the Speaker vote. Absent members would lower the two-thirds threshold.

headline: Growth to remain resilient in Q3FY27, inflation faces upside risks: FinMin
content: While India's economic activity remains resilient, with momentum expected to sustain in the December quarter, weather-related uncertainties and demand during the wedding season could add to inflationary pressures in the near term, the finance ministry said on Saturday. The retail inflation print for November is also expected to reflect the impact of an unfavourable base, the Monthly Economic Review (MER) for November mentioned. India’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) - which is used to measure retail inflation - for November last year was 104.01 as per the 2024 base year, but only 0.71 per cent as per the 2012 base year. “Inflation may face near-term upside pressures from the persistence of (unfavorable) base effect and weather-related uncertainties, including the possibility of a strong El Nino,” the ministry said in its MER. “With the festive season persisting into November and the onset of the wedding/nuptial season, upcoming inflation prints may face upside risks due to increased demand across food and non-food items,” it added. The cautionary report comes after India's retail inflation in October rose to a two-year high of 6.09 per cent, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI's) tolerance band of 2-6 per cent. However, a moderation in global crude oil prices, with benchmarks falling below $100 per barrel in early November, and a strengthening rupee following robust capital inflows could provide some relief from imported inflationary pressures, provided these trends persist, the review said. Potential supply-side shocks arising from the West Asia conflict are likely to remain a key risk to wholesale and retail prices in India. Continued hostilities and risks to the Strait of Hormuz could also keep oil import bills and maritime freight rates volatile, the ministry said. On the growth front, the ministry expects domestic economic activity to sustain its momentum in the December quarter, with high-frequency indicators pointing to continued expansion across goods movement, tax collections, energy consumption, and freight. "Business activity is likely to remain firm, with new orders gaining pace and input cost pressures easing. Domestic demand should stay supportive, with sequential momentum in vehicle sales and continued strength in rural consumption," the review said. Comfortable fertiliser availability bodes well for the rabi season, although sowing is at an early stage and reservoir storage remains below last year's level, it added. India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 7.8 per cent in the June quarter, while the October edition of the MER estimated growth at 7.35 per cent in the September quarter. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) will release GDP estimates for the September quarter on November 30, 2026. The external sector is also expected to remain resilient, supported by robust merchandise exports, a strong services trade surplus and adequate foreign exchange reserves, the ministry said. "Nevertheless, the evolving geopolitical situation, alongside uncertainty surrounding global trade policies, could weigh on the outlook," it said, adding that resilient domestic fundamentals and adequate macroeconomic buffers would help the economy navigate emerging challenges.

headline: Deepam lighting at Deepathoon  at 5pm, 50 people allowed atop Thiruparankundram hill
content: THIRUPARANKUNDRAM: The traditional Karthigai Deepam will be lit atop the stone pillar (Deepathoon) on Thiruparankundram hill at 5pm on Saturday, former Meghalaya High Court chief justice S Vaidyanathan said, following the Supreme Court's directive.Justice Vaidyanathan, who arrived in Madurai from Chennai along with former Madras High Court judge V Parthiban, confirmed the timing after consultations with officials and temple priests.In a brief statement, he said, "deepam will be lit at 5 pm."The former judges later asked district officials to ensure the presence of the District Collector during the ceremony. Collector Nishant Krishna subsequently joined them, with the group expected to reach the Deepathoon atop the hill on foot by 4pm.Justice Vaidyanathan and Justice Parthiban performed pooja and rituals at the Thiruparankundram temple before handing over the cauldron to the priests for installation atop the stone pillar.The Deepathoon is being accessed with the help of scaffolding erected on the hill.Devotees and local residents gathered in large numbers at the foothills to witness the lighting ceremony.CRPF personnel have taken control of the hill, while authorities have restricted the number of people allowed to witness the ceremony from atop the hill to 50.Announcements were made over the public address system informing devotees of the restriction. Local officials said arrangements were complete, including the deployment of medical teams and ambulances to handle any emergency.The developments came a day after the Supreme Court issued a contempt notice to the Tamil Nadu government for what it termed a "willful and brazen" violation of its earlier directive on the Karthigai Deepam issue.The court had ordered that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill on Saturday.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Delhi HC bars Old Monk makers from bottling 'iQ' gin in similar packaging
content: The Delhi High Court has restrained Old Monk makers from bottling its 'iQ' gin in a get-up which is deceptively similar to that of 'Greater Than' gin.The high court clarified that Mohan Meakin Limited, which manufactures Old Monk and iQ gin, is not restrained from using the mark 'IQ' or its 'iQ' device for gin or for any other goods and added that the company was at liberty to sell its gin in a different get-up.Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav said plaintiff Nao Spirits And Beverages Private Limited, which manufactures and sells 'Greater Than' gin, has no monopoly over the colours black and white, and the defendant (Mohan Meakin) is free to use them in a manner which does not result in a get-up deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff."The new get-up must differ not merely in the shape of the bottle, but also in its dress, that is, the size and placement of the label, the colour arrangement, the placement of the device, and the typography and arrangement of the words on the label, so that the overall get-up, seen as a whole, is not deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff," the high court said while passing an interim order on November 26.According to the plaintiff, Greater Than is its flagship product, and it is a London Dry Gin introduced in India in 2016 and one of the first homegrown craft gins in the Indian market.The plaintiff's counsel said it is a case of passing off of the overall get-up of the plaintiff's gin, that is, the shape of its bottle together with its trade dress.He contended that the defendant has copied the bottle along with the black-and-white scheme, the black cap, the placement of a large black angular device at the top centre of the label and the arrangement of 'LONDON DRY' in small letters over 'GIN' in large letters.The defendant, which has been in the liquor trade for over 160 years, sells brands including Old Monk, Big Ben London gin and Jamun gin.It submitted that it has been using the mark 'IQ' for beer since 1996 and launched gin under the impugned 'iQ' label in August 2023.Its counsel submitted that there is no similarity between 'Greater Than' and 'iQ', and the plaintiff has no registration for its label or its bottle.The counsel submitted that the bottle is an ordinary, generic and functional bottle and identical bottles are sold across the world and offered as stock designs by glass makers. In India, Haku vodka and Indri whisky use similar bottles, he added.The court, however, said it was prima facie satisfied that the use of the impugned get-up by the defendant was likely to cause confusion and deception, including confusion as to affiliation, sponsorship or connection, among ordinary consumers as well as among the plaintiff's loyal consumers and the trade.It said the plaintiff has made out a strong prima facie case of passing off in respect of the overall get-up of the defendant's iQ gin."The balance of convenience is also in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff has used its get-up since 2016 and has built its goodwill on it."The defendant entered the market with the impugned get-up only in August 2023. The defendant is an established company with several brands and a large turnover."The order proposed does not stop it from selling gin, or from using the mark 'IQ'; it only requires the defendant to sell its gin in a get-up of its own," the court said.It further said that the inconvenience to the defendant of changing the dress of one product is far less than the harm to the plaintiff if the impugned get-up continues in the market during the pendency of the suit.Public interest also lies in ensuring that consumers are not misled about the source of what they buy, the high court said.It directed that till the disposal of the suit, the defendant is restrained from manufacturing, bottling, selling, offering for sale, distributing, displaying or otherwise dealing in gin in the existing get-up.Considering that the products are liquor, sold through licensed channels under state excise regimes, the court said the defendant should file an affidavit within two weeks disclosing its stock of iQ gin in the existing get-up, at its premises, with its distributors or in transit.The court asked the defendant not to manufacture or bottle any fresh stock of gin in this get-up and not to place any fresh order for these bottles.It granted one month's time to the defendant to exhaust the existing stock after which the company should ensure that the product is removed from the shelves of the retail/wholesale outlets supplied by it or through its distributors.The defendant should be free to re-bottle and re-label such stock in a get-up that complies with the directions, the court said.

headline: Deepam row: Special team led by retired judges to light lamp at Deepathoon at 5pm
content: A special team led by retired high court judges S Vaidyanathan and V Parthiban has been constituted to light the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon (stone pillar) atop Tirupparankundram hill on Saturday evening.The decision was driven by several factors, including security concerns for the special team of judges and senior officials, as well as the difficult terrain along the route from the foot of the hill to Deepathoon.The special team comprises the two retired high court judges, district collector Nishant Krishna, Madurai City Police commissioner S Rajendran, CRPF IG Thummala Vikram, special monitoring officer Veeraraghav, IAS, sthanika bhattars Saminathan, Ramesh, Ajith and officials from the district revenue department. A team from the Arulmigu Arunachaleswarar Temple, Tiruvannamalai is also expected to join the event later in the day. Catch LIVE updates hereEarlier in the day, a consultation meeting was held under the leadership of Vaidyanathan and Parthiban. Krishna, S Rajendran, officials from the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments department, and sthanika bhattars (heritage priests) attended the meeting.It was decided that members of the special team will be allowed atop the hill while the members of the public are asked to witness the proceedings from the base of the hill.Meanwhile, a commotion developed as some members of Hindu outfits argued with the CRPF personnel demanding they be allowed to climb the hill along with the special team. However, they were pacified by senior CRPF personnel.It may be noted that the Supreme Court, in its ruling, allowed the priests to use the flame from the Uchi Pillayar temple, where the ceremonial lamp was lit at 6pm on November 24 as part of the Karthigai Deepam festival, to light the lamp at Deepathoon on Saturday.The Deepathoon is located about 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah, while the Uchi Pillayar temple is about 250 metres from the pillar.In another development, the entire Tirupparankundram Hill came under the thick blanket of security cover as four more companies of CRPF joined their colleagues to maintain security.

headline: ‘Crime victims must be heard before remission’: SC ruling raises questions over Bilkis Bano convicts’ bail
content: The Supreme Court has ruled that victims of a crime, or their legal representatives, must be given a reasonable opportunity to present their views before the State decides whether to grant premature release or remission to a convict, recognising that the victim’s right to participate in the criminal justice process does not end with the conclusion of the trial and imposition of sentence.In an important victim-centric interpretation of remission laws, a bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that the opportunity to make a representation must be read into the applicable prison rules, at least in cases involving grave offences where the victim or the victim’s family can reasonably be traced and approached. The court clarified that such participation would not give victims a veto over the State’s decision, which must ultimately be taken independently by the competent authority.The ruling, delivered on November 26 in a petition challenging the Bihar government’s decision to prematurely release former MP Anand Mohan, also raises a larger question about the right of victims to be heard when courts themselves consider pleas by convicts for suspension of sentence and bail.The question acquires particular significance in the context of the Bilkis Bano gang rape case, in which the Supreme Court on October 28 suspended the life sentences of two of the 11 convicts, citing their 17 years of incarceration. Bano, who survived gang rape during the 2002 Gujarat riots and lost seven members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, subsequently expressed anguish that the court had not even informed her about the proceedings, much less heard her before granting relief.“How could the honourable Supreme Court simply suspend the sentence of the men who did this to me? How could they not even inform me? How could they not even make sure my voice was heard in their courtroom?” she said in a statement after the order.Remission and judicial relief are legally distinctTo be sure, the judgment in the Anand Mohan case deals specifically with the State’s executive power to grant remission and premature release under the applicable prison rules. The suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the two convicts in the Bilkis Bano case, on the other hand, involved the exercise of the Supreme Court’s judicial power. The two situations are legally distinct, and the latest ruling does not automatically invalidate or govern the bail order in Bano’s case.But the reasoning adopted by the bench offers an important basis for examining the larger question of victim participation in proceedings that could result in a convict’s return to liberty before the full term of the sentence has run its course.The bench noted that neither Section 432 of the Code of Criminal Procedure nor its corresponding provision, Section 473 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), expressly provides for notice to or a hearing of the victim before a remission decision is taken. Yet, it questioned whether remission could continue to be treated as a matter exclusively between the State and the convict when criminal procedure had increasingly recognised victims as important participants in other stages of the justice system, including appellate and bail proceedings.“The victim’s participation in the criminal justice process cannot be regarded as having exhausted itself merely upon the conclusion of the trial and the imposition of sentence,” it noted.Why victims must be heard before premature releaseDrawing on the three-judge bench ruling in Jagjeet Singh Vs Ashish Mishra (2022), which recognised a victim’s participatory rights from investigation through appeal or revision, the court said a decision to prematurely release a convict could have a direct bearing on the victim and the victim’s family, particularly in serious offences whose consequences continued long after the trial.The victim could possess relevant information or have legitimate concerns relating to the continuing impact of the offence, the convict’s conduct, subsequent developments affecting the victim’s safety and the possibility of intimidation, harassment or renewed vulnerability following the convict’s release, it pointed out.The court, therefore, held that an identifiable and traceable victim or the victim’s recognised legal representative must be afforded a reasonable opportunity to submit a representation before the competent authority decides a remission plea. Such a representation must be considered along with other relevant material, without taking away the State’s independent responsibility to decide the matter.“The limited right that we propose to recognise is one of procedural participation: an opportunity to place relevant facts, objections and concerns before the authority, for their consideration along with the other relevant materials,” the bench said.The implications of this reasoning for cases such as Bano’s warrant consideration, particularly because the court’s concern was not confined to the formal process of remission but extended to the impact that a convict’s release could have on the victim’s life, dignity and sense of security.Article 21 protects victims as well as convictsThe judgment’s concluding observations went further in emphasising that the constitutional protection of life and liberty under Article 21 cannot be viewed as a guarantee tilted exclusively in favour of the convict. The court said the victim’s right to live with dignity and freedom from fear deserved equal constitutional recognition.“For the victim and/or his family, such release could revive trauma, breed insecurity and unsettle their fragile attempt to rebuild their lives and move on,” held the bench, adding that their right to live without being haunted by the consequences of such release was as much a part of Article 21 as the convict’s right to secure liberty.“The executive as well as the judiciary, as and when the occasion arises, must strike an appropriate balance that serves the cause of justice in its truest sense – justice to the convict, justice to the victim and justice to society at large,” it said.The court ultimately set aside the Bihar government’s April 2023 notification that removed the disqualification for remission of convicts sentenced for murdering a public servant on duty, as well as the consequential order releasing Anand Mohan. It directed him to surrender within a month and specifically ordered that the victim’s widow be given an opportunity to make a representation if his case for premature release was considered afresh..

headline: Supreme Court clears way for Hockey India elections, restores Odisha’s membership
content: New Delhi Hockey India on Saturday (November 28, 2026) received a shot in the arm, with the Supreme Court clearing the way for its proposed elections on December 5, although it remains to be seen how the entire process is completed within a week. A Bench of Justice K.V. Viswanathan and Justice Arun Palli, while setting aside the Orissa High Court orders staying the elections, also directed the continuation of Hockey Odisha as a permanent member, and recalled the two show-cause notices issued to it for violation of rules and the proposal to reclassify it as an associate member. The decision also allows incumbent president Dilip Tirkey to re-contest for the top post.. Also read | Odisha HC stays Hockey India elections https://www.thehindu.com/sport/hockey/odisha-hc-stays-hockey-india-elections/article71675306.ece Hockey Odisha had challenged the notices and the annual general meetings (AGMs) that issued them as illegal. Saturday’s order not only allows Hockey India to restart the election process, but also clears the way for a fresh set of office-bearers in charge of the federation. Any other grievances from affiliated units will be heard by the one-member Grievance Redressal Committee of retired Justice A.K. Sikri, as proposed by the Delhi High Court earlier. “The Supreme Court directed that the elections of Hockey India shall be conducted as per the election schedule already fixed, observing that the interests of the game must not suffer and that non-conduct of elections could have serious consequences, including possible disaffiliation by the International Hockey Federation,” Hockey India said in a statement. Coach Sjoerd Marijne amazed at the Indian women team’s resurgence Coach Sjoerd Marijne amazed at the Indian women team’s resurgence Coach Sjoerd Marijne amazed at the Indian women team’s resurgence storyline 1 Federation sources, admitting that completing the entire process within a week was extremely difficult, said they would nevertheless try to follow the Supreme Court’s order, although the ball is now in electoral officer Sudhir Tripathi’s court to come out with a fresh timeline. As per the original calendar, the draft electoral roll had been published on October 22, 2026, but the process has stalled since. Tirkey, who is also Hockey Odisha president, expressed satisfaction with the order. “I don’t know how the process will be completed in such a short period and whether I will contest again. But our contention was the unfair and illegal suspension of Hockey Odisha and that has been recalled today, which we are satisfied with. Rest, let’s see,” he said.

headline: ED searches Mohali, Chandigarh premises linked to Dream Meadows colonies in Kurali; seizes 1-kg gold bar, freezes Rs 3.16 cr
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) recently conducted searches at premises linked to a case involving the alleged development and regularisation of two illegal colonies — Dream Meadows-I and Dream Meadows-II — in Kurali, SAS Nagar district.The searches were conducted on November 20 by the ED’s Jalandhar zonal office under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) at premises in Mohali and Chandigarh linked to the accused.The ED said its investigation was based on two FIRs registered by the Vigilance Bureau, Mohali. The FIRs allege that WWICS Estates Pvt Ltd and its director, Davinder Singh Sandhu, in connivance with government officials and private persons, developed and regularised the two colonies.According to the ED, the accused had allegedly incurred excess expenditure of around Rs 35.58 crore, which was 1.73 times their total known legal income.The investigation revealed that WWICS Estates had initially conceptualised Dream Meadows-I and II as a single colony. The agency alleged that the company subsequently projected them as two separate colonies to evade payment of the requisite government fee, causing a loss to the exchequer.The ED further alleged that the colonies were developed on land parcels purchased from various sellers using forged consent letters, which were later used to obtain regularisation certificates from the development authorities.During the searches, the ED seized documents, digital devices and other incriminating records. It also recovered a 1-kg gold bar valued at around Rs 1.23 crore and froze fixed deposits and bank balances worth around Rs 3.16 crore belonging to the accused.The seized material is being examined to ascertain the extent of the alleged proceeds of crime. Further investigation is in progress.

headline: Odisha: Kalahandi hospital fined  ₹25 lakh for charging minor for unauthorised TB test
content: A consumer commission in Odisha’s Kalahandi district has imposed a ₹25 lakh penalty on a private hospital for allegedly collecting money for a tuberculosis test despite not being authorised to conduct it, and ordered it to pay ₹5 lakh compensation to a 10-year-old girl whose family had paid for the test.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Kalahandi, also directed Maa Manikeswari Multispeciality Hospital in Bhawanipatna to refund the ₹1,200 collected for a sputum examination for Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB), pay ₹25,000 towards litigation expenses and deposit ₹25 lakh in the Odisha State Consumer Welfare Fund for engaging in deceptive and unfair trade practices.The commission further directed the state health secretary and Kalahandi chief district medical officer to pay ₹50,000 each to the girl’s father for deficiency in their supervisory duties. The order was issued on Thursday.The case relates to Yashica, 10, who was taken by her father, Ranjan Kumar Patra, to the private hospital on October 24, 2025, for diagnostic tests prescribed by a paediatrician at the district headquarters hospital. The doctor had suspected advanced pneumonia.The prescribed tests included a complete blood count (CBC), MP ICT, C-reactive protein (CRP), sputum AFB and a chest X-ray. Patra paid ₹2,070 for the tests, but the hospital did not provide him with the sputum AFB report.Suspecting irregularities in the tests, Patra filed a Right to Information (RTI) application with the district health authorities, seeking to know whether the hospital was authorised to collect samples or conduct the test.“One of the tests was for TB. Without my knowledge, they collected the sample and charged me ₹1,200 for it. There were also X-ray and blood tests. The X-ray report was not clear and appeared to be just a black-coloured image. The blood test report, too, was handed over to me within just two minutes. This raised doubts in my mind about what kind of tests could be conducted and reports generated within two minutes,” he said.In a reply dated December 19, 2025, the assistant district public health officer (TB), Kalahandi, said only one private hospital in the district — Swasthya Swaraj at Kaniguma in Thuamul Rampur block — was authorised to conduct sputum AFB tests, which were provided free of cost. Maa Manikeswari Multispeciality Hospital was neither a notified TB diagnostic centre nor an authorised sputum collection site under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP), the reply said.The commission observed that despite lacking the required authorisation, the hospital had collected the sputum sample and charged the family ₹1,200. It held that the conduct amounted to a deceptive and unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and could pose a threat to the health and safety of the patient and others.The hospital denied any wrongdoing, claiming that Patra had initially agreed to the arrangement but later refused to allow the sample to be sent for testing. The commission, however, noted that the hospital had collected the money despite not being authorised to conduct the test.It also questioned the credibility of the technician involved, noting that he could not produce a registration number, identity card or appointment letter to establish that he was employed by the hospital at the time.The commission further noted that the hospital’s proprietor had admitted, in a communication to the district health authorities, that the facility had collected sputum samples from other patients for AFB tests in 2025.“Collecting sputum samples for TB testing at an unauthorised facility could expose other patients and attendants to health hazards, as the disease is airborne and requires designated arrangements for sample collection,” the commission noted.Hospital owner Santosh Agarwala said the facility did not conduct several specialised tests on its premises and instead collected samples before sending them elsewhere for testing. He claimed that the technician had told him that a person visited the hospital and purchased a ticket for a swab test.“At around 7 pm, the person called and said that he had admitted his patient to a government hospital and asked us not to send the sample for testing. Our technician told him to come and collect a refund. He agreed but never returned to collect the money,” Agarwala claimed.

headline: Keralam govt sanctions ₹2,029.15 crore as second installment of development funds for local bodies
content: Thiruvananthapuram The Keralam government has sanctioned ₹2,029.15 crore as the second instalment of development funds for local bodies in the State. The funds will enable local bodies to implement development scheme in a time-bound manner, strengthen basic facilities, and improve the effectiveness of service delivery, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan said in a statement on Saturday (November 28, 2026). The Chief Minister added that the government would go ahead with steps to strengthen local administrations as part of decentralisation of power. The government had sanctioned ₹2,029 crore as the first instalment of development funds on August 5. The funds were then sanctioned in the wake of strong criticism from the Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) of starving local bodies of Plan funds. The LDF had organised protests, including in the State capital, alleging that the United Democratic Front (UDF) government had slashed the Plan fund allocation for local bodies, knowing fully well that local bodies could not function without timely release of funds for developmental and welfare schemes, particularly those aimed at vulnerable sections of society. The Opposition had also raised the funds cuts to local bodies as an Adjournment Motion in the Assembly, saying that the local bodies were facing a serious crisis as the Revised Budget has not made allocations for spillover projects for the previous year.

headline: ‘No injustice to Telangana, no reduction in South’s representation’: BRS backs delimitation with conditions
content: BRS working president K T Rama Rao (KTR) on Saturday clarified the party's stance on delimitation, emphasising that the party is willing to support the bill on the conditions that there will be no reduction in South India's parliamentary representation and no injustice against Telangana.This comes a day after the Union cabinet cleared the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, which is scheduled to be tabled in the Lok Sabha during the special sitting on Monday.Track live updates on the delimitation bill here.Speaking about delimitation, in a post on X, KTR said, "No injustice to Telangana will be tolerated." He said BRS has consistently advocated for protecting South India's existing 24 per cent share in the Parliament."Keeping Telangana's interests paramount, our three Rajya Sabha MPs will vote in favour of the proposal. We have always supported women's reservation and remain committed to its implementation," KTR further said. The party has three members in Rajya Sabha but none in Lok Sabha.The leader also noted that the proposed 50 per cent increase in seats, with a safeguard against altering the inter-state representation ratio until 2051, addresses this concern while increasing Telangana's Lok Sabha seats from 17 to 26. Earlier, NCP (Sharad Pawar) and DMK indicated support for the revised delimitation proposals under the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill.Also Read | President recommends Lok Sabha to consider delimitation bill ahead of Parliament sittingDelimitation bill and Parliament sittingA special sitting of Parliament has been convened from November 30. The Lok Sabha has been reconvened on Monday and the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday. The sittings will conclude on December 3, subject to exigencies.Earlier on Saturday, President Droupadi Murmu recommended the Lok Sabha to consider the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026 under Article 117(3) of the Constitution.The bill proposes to add 50 per cent to every state’s and Union territory’s Lok Sabha seats, and to every assembly.Also Read | Unchanged Lok Sabha strength, women’s quota within existing seats among INDIA bloc demands on delimitationINDIA bloc's conditions on delimitationThe INDIA bloc on Saturday put forward three conditions on the proposed delimitation exercise.The bloc listed the following demands: the current strength of the Lok Sabha should be maintained; women's reservation should be provided based on the current strength of the Lok Sabha; and the current allocation of seats among states in the Lok Sabha should be maintained for the next 25 years.(with inputs from agencies)

headline: 18 surrendered Maoists get  ₹75 lakh rehabilitation aid in Andhra Pradesh
content: Amaravati, The Andhra Pradesh Police on Saturday distributed ₹75 lakh as rehabilitation assistance to 18 Maoists who had surrendered before the police as part of efforts to facilitate their return to mainstream society.Director General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta handed over demand drafts totalling ₹75 lakh to the beneficiaries at a programme in Vijayawada."We have extended rehabilitation assistance to 18 Maoists who surrendered before Andhra Pradesh Police, including a member of the outfit's state committee, to help them return to mainstream society," Gupta said while addressing a press conference.The beneficiaries comprise one state committee member Joriga Nagaraju alias Kamalesh, two divisional committee members, 10 area committee members and five party members.Gupta said 134 Maoist cadres, carrying cumulative rewards of over ₹2.8 crore, had surrendered before Andhra Pradesh Police during the last two-and-a-half years. They included one central committee member and two special zonal committee members.Of the total reward amount, ₹91 lakh had already been distributed, while rewards amounting to ₹74 lakh were being disbursed in the latest exercise.The DGP assured the surrendered cadres of continued assistance to help them rebuild their lives.Reviewing the police department's efforts against Left-Wing Extremism, Gupta said 18 Maoist cadres, including three central committee members and three special zonal committee members, had been killed in exchanges of fire during the period. Another 73 cadres, including four special zonal committee members, were arrested.Andhra Pradesh Police also extended operational assistance to their counterparts in Chhattisgarh and Odisha, contributing to operations in which 74 Maoist cadres were neutralised, he said.The state government has also linked rehabilitation efforts with skill development and employment programmes. Under SARAL, which offers training in sewing, coffee-making and other trades, more than 2,000 people secured employment.PRERANA facilitated jobs for 1,200 youth, including placements in Tata Electronics companies and opportunities in bamboo crafts and home nursing.Under SPOORTHY, candidates are provided coaching for recruitment into the Central Armed Police Forces, state police, Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission and other government services. As many as 175 candidates secured jobs through the programme.The state government has also taken up road and communication infrastructure projects in Maoist-affected areas.Under the Road Connectivity Project for Left Wing Extremism Affected Areas, 169 roads covering 1,265.8 km and 39 bridges were constructed in Alluri Sitarama Raju, Polavaram and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.Separately, 287 roads covering 793.7 km have been taken up under the Adavi Thalli Bata initiative to connect 90 remote villages in Alluri Sitarama Raju and Polavaram districts.A total of 2,090 mobile towers have been installed under the telecom infrastructure project, including 1,500 in Alluri Sitarama Raju and Polavaram districts. The initiative has enabled mobile connectivity in 96 per cent of the villages most affected by Left-Wing Extremism.The DGP further said ₹over 1.2 crore in rehabilitation assistance would soon be distributed to 32 other Maoists who had recently surrendered before Andhra Pradesh Police.District administrations and police officials have been instructed to maintain regular contact with surrendered cadres, hear their grievances and address their problems, he said.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 'Shift stance, set aside politics': Kiren Rijiju urges Congress to back Delimitation Bill
content: NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday urged the Congress to set aside political differences and support the Delimitation Bill, saying the concerns raised by various states and communities had been addressed.Appealing to the Congress to reconsider its opposition, Rijiju said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had made a proposal that took into account the interests of every state while seeking to ensure 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies."I believe that following the Prime Minister's appeal, the Congress party must also shift its long-held stance and outdated mindset. I urge the Congress party, as well as those few others who are opposing this bill at the behest of the Congress, to set aside politics and join hands in Parliament to work towards women's empowerment and ensure the passage of this bill," he said.'Congress has never believed in democracy': RijijuRijiju said the proposed legislation would not only provide 33% reservation for women but also increase the number of elected representatives in Parliament and state assemblies.He maintained that the proposal addressed the interests of all states and communities, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and questioned why the Congress was opposing a measure aimed at women's empowerment.Responding to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's remarks on the bill, Rijiju accused the opposition party of not believing in democratic processes."The Congress party has never believed in democracy. We are seeking support for the sake of the democratic system itself. Otherwise, why would we even bring a bill forward? We could have just passed it," he said.He stressed that the government was seeking the bill's passage through a democratic process and appealed to the Congress not to turn the issue into a political confrontation.On Kharge's remarks, he further suggested that Rahul Gandhi might have influenced the Congress president's position, while adding that he could not say so with certainty."I cannot say for sure, but perhaps Rahul Gandhi ji pressured him; I really don't know. This is not the time for politics. What objection could there possibly be to empowering women?" Rijiju said.Centre is set to introduce the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday, seeking to implement one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state and Union territory legislative assemblies through a fresh delimitation exercise.The proposed legislation differs from the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, defeated in the Lok Sabha in April, mainly in its approach to delimitation, the allocation of seats among states and the census data to be used for redrawing constituencies.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: CRM team appreciates Tripura’s digital health ecosystem
content: The 18th Common Review Mission (CRM) state-level debriefing meeting was held on Saturday at Sonar Tori State Guest House, Agartala. Director of National Health Authority Dr. Piyush Singla, State Health Secretary Kiran Gitte, West Tripura District Magistrate Dr. Vishal Kumar; MD, NHM Tripura; and the CRM team led by Dr. Indu Grewal, Additional Commissioner, Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, were present. In the meeting, the central team appreciated Tripura’s progress and initiatives in strengthening the Digital Health Ecosystem. Meanwhile, Tripura has achieved a significant milestone with 2 Lakh+ Digital Health Records created through IHMIS (Integrated Health Management Information System). This achievement marks another important step towards a digitally empowered, efficient and patient-centric healthcare ecosystem, according to official sources. Through IHMIS, healthcare facilities across the State are embracing digital transformation with services including- Digital Patient Registration, ePrescription, Laboratory Reports, Digital Pharmacy Management and Admission & Discharge Management.

headline: CAT 2026: Check How Scores Are Normalised, Scaled And Converted Into Percentiles
content: CAT 2026 Scoring And Equating Process:The Common Admission Test (CAT) 2026 is scheduled to be held on November 29 in three sessions: from 8:30am to 10:30am, 12:30pm to 2:30pm, and 4:30pm to 6:30pm. To ensure fairness and equity in comparing the performance of candidates across different test sessions, their scores will be subjected to a normalisation process. The normalisation process will adjust for differences in the location and scale of score distributions across different test forms. After normalisation across the different forms, the scores will be further normalised across sections. The scaled scores obtained through this process will then be converted into percentiles for shortlisting purposes. For reporting purposes, the scaled scores for each section, namely Section 1: Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension (VARC), Section 2: Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR), and Section 3: Quantitative Ability (QA), along with the overall scaled score and percentiles, will be published. Through the normalisation process, candidate scores across multiple test forms are compared. This process is similar to the methods adopted in other large-scale educational selection tests conducted in India, such as the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE). The official release states that percentile equivalence will be used for normalisation across sections.

headline: Delimitation Bill provides for redrawing J&K seats in Pakistan-occupied area after occupation ends
content: NEW DELHI: The Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, listed for introduction in the Lok Sabha, provides for redrawing Jammu and Kashmir assembly constituencies in the part of the region under Pakistan's occupation once the occupation ends. Section 3(4) states that the Election Commission will act as the delimitation commission for the area when it ceases to be under occupation.The provision is conditional and would take effect only if the area is no longer occupied. The Bill uses the phrase "falling under the occupation of Pakistan" and does not use the term "PoK".Also Read| Gerrymandering is the new buzzword amid delimitation debate: What is it and why is opposition worriedWhat does the Bill sayUnder Section 3(4), the Election Commission would take on the role of the delimitation commission for assembly constituencies in the area. This differs from the arrangement proposed for the rest of the region.For other areas, the Bill provides for a separate delimitation commission chaired by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge. The Chief Election Commissioner or an election commissioner and the state election commissioner would be its members.The provision specifically refers to the Jammu and Kashmir legislative assembly. It does not mention Lok Sabha constituencies in the area.The Bill also does not refer to the 24 assembly seats reserved for the area or clarify whether the proposed 50% increase in seats would apply to them.The government will also introduce the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Second Bill, 2026. It seeks to amend laws governing Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry to align them with the proposed 132nd Constitutional Amendment.The constitutional amendment seeks to implement 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies after a fresh delimitation exercise, alongside a proposed 50% increase in seats.Also Read|No change in LS strength, 25-year seat protection: INDIA bloc's demands on delimitationDelhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry are the three Union territories with legislative assemblies.The delimitation and Union Territories Bills were first introduced in April along with the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill. The package was intended to operationalise women's reservation from 2029.However, the Constitution amendment Bill failed to secure the required numbers in the Lok Sabha. As a result, the other two Bills could not be taken up for voting.The government will now withdraw the pending Bills and introduce fresh versions on Monday, along with a new Constitution amendment Bill.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
