headline: Chandrababu Naidu hails Chennai Jain couple's  ₹206 crore donation to Tirumala temple: Here's what they offered
content: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has praised a Chennai-based Jain couple for donating 121 kg of gold ornaments and diamonds, valued at around ₹206 crore, to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), describing the contribution as unprecedented in the temple body's history.Vardhaman Jain and his wife Radhika Jain made the offering to Lord Venkateswara in the presence of Naidu at Tirumala on Thursday. According to TTD sources cited by PTI, this is believed to be the largest donation made by an individual devotee to the deity.Addressing the media alongside the donors, Naidu said the contribution would inspire others to use their wealth for charitable and religious purposes. He described service to humanity as an important purpose of life and said the couple had demonstrated the principle of 'Manava Sevaye Madhava Seva' (service to humanity is service to God), Hans India reported.Naidu also recalled the contributions made by several royal dynasties, including the Pallavas, Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas and Vijayanagara rulers, towards the development of the Tirumala temple. He said the Jain couple's offering continued the tradition of devotees and rulers donating valuable ornaments and other assets to Lord Venkateswara.What did the Jain couple donate?The donation comprises 46 ornaments arranged in nine sets, including a crown for Lord Venkateswara, ornaments for the deity's feet and diamonds weighing 238.2 carats, according to PTI.The offering includes:106 kg of gold ornaments: These have been made for Lord Venkateswara and include crowns, chains and several other types of jewellery.15 kg of gold: This portion will be used to prepare a ceremonial garment, or Vastram, for Goddess Sri Padmavati Ammavaru at Tiruchanoor. Donor Vardhaman Jain said it is expected to be presented within the next three months, according to Hans India.238.2 carats of diamonds: The precious stones form part of the jewellery offering.A Srivaru crown: A crown offered to Lord Venkateswara.Padma Paadalu: Ornaments designed for the deity's feet.A golden tiger nail: Among the distinctive ornaments included in the donation.Chains, crowns and other jewellery: The offering also includes different varieties of gold chains, precious stones and other ornaments.The official press release said the donation included 46 ornaments across nine sets. The gold ornaments for Lord Venkateswara weighed 106 kg, while the remaining 15 kg was earmarked for the costume of Goddess Padmavati.What did Chandrababu Naidu say about the donation?Naidu said he considered himself fortunate to witness what he described as a historic contribution to the temple. He noted that the donation included valuable diamonds along with the gold ornaments.He also urged TTD to protect the sanctity of the temple and strengthen its religious and social service activities. He called for greater focus on cow protection, preservation of Vedic traditions and expansion of services by Srivari Sevaks.He further said that 5,000 temples would be built with TTD's assistance and called for free food services for devotees at temples. He also suggested constructing temples overseas in places with large Hindu populations.

headline: Indias domestic economy expected to sustain momentum into Q3 FY27 amid global uncertainties: Monthly Economic Review
content: New Delhi [India], November 28 (ANI): Domestic economic activity is expected to sustain its momentum into Q3 FY27, with high-frequency indicators pointing to continued expansion across goods movement, tax collections, energy consumption and freight, according to the Department of Economic Affairs’ Monthly Economic Review November 2026 report."Business activity is likely to remain firm, with new orders gaining pace and input cost pressures easing," the report stated.Consumption continues to back growth across both urban and rural pockets. Vehicle sales maintain sequential gains, while rural spending shows steady strength. Fertiliser stocks remain comfortable for the rabi season, though sowing stays in its early stage and reservoir storage sits below last year's level."Overall, industrial activity continued to expand, although industrial production growth moderated in September and manufacturing PMI eased in October while remaining in the expansionary zone," the report noted.Industrial production grew 6.7 per cent in September, with manufacturing acting as the primary driver. The Index of Core Industries expanded 10.9 per cent year-on-year in October 2026, bringing cumulative growth during April-October 2026-27 to 6.0 per cent. Bank credit to industry and infrastructure increases alongside steel consumption, while policy measures target capacity creation across critical minerals, electronics, energy storage and container manufacturing.On the price front, headline retail inflation rose by 55 basis points to 6.09 per cent in October 2026, pushed up by consumer food prices and an unfavourable base effect. Still, more than half of the consumer price index basket records inflation below the four per cent target."With the festive season persisting into November and the onset of the wedding/nuptial season, upcoming inflation prints may face upside risks due to increased demand across food and nonfood items," the report added.Weather patterns also demand attention, as the World Meteorological Organisation warns that an exceptionally strong El Niño event could peak toward the end of 2026. The Indian Ocean Dipole Index stands at 0.8 degrees Celsius, which could offset El Niño conditions if it persists."However, recent moderation in global crude oil prices, with benchmarks falling below USD 100 per barrel in early November and strengthening of the rupee following robust capital inflows, may provide some relief from imported inflationary pressures, contingent upon the persistence of this trend," the report said.India's external sector displays resilience despite conflict in the Middle East and shipping risks in the Strait of Hormuz. Merchandise exports rose 45 per cent year-on-year in October 2026 to USD 49.5 billion, marking the highest monthly export value on record. A strong services trade surplus offsets 49.6 per cent of the merchandise trade deficit during the month."Higher foreign direct investment inflows, along with substantial banking capital inflows, continue to support the overall balance of payments," the report stated. Foreign exchange reserves stood at USD 705.3 billion as of November 13, 2026, covering 10 months of imports."The economy enters the coming months with firm domestic momentum, underpinned by resilient consumption demand, a gradual broadening of private investment and continued policy support for manufacturing," the report noted, adding that domestic fundamentals and macroeconomic buffers leave India well placed to navigate global trade uncertainties. (ANI)(This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: 'Historic blunder': Congress's Imran Masood warns DMK, NCP over delimitation Bill support
content: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Saturday criticised the DMK and the NCP (SP) over reports that they could support the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, warning that such a move could have serious political consequences for the parties.“This would be a historic blunder for DMK and and for the NCP, such a move could threaten their very existence—it will prove most detrimental to them...” Masood said.His remarks came hours before the DMK formally backed the revised delimitation proposal, with party chief MK Stalin calling it a "major victory" for Tamil Nadu after a three-year struggle to protect the state's share of Lok Sabha seats.The decision was taken at a meeting of DMK MPs chaired by Stalin ahead of the special sitting of Parliament, scheduled to begin on November 30.Also Read| 'Stalin, aka Savarkar 2.0': Vijay's TVK mocks DMK with RSS posts over Centre's delimitation bidMasood also accused the Centre of attempting to manipulate political representation through delimitation and alleged that the government was working to alter the country's constitutional framework.Reacting to the Union Cabinet's approval of the proposed Bill, he alleged that the government had been undermining the Constitution for the past 12 years."Under the pretext of delimitation, they intend to manipulate representation. This has been an ongoing trend for the last 12 years—just yesterday, Justice Gavai even wrote a letter to the President, noting that there is a caste imbalance within the Supreme Court itself. They are consistently working to trample upon the Constitution. You will see that the representation of the most backward communities, Scheduled Castes, and minorities is extremely low in this framework. In reality, they are attempting to alter the very fabric of the nation. The Constitution is the soul of India, and that soul is being tampered with..." he said.DMK formally backed BillThe DMK's backing comes after the party opposed an earlier delimitation proposal, arguing that using recent population figures to redraw constituencies could reduce Tamil Nadu's share of parliamentary representation and disproportionately benefit northern states.Stalin said the revised proposal addressed the party's key concerns by providing for a uniform 50% increase in seats across states while retaining Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18% share in the Lok Sabha.Earlier on Friday, Stalin had asserted that Tamil Nadu's existing share of Lok Sabha seats must not be reduced under any circumstances."No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu's interests; nor will it depart from its principles," Stalin said.NCP (SP) yet to clarify standMeanwhile, NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule has said she will skip the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled for Saturday, citing the health of her father and party chief Sharad Pawar.Sharad Pawar was admitted to a hospital in south Mumbai on Thursday due to dehydration. Sule said she would remain in Mumbai over the weekend and travel to Delhi on Monday to attend the Parliament session."I will go to Delhi on Monday morning to attend the session," she wrote in her WhatsApp status, PTI reported.Meanwhile, Leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge called for a meeting of opposition floor leaders at his residence in New Delhi to formulate a joint strategy ahead of the proposed legislation.The INDIA bloc put forward three key demands on the proposed delimitation exercise, calling for the existing strength of the Lok Sabha to be maintained, women's reservation to be implemented within the current House strength and the allocation of seats among states to remain unchanged for the next 25 years.This comes before the special sitting of Parliament scheduled to begin on November 30 in the Lok Sabha, while the Rajya Sabha will meet on December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: KCBC panel expresses concern at delay in announcing UDF govt’s liquor policy
content: KOCHI The Temperance Commission of the Kerala Catholic Bishops Council (KCBC) has expressed concern at the State Government’s inordinate delay in announcing its liquor policy for the fiscal, six months after assuming office. The delay has occurred, even as there are only four more months left for the expiry of the annual policy’s time span. The policy for the forthcoming 2027-28 fiscal ought to be announced in April, 2027, said Prasad Kuruvilla, the State secretary of the KCBC Madya Virudha Samity. There is need for clarity on a decision taken by a sub committee on the matter. Former Excise Minister M.B. Rajesh’s response on the matter is nothing but an acknowledgement that the previous Government’s liquor policy too was a damaging one, he added. The ruling coalition, the United Democratic Front (UDF), has the other day constituted a sub committee to carry out consultations before formulating the government’s liquor policy. In the wake of a controversy over the issue of bar licences, including the grant of licence to a lounge at the Cochin International Airport Ltd (CIAL),the government in early November announced a blanket ban on the issue of new licences until the liquor policy was promulgated. The controversy also led to an open war of words between Excise Minister M. Liju and the then Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao.

headline: Mayawati seeks separate quota for SC, ST women ahead of Parliament session
content: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Saturday welcomed the Centre’s renewed push for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies but demanded a separate sub-quota for women belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST), saying it would ensure more meaningful and equitable representation.Ahead of the special session of Parliament beginning November 30, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister also questioned the political intentions behind the proposed 50% expansion of the Lok Sabha and state assemblies and the accompanying delimitation exercise. She alleged that governments in power often use electoral arrangements to advance their political interests rather than public welfare.In a series of posts on X, Mayawati said the BSP consistently supported women’s reservation and demanded its early implementation. However, she argued that women from historically oppressed and marginalised communities needed a separate arrangement within the proposed quota.Delimitation bill LIVE updates | Kharge says Oppn will oppose bill over SC/ST concerns as INDIA bloc lists 3 demands “Had a separate reservation been provided to women from SC and ST communities, it would have been a historic step,” she said, urging the Centre to consider the demand sympathetically.The Union Cabinet cleared a legislative package to operationalise women’s reservation through delimitation, proposing a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha and assembly seats in every state. The package includes the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026 and legislation relating to Union Territories.The proposals seek to facilitate 33% reservation for women ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The delimitation exercise is proposed to use the 2011 Census for redrawing constituency boundaries while retaining the existing inter-state representation ratio based on the 1971 Census until 2051.ALSO READ | Stalin-led DMK backs Centre on delimitation, says core demands included in proposed billQuestioning the proposed exercise, Mayawati alleged that the party in power at the Centre could influence seat allocation and constituency boundaries to suit its electoral interests.Her remarks assume political significance ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, particularly as the proposed expansion of legislative seats and reservation arrangements could reshape political representation and candidate selection.Mayawati also appealed to voters to rise above religious, caste and regional considerations while choosing their representatives. She urged them not to be swayed by political parties’ promises and announcements, but to elect candidates with integrity and commitment to public welfare.ALSO READ | Supreme Court judge, poll chiefs in the panel poised to redraw every constituency’s boundariesInvoking BR Ambedkar’s legacy, she said the BSP remained committed to the Constitution’s principles of equality, dignity and social justice.The proposed constitutional framework provides for women from SC and ST communities to be covered under the one-third reservation, with their reserved seats rotated within existing SC/ST constituencies. Mayawati, however, is seeking a more explicit separate arrangement for women from these communities.The Centre’s proposals are yet to receive parliamentary approval, with the special session expected to discuss the constitutional amendments and the proposed delimitation framework.

headline: No change in LS strength, 25-year seat protection: INDIA bloc's demands on delimitation
content: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Saturday put forward three key demands on the proposed delimitation exercise, calling for the existing strength of the Lok Sabha to be maintained, women's reservation to be implemented within the current House strength and the allocation of seats among states to remain unchanged for the next 25 years.The demands were outlined by the Congress after a meeting of INDIA bloc floor leaders at the residence of party president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, in New Delhi. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and several other Opposition leaders attended the meeting to discuss the proposed legislation and formulate a joint strategy ahead of the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.In a post on X, the Congress said the proposed delimitation Bill was discussed at the meeting and reiterated the Opposition's position on the exercise.Also Read| Gerrymandering is the new buzzword amid delimitation debate: What is it and why is opposition worried"Our clear demands are: The current strength of the Lok Sabha should be maintained; Women's reservation should be provided based on the current strength of the Lok Sabha; The current allocation of seats among states in the Lok Sabha should be maintained for the next 25 years," the party said.\Addressing a press conference after the meeting, Kharge said the government was now aiming for "800 paar" by proposing to increase the Lok Sabha's strength to 850, after its earlier electoral slogan of "400 paar" had fallen by the wayside. He alleged that the move was intended to help the ruling party seize and retain power indefinitely.Also Read| EC hikes honorarium for SIR tribunal judgesKharge also accused the government of disregarding the interests of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the proposed amendment. He said the number of seats reserved for these communities in each state should be proportionate to their population and argued that the proposed legislation made no provision for increasing the number of SC-reserved seats."Furthermore, the interests of the Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) have been completely disregarded; this is an act of injustice... The number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in any given state must be proportional to their respective populations within that state. Consequently, the number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Castes should increase; however, there is no provision for this in the proposed amendment," he said.Pointing to the upcoming 2026 Census, Kharge questioned why the government had remained silent on using the latest population data for the exercise. He alleged that relying on the latest Census figures would increase the number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in line with their population, but the proposed amendment appeared aimed at denying these communities their "rightful share".Among those who attended the meeting were Congress leaders Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Pawan Khera, KC Venugopal, Syed Nasir Hussain, Pramod Tiwari and Gaurav Gogoi, besides Trinamool Congress MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek O'Brien.CPM leader A. Rahim, Rashtriya Samaj Party MP N K Premachandran, National Conference leader Chowdry Mohammad Ramzan, Rashtriya Janata Dal leaders Abhay Kushwaha and Manoj Jha, Samajwadi Party MP Ramji Lal Suman and Indian Union Muslim League leader E T Mohammed Basheer were also present.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Arvind Sawant, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha leader Baidyanath Ram, who joined online, CPI leader P. Santosh and Independent MP Kapil Sibal attended the meeting. A VCK leader could not participate due to a wedding at his residence.The Nationalist Congress Party-Sharadchandra Pawar (NCP-SP), which has indicated support for the revised delimitation proposals, was absent. The DMK, which has also backed the revised proposals subject to safeguards for Tamil Nadu's representation, did not attend either.The meeting comes amid differences within the Opposition over the proposed legislation. While some regional parties have indicated support for the revised proposals, others have raised concerns about their impact on the representation of states.The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), meanwhile, has received a boost after the DMK and NCP-SP indicated support for the revised proposals. The two parties together have 30 Lok Sabha MPs, potentially taking the alliance's estimated strength from around 320 to 350.The DMK, which has 22 Lok Sabha MPs, has backed the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states but has insisted that Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18 per cent share should not be reduced. DMK MP A Raja has said the party would seek amendments to other provisions if necessary.The NCP-SP, which has eight Lok Sabha MPs, has also indicated support for the revised proposals. Party leader Jitendra Awhad said on Friday that the party had decided to back the delimitation process, describing it as a constitutional requirement. The party had opposed the earlier Bill introduced in April but said it would support the fresh proposal if it provided for a uniform 50 per cent increase in seats.The BJP is confident of securing the required two-thirds majority, banking on support from some parties that opposed the earlier Bill and possible backing from Trinamool Congress MPs who may break ranks.The government would need 360 votes if all 540 sitting members participated in the voting. However, the actual two-thirds threshold would depend on the number of members present and voting. A separate requirement of a majority of the House's total membership would also apply.The Lok Sabha currently has 540 sitting members and three vacancies. If Trinamool Congress MP Kalyan Banerjee's suspension remains in force, 539 members, including the Speaker, could attend the proceedings. The Bill would require 359 votes if all 538 members other than the Speaker voted. The threshold would fall if some members were absent.The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations: the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and a proposed amendment to laws governing Union Territories. The Bills are scheduled to be taken up during the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.The proposed legislative package provides for a 50 per cent increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to every state and Union Territory, along with a corresponding increase in the strength of state legislative assemblies. It is also intended to facilitate the implementation of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provides for 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.The Opposition has backed women's reservation but objected to linking its implementation with delimitation. It has also called for the exercise to be based on the latest Census data.Under the Centre's proposal, the 2011 Census would be used for redrawing constituencies and determining seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while the 1971 population basis for allocating Lok Sabha seats among states would be retained until 2051.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Delimitation Bill won't pass': Congress MP says opposition will 'unite to defend' Constitution
content: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Pramod Tiwari on Saturday asserted that the proposed delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, would fail to clear Parliament during the upcoming special session beginning November 30. He expressed confidence that Opposition parties would close ranks to “defend the Constitution”, accusing the government of attacking and disrespecting its principles.Tiwari's remarks came as INDIA bloc floor leaders met at leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi to discuss a joint strategy against the Centre's proposed constitutional amendment and delimitation exercise."We are fully confident that when it comes to the Constitution, everyone will unite. As the Constitution is being attacked and disrespected, everyone will also stand with us to defend the Constitution. We are fully confident that it will not pass," Tiwari told news agency ANI.The meeting was attended by Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Jairam Ramesh, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K C Venugopal, besides Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, RJD leaders Abhay Kumar Singh and Manoj Jha, CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar, IUML MP ET Mohammed Basheer and RSP MP NK Premachandran, among others.Parties outside the INDIA bloc, including the DMK, AAP and BJD, were also invited but did not attend.Meanwhile, DMK MP A Raja indicated that his party was prepared to support the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states, provided Tamil Nadu's existing share of representation remained protected.Speaking to ANI after a DMK meeting, Raja said, "Our consistent demand is that the share of 7.18% (seat share in Lok Sabha) should not be altered. Now it is being maintained. Of course, procedural issues are there; we will address them. If necessary, we will give an amendment."The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared three revised draft legislations: the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and a proposed amendment to laws governing Union territories.The constitutional amendment proposes increasing the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, including up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories. It also seeks a 50 per cent increase in the number of seats allocated to each state and Union territory, while raising the maximum strength of state assemblies from 500 to 650.The proposed changes are intended to facilitate the implementation of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provides for 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The revised seat allocations and boundaries are also proposed to remain frozen until 2051.However, Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal questioned the need for increasing the strength of Parliament to implement women's reservation."At the national level, if this Bill is passed, the number of Lok Sabha seats could increase to around 850. The first question is whether a House of 850 members can function properly," Sibal told reporters ahead of the Opposition meeting."We are ready for women's reservation. They can implement it immediately within the existing 543 seats. So that is not their real objective. Their real objective is to remain in power for the next 30-40 years. And for that, what matters most to them is the delimitation Bill," he alleged.The fresh legislative push comes seven months after the earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17. It received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, falling 54 votes short of the 352 required.The special session is scheduled to begin on November 30, with the Rajya Sabha reconvening on December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: CCSI Computer Education Empowers Students with Future-Ready Skills Through Industry-Focused Training
content: VMPLNew Delhi [India], November 28: CCSI Computer Education is more than a computer training institute; it is a platform designed to help learners build future-ready careers. With over 20 years of expertise, ISO certification and a reputation for training excellence, the institute focuses on empowering students with practical and industry-relevant skills across IT, design, coding and digital technologies.Driven by its mission to transform learners into confident, industry-ready and future-proof professionals, CCSI Computer Education offers a wide range of training programmes designed to support career development and skill enhancement in an evolving professional landscape.Building Careers Through Industry-Oriented EducationAt CCSI Computer Education, the focus is on equipping learners with practical knowledge, technical expertise and professional skills that can support their career ambitions. The institute highlights its ISO and IAF certification, more than 20 years of career excellence, experienced trainers, job-ready diploma programmes and career support as key strengths.By combining structured training with a focus on industry requirements, CCSI aims to create learning opportunities for students and aspiring professionals seeking to build careers in technology and business-related fields.Comprehensive Future-Ready Training ProgrammesCCSI Computer Education offers a diverse selection of programmes across programming, development, design, animation, business productivity and advanced IT disciplines.Programming and DevelopmentThe institute offers training in C, C++ and Java programming, Python, Django and Flask, along with Full Stack Web Development and Mobile App Development. These programmes are designed to help learners develop programming knowledge and application development skills.Design and AnimationFor learners interested in creative and digital design careers, CCSI provides training in Graphic Design, UI/UX Design, 2D and 3D Animation, VFX and Motion Graphics, and Game Design. headline: Common Admission Test 2026 Tomorrow: Check Slot Timings, Dress Code, Exam Day Guidelines
content: CAT 2026 Exam Day Guidelines: The Common Admission Test 2026 (CAT 2026) is scheduled to be held tomorrow, November 29, in three sessions across approximately 170 cities. To ensure the security of the test, the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) have put in place additional measures, including face matching and the deployment of mobile jammers at select locations. The CAT 2026 examination will be held for 120 minutes (2 hours). The test will comprise the following three sections: Candidates will be allotted exactly 40 minutes to answer questions in each section. They will not be allowed to switch from one section to another while attempting a section. Candidates are advised to locate their test centre and check its accessibility at least a day before the examination. This will help them choose an appropriate mode of transport and reach the test centre on time on the exam day. Candidates arriving late will not be allowed to enter the test centre and will be barred from appearing for the test.

headline: 'Made promise to Nari Shakti': PM Modi pushes for delimitation Bill after Cabinet nod
content: NEW DELHI: With the Union Cabinet clearing the revised constitutional amendment and delimitation Bills to pave the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday vowed to overcome all hurdles to their implementation. He also hit out at parties opposing the move, asserting that they would not be able to prevent women from securing greater representation in legislative bodies.Taking to social media platform X, PM Modi shared a video with the caption: "We made a promise to our Nari Shakti and we remain committed to fulfilling it..."In the video, the Prime Minister said the struggle to secure greater political participation for women had continued for decades, adding that he had also been working towards the cause for years."The fight to give Nari Shakti their rightful participation has been going on for decades. For years, I too have been among those making efforts towards this cause. Many women have raised this issue before me. Many sisters have written letters to me, sharing their concerns," PM Modi said.He further said he was aware of the expectations of women across the country and assured them that his government would address obstacles to implementing the quota."I know that the blessings of 100 per cent of the country's Nari Shakti are with us. I assure every woman in the country that we will remove every obstacle that comes in the way of women's reservation. We will ensure that these hurdles are removed," he said."Our morale is high, our courage is unshaken, and our resolve is firm," PM Modi added. He also accused parties opposing women's reservation of attempting to prevent women from securing greater representation in legislative bodies."Parties opposing women's reservation will never be able to stop the Nari Shakti of this country from increasing their participation in Parliament and state assemblies. It is only a matter of time," he said.The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations, including the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026. The constitutional amendment proposes increasing the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, comprising up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories.The proposal also provides for a uniform 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states and Union territories, alongside an increase in the maximum strength of state assemblies from 500 to 650. The revised allocation of seats between states is proposed to remain frozen until 2051, with the 1971 Census retained as the basis for inter-state seat distribution.The fresh proposal comes after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha in April.Meanwhile, INDIA bloc leaders met at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to discuss a joint strategy. Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal questioned the proposed expansion, asking whether an 850-member Lok Sabha could function effectively. He also alleged that the government's objective extended beyond women's reservation.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Boost To Centre As DMK Declares Support For Delimitation Bill
content: The turnaround by the southern party with 22 MPs, which has been critical of the delimitation exercise in the past, has bolstered the ruling side's numbers that plans to avenge the defeat of the bill in April.

headline: CJI lauds outgoing SC judge S C Sharma's judicial contributions, warmth and wit
content: New Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday paid a glowing tribute to outgoing Supreme Court judge Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, saying that his cheerful disposition, warmth and sense of humour enriched the institution beyond his judicial contributions.Speaking at the ceremonial bench proceedings, the CJI said a judge's contribution to an institution was reflected not merely in the judgments delivered or positions held, but also in the temperament brought to the Bench, relationships built with colleagues and warmth extended to everyone in institutional life.The ceremonial bench comprised the CJI and Justices Sharma, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana."The contribution of a judge to an institution is not always captured by the judgments they write or the office they occupy. It is equally reflected in the temperament they bring to the bench. The relationship they build with colleagues and the warmth they bring to everyone in institutional life," the CJI said.Describing Justice Sharma as a judge of "considerable experience and learning" with a lively disposition and a wonderful sense of humour, the CJI said he admired his ability to remain cheerful despite the demands of judicial work.Tracing his journey, the CJI recalled that Justice Sharma was designated a senior advocate at 42, a rare distinction, and was elevated to the Madhya Pradesh High Court in January 2008.The CJI also referred to Justice Sharma's tenure as the Acting Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court and then as Chief Justice of the Telangana and Delhi High Courts.The CJI highlighted Justice Sharma's work in the Delhi High Court on the implementation of statutory protections for persons with disabilities, where he stressed that the promise of equality must translate into meaningful opportunities.He also cited the Ashok Agarwal case, in which the court emphasised effective safeguards against manual scavenging.These decisions, the CJI said, reflect the recognition that "the true worth of legal protections lies in their implementation."Justice Sharma thanked the CJI, fellow judges, bar leaders, the registry and his staff, including law clerks.Recalling that he joined the bar at Jabalpur 42 years ago as a first-generation lawyer, he said, "The bar at Jabalpur gave me a place and a chance to prove myself. The bench gave me a purpose."He said his career across the Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana and Delhi High Courts had given him many memories and friendships, and called his service in the Supreme Court "the greatest privilege of life".Justice Sharma hoped the institution would "continue to uphold the majesty of law, protect the rights of citizens and strengthen the faith of the people in the administration of justice".Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the court would miss two things: Justice Sharma's smile and his habit of saying "I'm so sorry" to the losing party when dismissing a special leave petition.Supreme Court Bar Association president Pradeep Rai described Justice Sharma as known for his smile, humility and willingness to encourage young lawyers. Recalling his time in Indore, he said the judge had been particularly considerate towards the poor. On behalf of the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association , a representative thanked him for standing by the bar and AORs.Born on November 30, 1961 in Bhopal, Justice Sharma initially practised in constitutional, service, civil and criminal matters before the Madhya Pradesh High Court at Jabalpur.He was appointed additional central government counsel on May 28, 1993 and was appointed a senior panel counsel by the Government of India on June 28, 2004.In 2003, at the age of 42, Justice Sharma was designated as a senior advocate by the Madhya Pradesh High Court.He was elevated as an additional judge of the Madhya Pradesh High Court on January 18, 2008 and was appointed as a permanent judge on January 15, 2010. He was transferred to the Karnataka High Court as a judge on December 31, 2020.Justice Sharma was later appointed as Acting Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court on August 31, 2021 and was elevated as the Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court on October 11 that year.He was later transferred to the Delhi High Court as Chief Justice and took the oath of office on June 28, 2022.Justice Sharma, who was elevated as a judge of the apex court on November 9, 2023 is slated to retire on November 29.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 'Stalin, aka Savarkar 2.0': Vijay's TVK mocks DMK with RSS posts over Centre's delimitation bid
content: NEW DELHI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Saturday mocked Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam chief MK Stalin, with a morphed image of him clad in RSS uniform after the party announced its support for Centre's proposed delimitation Bill."Stalin, aka Savarkar 2.0," TVK's IT wing tweeted with the picture.In another animated post, MK Stalin and his son Udhayanidhi Stalin were represented as taking the oath as RRS members."The moment [they] turned completely Sanghi!" it read.The criticism came after DMK decided to support the revised Delimitation Bill in Parliament, with party deputy general secretary and MP A Raja saying the legislation provides for a uniform 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for all states. DMK has 22 members in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha.Justifying the party's decision, Stalin described the revised legislation as a major victory for Tamil Nadu's three-year-long struggle over delimitation. He said the Bill addressed the party's two key demands raised in its 2024 Assembly resolution.The revised proposal does not base delimitation on recent population figures, which the DMK had argued would disproportionately benefit northern states. Instead, it uses the 1971 Census as the basis for determining parliamentary representation.Stalin said the arrangement would allow Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha seats to increase while preserving its existing proportion of representation in Parliament, safeguarding the state's political interests for the next 25 years.The DMK had earlier opposed and defeated a previous version of the Bill, which it had described as hurriedly introduced.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Unchanged Lok Sabha strength, women’s quota within existing seats among INDIA bloc demands on delimitation
content: The INDIA bloc on Saturday laid down three conditions on the proposed delimitation exercise, demanding that the Lok Sabha's existing strength and the current allocation of seats among states remain unchanged for the next 25 years. INDIA bloc floor leaders met at Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi on Saturday and discussed a joint strategy in view of the Centre's move to reintroduce a constitutional amendment bill in Parliament, involving delimitation.The bloc put forward three demands: maintaining the Lok Sabha's current strength, providing women's reservation based on the existing strength of the House, and retaining the current allocation of seats among states in the Lok Sabha for the next 25 years.Also Read: 50% more seats, bigger state assemblies: Five changes in the new delimitation bills"The current strength of the Lok Sabha should be maintained. Women's reservation should be provided based on the current strength of the Lok Sabha.The current allocation of seats among states in the Lok Sabha should be maintained for the next 25 years," the party posted on X, sharing a picture from the meeting. Besides Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, TMC's Abhishek Banerjee, Independent Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, RJD's Abhay Kumar Singh and Manoj Jha, CPI's P Sandosh Kumar, IUML's ET Mohammed Basheer, RSP's NK Premchandran, among others, participated in the meeting.Congress general secretaries Jairam Ramesh, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K C Venugopal, among others, also attended the meeting.Meanwhile, the NDA has received a boost in its numbers after the DMK and the NCP-SP indicated support for the revised delimitation proposals. Their combined strength of 30 MPs could take the ruling alliance's estimated tally from around 320 to 350 in the Lok Sabha.The government would, however, require 360 votes if all 540 sitting members participate in the voting to meet the two-thirds threshold. The actual requirement will depend on the number of members present and voting, while the separate requirement of a majority of the House's total membership will also apply.The DMK, which has 22 Lok Sabha MPs, has announced support for the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states, while maintaining that Tamil Nadu's existing share of representation must remain protected. DMK MP A Raja said the party would seek amendments to other provisions if necessary. (With inputs from agencies)

headline: Former judges meet officials, CRPF personnel over Karthigai Deepam row
content: Former judges S Vaidyanathan, former Chief Justice of the Meghalaya High Court, and V Parthiban, former judge of the Madras High Court, travelled from Chennai to Madurai on Saturday following the Supreme Court’s suspension of the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramanya Swamy Temple at Tirupparankundram.The two judges met senior district officials and CRPF personnel as part of the process of assuming administrative control of the temple, located about 8km from Madurai. They arrived in the temple town on Saturday morning and drove to Residency Hotel, where media access was restricted as part of security arrangements, police said.The consultation meeting was held at the third floor of the hotel in presence of top CRPF personnel including Inspector General (IG) Thummala Vikram. According to people familiar with the matter, the meeting went over for more than 40 minutes. Also Read:Deepathoon: Why the Supreme Court ordered the Karthigai Deepam to be lit on November 28 Discussions also focused on the spot where the ceremonial lamp would be lit at the Deepathoon, the location of the Dargah and the pathway leading up to the hill.The Deepathoon (stone pillar) is located about 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah, while the Uchi Pillayar temple is about 250 metres from the pillar.The former judges also consulted officials of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department and sthanika bhattars (heritage priests) on the procedures to be followed for lighting the ceremonial lamp.On Friday, the Supreme Court reiterated its November 20 order directing that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the Deepathoon. On November 24, the Tamil Nadu government failed to comply with the directive.The two former judges or the receivers should ensure that the ceremony is carried out properly.The apex court also allowed members of the public to light the lamp on the hill on Saturday, while ensuring that members of Muslim groups could access the Dargah, also located atop the hill, to offer prayers.Members of the Muslim community and various Muslim organisations arrived in large numbers on Saturday and queued up to climb the hill to offer prayers at the Dargah.CRPF personnel, who arrived in the early hours of Saturday, checked the identity cards of Muslim visitors before allowing them access to the hill.

headline: ‘Committed to fulfil promise to Nari Shakti’: PM Modi vows to clear all hurdles to women’s quota
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday reaffirmed his government's commitment to implementing 33% reservation for women in the Parliament, adding that parties opposing this move would not succeed.His remarks came as the Union Cabinet on Friday approved two bills proposing a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states and Union Territories and the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament following delimitation.In a post on X, PM Modi vowed to remove all hurdles to women's reservation in Parliament and state legislatures. Follow Delimitation Bill LIVE Updates hereThe PM posted a brief video, where he said, "The fight to ensure women's participation has been going on for decades. I, too, have been among those striving for this. Women have consistently raised this issue with me, and many sisters have shared their concerns." The Prime Minister asserted that the BJP government had the backing of all women in the country and assured that the Centre will remove all obstacles standing in the way of women's reservation."Humara hausla bhi buland hai, humari himmat bhi atoot hai aur humara iraada bhi adig hai. (Our morale is high, our courage is unbreakable and our resolve is firm)," he said.He had also stressed that parties opposing women's reservation will never be able to stop them from increasing their participation in Parliament and legislative assemblies.Also Read | Unchanged Lok Sabha strength, women’s quota within existing seats among INDIA bloc demands on delimitationCentre's delimitation pushPM Modi's latest message comes amid the Centre's fresh push on the delimitation bill. The Centre had earlier passed a bill that paved the way for 33% reservation for women in Parliament, but an effort to pass the delimitation bill in April to operationalise the quota was defeated by the Opposition.The Union Cabinet on Friday approved an amended bill on delimitation, which proposes a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states and Union Territories, taking the House's maximum strength to 850. The proposed seat arrangement will remain in place for the next 25 years.Also Read | Stalin-led DMK backs Centre on delimitation, says core demands included in proposed billBJP leaders have appealed to Opposition MPs to support the proposed Delimitation Bill and women’s reservation, saying the move would strengthen democracy and ensure women receive their rightful representation in Parliament and state Assemblies. The bill has also received support from Tamil Nadu's DMK and Maharashtra's NCP (SP).On the other hand, the INDIA bloc held a meeting on Saturday and listed three key demands for delimitation, such as maintaining the current strength of the Lok Sabha, implementing women's reservation and keeping the allocation of Lok Sabha seats unchanged.

headline: Both seats belong to Congress: Imran Masood on SP naming candidates for Saharanpur
content: Congress MP Imran Masood on Saturday said the two Assembly seats in Saharanpur district on which the Samajwadi Party has announced its candidates "belong to the Congress", and urged SP chief Akhilesh Yadav to show a big heart and give space.Asserting that the Congress' position is "very clear", Masood said his party wants to fight the Assembly elections with the SP and wants Yadav to become the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister."But our only demand is that we too should be given space," Masood told PTI Videos here."Both those seats belong to the Congress. The Congress won them in 2017. In 2022, the Samajwadi Party won them because I had joined the Samajwadi Party. If you look at the electoral equations in those constituencies, whenever the Samajwadi Party contested without me, the party had no presence there," Masood said when asked about the SP naming candidates for the two Saharanpur seats.If the Congress leaves seats in which it has a strong base, then what will be left with it, he argued.On the SP offering the Congress 26 seats, Masood said underestimating the Congress in this manner is not a good thing. The Congress cannot contest polls by surrendering itself, he said.He further said Yadav is a very senior leader who wants to become the Chief Minister and he must show a big heart by giving the Congress some room.On the status of the Congress-SP alliance, Masood said, "Our position is very clear. We want the elections to be fought together, and we want Akhilesh Yadav to become the UP CM. But our only demand is that we too should be given space."Responding to SP leader Azam Khan's remarks on the Congress' demands for seats, he said, "We are not beggars asking you for something. We have nothing to ask from you. That is all I will say on this."On the number of seats the Congress wants to contest, Masood said the party contested 107 seats in 2017 and the situation now is much better for it.Asked about the Aazad Samaj Party-AIMIM alliance for the Uttar Pradesh polls, Masood said everyone is free to do what they want and it makes no difference."The contest is a straight fight between two ideologies. One ideology is led by (PM Narendra) Modi ji, while the other is led by Rahul (Gandhi) ji," he stressed.Tensions are simmering between the Congress and the SP over seat-sharing negotiations and at the centre of the strain is Masood and his claim to two seats that fall within his parliamentary constituency of Saharanpur -- Saharanpur and Behat.There are five Assembly segments in the Saharanpur Lok Sabha constituency -- Behat, Saharanpur Nagar, Saharanpur, Deoband and Rampur Maniharan (SC).Saharanpur district has seven Assembly seats overall, but Nakur and Gangoh fall under other parliamentary constituencies.The SP's announcement of five candidates for the Assembly polls amid the seat-sharing talks with the Congress has exposed alliance constraints.While the SP has played down the announcement as having declared seats in which its claims are indisputable, the Congress has said that this should have been avoided when seat-sharing talks were ongoing.Miffed at the SP leadership announcing the names, Masood had earlier said that his party "isn't begging" and he would consult the leadership on whether to continue the seat-sharing negotiations.The SP has maintained that four of the five seats where it announced candidates were represented by four sitting MLAs -- Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Umar Ali Khan from Behat (Saharanpur), Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha, all west Uttar Pradesh seats, where the SP and Congress are likely to face a challenge from BJP ally RLD and the Samajik Parivartan Morcha of Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Aazad.The fifth candidate, Jyoti Lodhi, has been named from Lalitpur. The SP had earlier declared Tej Narain Pandey alias Pawan Pandey as its candidate from Ayodhya.Of Saharanpur district's seven assembly seats, the BJP won five in 2022 -- Deoband, Gangoh, Nakur, Rampur Maniharan (SC) and Saharanpur Nagar -- and the SP won Behat and Saharanpur.Yadav has also urged the Congress to prefer "winnability" over the number of seats, suggesting that both parties jointly identify the strongest candidate for each constituency.

headline: Rahul, Akhilesh, Mamata to participate in ‘protect constitution’ march in MP capital
content: Senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, including Congress's Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, and Mamata Banerjee, will attend a 'Constitution Protection March' in Bhopal on December 12.The march is expected to draw between one lakh and 1.5 lakh people, according to the Madhya Pradesh Congress Committee (MPCC), which has sought the Lal Parade Ground in Bhopal as the venue for the rally, MP Congress media coordinator Abhinav Barolia told PTI.The Congress had earlier announced plans to launch a nationwide campaign in December against what it calls "vote theft" and to protect the Constitution, with Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra expected to lead the movement.Madhya Pradesh Congress president Jitu Patwari had said that safeguarding democracy and every citizen's right to vote remained the party's top priority.Also read: INDIA bloc races to consolidate Opposition against delimitation bill, may appeal to DMKBarolia said opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, Congress chief Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee are scheduled to attend the mega event.He said the march will begin from Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar's statue, where Rahul Gandhi will pay a floral tribute to the architect of the Constitution.The march will pass in front of the district court, the old jail, and the control room before reaching Lal Parade Ground, where a rally will be organised.Congress media department chairman Mukesh Nayak said the party was awaiting the administration's decision on the venue.He expressed apprehension that obstacles could be created for the Bhopal event, as allegedly happened in Indore in connection with Rahul Gandhi's function. He said repeated uncertainty over the venue would affect preparations.Also read: Congress wants Akhilesh as UP CM but seeks ‘more space’ in seat-sharing deal: Imran MasoodNayak said the Congress needed the ground at least seven days before the rally to make arrangements for domes, sound systems, barricades and other infrastructure.The Congress has urged the administration to make the venue available in advance so that preparations can be completed in time.A Congress delegation, including Nayak and other office-bearers, met Additional Commissioner of Police Monika Shukla on Friday and submitted a memorandum seeking permission for the venue.Nayak said Shukla informed the delegation that the permission process involved coordination with the traffic department and the Seventh Battalion.He said the application would be forwarded to the battalion through police headquarters as per procedure, and the delegation would be informed about the decision on Saturday or Sunday.

headline: EC hikes honorarium for SIR tribunal judges
content: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday enhanced the honorarium payable to judges of tribunals hearing appeals against inclusions and exclusions made in West Bengal’s electoral roll during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. With this, one of the key grievances aired by the tribunals and endorsed by a committee led by chief justice of the Calcutta High Court, has been resolved.All former high court judges assigned to SIR tribunals shall now receive a monthly honorarium of Rs 2.5 lakh, while a judge who has been a former Chief Justice of a High Court would be paid Rs 10,000 over and above this amount. The revised honorarium would be effective from Nov 20, 2026.Also Read| No change in LS strength, 25-year seat protection: INDIA bloc's demands on delimitationAs per the original EC order dated April 7, 2026, honorarium was payable to the tribunal judges on a weekly basis: Rs 1.5 lakh to former HC judges and Rs 1.6 lakh to former HC chief justice for base two weeks and Rs 25,000 per week thereafter.The Supreme Court had on Nov 23 directed EC to increase the number of tribunals. The higher honorarium will serve as an incentive for other ex-judges to sign up for the additional tribunals, said an officer.The apex court had earlier issued a directive for addressing the SIR tribunals’ administrative and infrastructure bottlenecks, to expedite the disposal of appeals. An internal committee of the Calcutta HC recently recommended the hiked compensation for the tribunals judges, communicated to EC by the HC registrar general on Nov 20, which the commission accepted in toto.Sources in the poll panel told TOI that almost all the grievances and issues raised by the tribunal judges have been addressed by EC. These include tweaking the SIR tribunals portal to enable the judges to login and issue orders with their digital signature certificate, allowing additional documents to be uploaded on the portal, and enabling judges to save the order as draft and edit it before issuing the final order, etc. Also, the judges have been allowed to work from alternative sites -- rather than the assigned office in Joka -- including their home or a place closer to their home. The staffing issues have also been suitably addressed.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Stalin-led DMK backs Centre on delimitation, says core demands included in proposed bill
content: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday said that it will support the delimitation bill proposed by the Centre saying that core demands of the party were included in the proposed bill. Senior DMK leader and former union minister A Raja said the decision was taken after deliberations during a key party meeting of MPs chaired by DMK chief MK Stalin.Track live updates on delimitation billThe decision was announced after the MPs meeting chaired by party chief MK Stalin held at Anna Arivalayam, the party headquarters in Chennai. Earlier on Friday, Stalin had said that the party would not compromise on the state’s share of parliamentary representation.Stalin said the proposed bill has accepted the ‘fair delimitation’ demands put forth by his party. “One must pause and think without getting carried away about what would happen if we were to miss out on this Delimitation Bill, which provides a 50 per cent increase in constituencies for all states based strictly on the 1971 population,” he said. Stalin had earlier reiterated two key demands – that Tamil Nadu’s share of Lok Sabha seats remain at 7.18% even if the total number of constituencies is increased, and that the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, based on the 1971 Census, be frozen for another 25 years. Following the meeting on Saturday, Raja said that the DMK maintained consistency in ensuring Tamil Nadu's 7.18 per cent Lok Sabha share remained unaffected. The southern state's share is now set to increase to 7.21 per cent.Also read: ‘Will remove every hurdle to women’s reservation’: PM Modi on women’s quota bill“We have passed a resolution that the DMK will extend its support to the current proposal—which is about to be tabled—to increase seats by 50 percent across all states. This is not a decision made today; while the DMK was in power, MK Stalin had already passed a resolution in the Legislative Assembly. In line with the decision taken in that Assembly resolution, we have taken this decision," Raja said.Earlier, leaders of the DMK, which has 22 members in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha, had indicated that they might back the bill if written assurances of a proportional increase in the state’s Lok Sabha strength were given.He noted that during the previous delimitation process in 1971, Tamil Nadu's share was 7.18 percent which was ‘allocated in a manner that did not harm the culture and civilisation of an India comprising diverse languages and diverse states.’Also read: 50% more seats, bigger state assemblies: Five changes in the new delimitation billsAdding that the same practice must continue, Raja took a dig at the Congress and said, “That exact same limit must continue; even those who were in that alliance, including the Congress party, merely said 'we want to have fair delimitation.' Nowhere did anyone suggest any new strategy back then other than the phrase 'fair delimitation' or ‘just constituency reorganization’.”He also sought to address the buzz that the DMK has broken ranks with the INDIA bloc to back the delimitation bill and said that the decision was taken with everyone, including the Congress, in consensus.“Today, we have taken this decision in alignment with everyone who was part of that earlier consensus—including the Congress party and all INDIA Bloc party leaders—and in accordance with the decisions taken at the all-India level, both inside and outside Parliament,” Raja said.
