headline: Karnataka govt issues show-cause notice to Indian Oil: What ethanol measurement discrepancies did it find?
content: The Karnataka government has issued a show-cause notice to Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) after inspections at its Devanagonthi terminal near Bengaluru found discrepancies in the measurement of ethanol and motor gasoline, PTI reported.An inspection conducted by the state's Legal Metrology Department on November 25 found that one of the mass flow meters was delivering 14 litres more ethanol for every 3,000 litres recorded. The same meter also showed a short delivery of four to six litres of motor gasoline for every 3,000 litres measured, according to the government notice.A second ethanol mass flow meter was found to be delivering three litres more than the recorded quantity for every 3,000 litres, the notice said.Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad said the department had begun inspecting terminals operated by oil marketing companies (OMCs) following allegations of ethanol blending in petrol beyond the prescribed E20 limit."After the Karnataka Government exposed over-blending of ethanol in petrol beyond the prescribed E20 limit, our Legal Metrology Department has begun inspecting Oil Marketing Company (OMC) terminals, where the blending is carried out," Arshad said in a Facebook post on Friday.He added that the inspection findings exceeded permissible limits and that a notice had been issued under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, PTI reported.What has Karnataka asked Indian Oil to do?The notice, addressed to the deputy general manager and terminal in-charge of IOCL's Devanagonthi facility, seeks an explanation for the measurement discrepancies. The company has also been asked to provide details of the latest calibration and maintenance of the equipment, along with the corrective steps taken to ensure compliance.IOCL has been given seven days from the receipt of the notice to submit its written response, along with verification certificates and calibration and maintenance records.The department has also directed the company to stop using the concerned measuring systems for commercial transactions until their accuracy and compliance with statutory requirements are established.Failure to provide a satisfactory explanation could lead to further legal and departmental action, the notice said.Why is Karnataka scrutinising ethanol blending in petrol?The latest action comes amid a dispute between the Karnataka government and public sector oil marketing companies over allegations that petrol supplied in the state contains ethanol beyond the prescribed 20% limit under the E20 programme.On November 6, Arshad alleged that petrol supplied by major OMCs contained ethanol above the permitted limit. Tests conducted on samples collected from seven districts reportedly found ethanol concentrations of up to 31.2% in IOCL petrol and 30.5% in Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) petrol.However, IOCL, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and HPCL rejected the allegations in a joint statement issued the same day. The companies said the findings were not based on tests conducted in accordance with prescribed statutory and technical procedures.They maintained that the E20 petrol supplied by them complied with the Bureau of Indian Standards specification IS 17021.On November 9, Arshad reiterated that the state government stood by its findings and challenged the oil marketing companies to explain the ethanol content detected in 63 samples collected from petrol pumps across Karnataka.

headline: Haryana amends TDR policy, changes land valuation formula and usage norms
content: Haryana has amended its policy for the grant and utilisation of Transferable Development Rights (TDR), changing how notional land is calculated and where the certificates can be used. The Town and Country Planning Department issued the amendment on Friday, in continuation of the policy first notified on November 16, 2021.The order, issued by Additional Chief Secretary Anurag Agarwal to the Director General, Town and Country Planning, was framed under the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975. It follows approval by the Council of Ministers at its meeting on November 3, 2026.Under the revised clause, notional land for which a TDR certificate is issued will be worked out by multiplying a Land Rate Index, based on the weighted average collector rate for the surrendered land on the date of application, by the area surrendered to the government in acres and by a Land Use Index.The collector rate notified by the Deputy Commissioner concerned and prevailing on the date of application will apply, irrespective of when the certificate is eventually used.The amendment protects certificates already issued, which cannot be amended or modified to claim the benefit of the new index. The new formula will also not apply to pending applications where in-principle approval for grant has already been given.For utilisation, the clause has been changed so that the notional land of the receiving site is calculated by taking the notional land of the TDR certificate and applying a Land Rate Index based on the weighted average collector rate for the receiving site, as on the date of the application on which the certificate was granted.This formula will also govern all pending applications for a utilisation certificate where no permission, including in-principle approval, has been given.The amendment also rewrites two general conditions. A TDR certificate issued in a specific development plan will be valid for use either in the same development plan or in any lower-potential development plan in the state. Every TDR certificate will carry a floor area ratio (FAR) of 2.0.What is TDR?Transferable Development Rights are a planning tool that lets a landowner who gives up land to the government, typically for public purposes such as roads or other infrastructure, receive development rights in return instead of cash compensation. These rights are issued as a certificate and measured as "notional land".The holder can use them on another eligible site, usually to build more than would otherwise be allowed, and in many schemes can transfer them to another party. The Land Rate Index in the amended formulas links the value of the land given up, and of the site where the rights are used, to the collector rates notified for each area. FAR is the ratio of total built-up floor area to plot area and so determines how much can be built on a site.

headline: ‘Maharashtra will not forgive’: Sanjay Raut warns NCP (SP) over delimitation bill
content: The Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) [NCP (SP)] MPs’ decision to back the Centre on the delimitation bill has opened a rift in the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA). In an interview with HT, Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut called the move a betrayal of Maharashtra. He said NCP (SP) should first apologise to Anil Deshmukh and Nawab Malik, and that Sharad Pawar is too unwell to take any decision. He also alleged that MPs are being bought at a “national horse-trading stock exchange”.Q. NCP (SP) MPs won as part of the MVA, and now they appear set to back the Centre. Is this a betrayal of the allianceYou have eight MPs, and they were elected as part of the Maha Vikas Aghadi. The Congress and the Shiv Sena are in that alliance. The BJP played no part in getting you elected, and in five of those eight seats we defeated BJP candidates. If you now take a one-sided decision and stand with the government, I don’t think the people of Maharashtra will tolerate it. Amit Shah and Modi broke Sharad Pawar’s party and fractured his family. Going and falling at their feet amounts to pawning your self-respect. If you are going that way to help the BJP, then the party must first apologise to Anil Deshmukh, who went to jail because of Amit Shah. It must apologise to Nawab Malik. He was a senior leader then, and it must apologise to him. Both of them fought against the tendencies of Amit Shah and Modi, and both had to go to jail. If some people today join hands with the BJP like this for power, Maharashtra will not remain Maharashtra.For some time now, Modi and Shah have been working to bring Maharashtra down. Strengthening their hands is treachery against Maharashtra and against the Marathi manoos, and we will not tolerate it.Q. NCP (SP) leaders say the party will split if they don’t fall in line. Have you spoken to Supriya Sule? And what is behind your allegation that MPs are being bought?No. Their argument is that otherwise the party will split. Our position is: what matters more, the party or the country? Our party was split too. Seven of our MPs were taken away to get support for this same delimitation. Did we go and fall at Amit Shah’s feet, or Narendra Modi’s? No. We kept fighting, and we are still fighting. MLAs and MPs will come and go, and parties will split and rise again. What matters is the country, Maharashtra and the ideology. Who are you trying to scare with talk of the party splitting? If you think it will split, then resign. You were elected from the MVA.I can tell you that the going rate right now for MPs who vote for this bill is in tens of crore. If anyone takes that money and votes against Maharashtra or against the country, then until now there were slogans of “50 khoke”, and now there will be slogans of “ 150 khoke” against you. NCP MPs should introspect and vote according to their conscience. If they vote with Modi and Shah, not one of them will get re-elected. I am not saying with the government. A vote for this is a vote against Maharashtra.We will raise a storm in Maharashtra over this delimitation commission. What kind of delimitation is this? BJP people are out-and-out rogues. They are traders who have turned the country’s politics into a business, and all our people in Maharashtra have fallen into their clutches. Just let them vote with Modi and Shah, and then they will find out what Maharashtra is.It was the MVA that got Sharad Pawar elected to the Rajya Sabha. Many people opposed it. Supriya Sule knows that I took the initiative. If you now take a stand against Maharashtra, Maharashtra will not forgive you. Don’t bother giving explanations.Then there are those leaders who keep coming before the mic saying “Shahu, Phule, Ambedkar”. You have no right to take the names of Shahu, Phule, Ambedkar or Yashwantrao Chavan. Don’t go to the Sangam and lay wreaths for Yashwantrao on his birth and death anniversaries. The Marathi manoos of this state will not tolerate this betrayal of Maharashtra.MPs have been sold at ₹ 150 crore. I am saying this with full responsibility. As I said yesterday, Amit Shah has set up a National Horse-Trading Stock Exchange, and their shares are currently trading at tens of crore. MPs are being sold. That is this country’s misfortune and Maharashtra’s.Q. Is Sharad Pawar himself on board with backing the BJP?I know Sharad Pawar’s health is poor, so I won’t say much. At this moment Pawar saheb is not in a physical or mental condition to take any decision. That is why it was his colleagues’ responsibility to stand firm and fight. Of the eight MPs, I know that three or four do not want to go with this bill. I can name them.Q. If NCP (SP) MPs back the bill, can they still sit at the INDIA bloc table?I don’t know. With what face will they go? The INDIA bloc and the MVA gave you respect, prestige and everything else. If you now back Amit Shah and Narendra Modi, the enemies of Maharashtra, and take a one-sided stand against your allies, you will have no place in the BJP and no place in the MVA or the INDIA bloc either.Over the past 60 years, Sharad Pawar made a towering leap in politics and public life. It looks like his colleagues have destroyed all of that within his own lifetime. They must make one thing clear. I am not talking about supporting the BJP; I am talking about the decision to support Amit Shah, who is Maharashtra’s enemy. Does Sharad Pawar consent to that decision? They should say so.Q. Congress state LoP Vijay Wadettiwar says backstabbing allies is part of Sharad Pawar’s and the NCP’s history. Do you agree?I won’t speak on that, and I won’t use that kind of language. Sharad Pawar’s health is very poor and he is not well. As I said yesterday, at this moment he is not in a physical or mental condition to take any decision. I know that, so I will not make any such comment.But Pawar saheb’s ideology is the ideology of Yashwantrao Chavan and of Phule, Shahu and Ambedkar. His colleagues had the responsibility to protect it and carry it forward, and I feel they have made a mess of it. He raised these colleagues, took them to the highest posts and gave them power. Perhaps they are now hungry for power, and they have ruined his ideas and his positions. One can disagree with Sharad Pawar’s positions, but for some time now he had been consistently fighting Modi, Shah and communal forces alongside us. I don’t think he ever directly joined hands with them.Supriya Sule, Jayant Patil and their MPs had a duty here. You were elected on that ideology. Did Amit Shah or Modi come to campaign for you? No. Uddhav Thackeray came, Congress leaders came, Rahul Gandhi came, Sharad Pawar came. The people of Maharashtra voted for you so that Modi and Shah would be defeated. Going and sitting at their feet now is a blow to Maharashtra’s self-respect. I don’t know how much Amit Shah will gain from this, though he will gain because of you. But Maharashtra will lose. Will the people of the state trust this party, the NCP formed under Sharad Pawar’s leadership, in future?Q. Are some Congress MPs also likely to back the bill?No chance, I don’t think so. No major party has openly given its support so far. NCP (SP)’s support to this anti-Maharashtra, anti-national bill has come to light, and it is wrong. Wrong is wrong, and it cannot be justified. If anyone offers explanations, the people will turn their backs on you, because they don’t like this.In most of these constituencies the Shiv Sena has influence. Take the Shirur Lok Sabha seat: you can’t win there without the Shiv Sena. I want to tell Amol Kolhe to watch how we fight and see how you win those seats. There are many such constituencies, Solapur and Madha among them. We have strength everywhere, we will fight in every seat and we will show what Maharashtra is. You cannot betray people like this. Our party was split too, and we did not surrender. The country matters more than a party splitting. The Shiv Sena has always sacrificed for the nation and for dharma.Q. With Shinde’s ‘Operation Tiger’ under way, your own MPs could be poached, and you are down to a handful. Don’t the numbers worry you?Numbers? Does he know 3.5 or 4.5? Has he ever sat a maths paper? He knows only one figure: counting money. They bought people. Our people too were sold for ₹50 crore. MPs left and MLAs left. Did the party stop? It is still going and it will move ahead. And we will draw our last breath only after burying you completely in the dirt.Q. On protests against the delimitation exercise / Gyanesh KumarMaharashtra has seen the most protests against this. Gyanesh Kumar was made the head of this commission. Look, India is a great country. It has seen the Mahabharata and the Ramayana, and it has seen many struggles: the first, second and third phases of the freedom struggle, and the movement led by Jayaprakash Narayan. Now we have launched one more struggle. Who is Gyanesh Kumar? Did he fall from the sky? Did Amit Shah or Modi fall from the sky? Even lord Ram and lord Krishna came and went, so who are these people?The 106 martyrs did not give their lives so that Mumbai could be laid at Amit Shah’s feet. They gave their lives so that Mumbai would stay in Maharashtra and the Marathi manoos could live with self-respect. People have forgotten that now.

headline: Punjab and Haryana High Court flags delay in infrastructure expansion plan, seeks urgent action
content: Taking serious note of the delay in implementing the holistic development plan for the Punjab and Haryana High Court, a Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Sanjiv Berry observed that the administration of justice could suffer unless the project was executed at the earliest.The Bench requested the Additional Solicitor General of India to personally meet the Union Home Secretary and impress upon the authorities concerned the need to expedite the matter.During Friday’s hearing, the court was informed that a meeting chaired by the Union Home Secretary had discussed approval of the plan. According to the minutes, the Chandigarh Administration will share the proposal with the Punjab and Haryana Governments, including details of cost sharing among stakeholders, seek their views, obtain the High Court’s opinion and convene another meeting to finalise future development.The Bench noted that the petition had been pending for some time and highlighted severe infrastructure constraints affecting the court’s functioning. It pointed out that although the High Court has a sanctioned strength of 85 judges, the number of courtrooms is inadequate. Space for Bar offices and parking facilities is also insufficient, making additional infrastructure an urgent necessity.The court further observed that the High Court forms part of the Capitol Complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, which places restrictions on development. Any expansion must remain consistent with the original vision of architect Le Corbusier.Referring to the proposed plan, the Bench said it had been conceived by the High Court and subsequently processed by the UT Administration. It therefore, found little need for the Administration to seek the High Court’s views again. Issues relating to cost sharing, it said, could be addressed at the appropriate stage.The Bench observed: “Approval of preliminary stimulants, therefore, mark the commencement of the project itself. We therefore, expect officials concerned of the Union Government, who are seized of the matter, to examine the issue with the requisite sensitivity so as to ensure that the required infrastructure is made available to the court at the earliest possible. We hope and trust that the authorities will give due priority to the imminent concerns of the courts, as noticed above.”

headline: New quota bill proposes 50 per cent increase in seats, freezes delimitation till 2051; April bill left both open
content: New Delhi, The Constitution Bill, 2026, slated for introduction in Parliament next week, proposes a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats and a freeze on delimitation until 2051 to facilitate the implementation of women's reservation.The proposed legislation marks a significant departure from the Constitution Bill, introduced in April, which had sought to facilitate the implementation of women's reservation but provided neither for an increase in the number of seats nor for an extension of the delimitation freeze.The bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha for want of the required two-thirds majority. The changes come against the backdrop of strong opposition from southern states, led by the DMK, to the earlier delimitation proposal. The party argued that states which had successfully controlled population growth should not be penalised through a reduction in their relative representation in Parliament.The DMK has maintained that Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18 per cent share in the Lok Sabha should not be reduced in any expansion of the House. It has also insisted that the relative proportion of parliamentary representation among states, based on the 1971 Census, should remain protected for another 25 years.The new bill retains the 1971 Census as the basis for allocating Lok Sabha seats among states, while providing for the redrawing of constituencies within states based on the latest published census figures.It proposes raising the maximum strength of state assemblies from 500 to 650 and the Lok Sabha ceiling to 850, comprising 815 seats for states and 35 for Union Territories.Unlike the April bill, the latest proposal provides for a uniform 50 per cent increase in seats across states and Union Territories, while extending the freeze on inter-state allocation until 2051. This is intended to address concerns that population-based delimitation could alter the existing balance of representation between states.The DMK's support has emerged as an important factor in the government's efforts to secure the special majority required for passage of the constitutional amendment.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 5 youths from Himachal’s Mandi allege job fraud, say 8 companions stranded in Russia
content: Five youths from Himachal Pradesh's Mandi district have alleged that they were duped by agents who promised them lucrative jobs in Russia but sent them on tourist visas and made them do menial work.They have approached the district administration for help in bringing back eight of their companions who are allegedly still stranded in the country. The affected youths, including Manohar Lal, met Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Mandi Priyanshu Khati and narrated their ordeal.According to the victims, an agent from Sundernagar, in collaboration with his associate from Baijnath, allegedly promised them employment in a company in Russia with attractive salaries.Around 13 people, including Sanju Lal, Jagdish, Duni Chand and Nokhu Ram, were reportedly approached with assurances of overseas employment. In exchange, the agents allegedly collected substantial amounts of money from the aspirants.The youths claimed that they were promised proper employment arrangements and work visas before being sent abroad. However, upon reaching Russia, they allegedly found themselves in a completely different situation from what had been promised.According to their account, they were handed over to a Pakistani national after arriving in Russia. Instead of being provided employment at the warehouse or company where they had been assured jobs, they were allegedly made to wash dishes and work in a stable.The victims alleged that the agents had misled them by arranging tourist visas instead of work visas, leaving them vulnerable and without the promised employment opportunities. They said the circumstances in Russia were far different from what they had been told before departure.After realising that they had been cheated and were not receiving the promised jobs, five youths managed to return to India. However, they claimed that eight of their companions were still in Russia and facing difficulties.The victims have appealed to the district administration to intervene and facilitate the safe return of their stranded companions. They have also sought strict action against the agents allegedly involved in the fraud, demanding that those responsible be held accountable for exploiting young people seeking employment opportunities abroad.ADC Priyanshu Khati told The Tribune that the police had been directed to investigate the matter and take necessary action against the accused.

headline: Tata Sons files caveats in Bombay HC, SC ahead of November 30 board meet
content: Even after the Bombay High Court had wrapped up the Tata Trusts versus Tata Sons hearing for the day on Friday, allowing the Tata Sons board meeting to go on as scheduled on November 30, lawyers for the holding company of the conglomerate were working on a caveat. ALSO READ: Tata Sons listing, restructuring, EGM on November 30 board meet plan Tata Sons is learnt to have filed a late evening caveat in the division bench of the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court on November 27. The caveat is a precautionary step to ensure that the company is heard before any verdict is passed on an appeal challenging the Bombay High Court’s order. ALSO READ: Tata Sons should choose its future rather than face a forced listing In a single-bench order on Friday, Justice Abhay Ahuja of the Bombay High Court refused to grant any interim relief to Tata Trusts, which holds 66 per cent in Tata Sons, while setting January 21, 2027, as the next date of hearing. This means that despite the Tata Sons board meeting proceeding on November 30 without any legal restraint, any board resolution will be subject to the final court order. ALSO READ: Inside the Tata Sons power struggle: The rules, the rift and the road ahead Two entities of the Tata Trusts — Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and RD Tata Trust — had moved court on Thursday against Tata Sons and its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman for a third term. The Tata Trusts suit also sought a restraint on the November 30 board meeting agenda that includes a proposed listing of Tata Sons. Citing Section 121 of the Articles of Association (AoA) of Tata Sons, the petition asked the court to prevent a casting vote by Chandrasekaran or any other director in case of a tie, as had transpired during the contentious September 17 board meeting. Noel Tata, Tata Trusts chairman and nominee director on Tata Sons board, had voted against Chandrasekaran’s third term while Venu Srinivasan, the other nominee director, had voted in favour of the proposal on September 17, resulting in a tie, forcing a casting vote from acting chairman Harish Manwani. All board members, other than Noel Tata, backed the proposal. The development put a question mark on the definition of the affirmative vote in relation to Section 121, with varied legal interpretations. Section 121 provides for additional voting requirement by nominee directors appointed by Tata Trusts as well as a casting vote by the chairman in case of a tie. Tata Trusts’ argument is that when the two nominee directors are split in their views, there is no affirmative majority and that a casting vote can’t be used in such a scenario. Tata Sons has maintained that the chairman can exercise a casting vote when the Trusts nominee votes are split.

headline: Why an academician’s ego is a hidden threat within higher education
content: There is a devil that rarely appears in university policy documents, faculty appraisal forms, or accreditation reports. It does not show up in research metrics, citation counts, or institutional rankings. Yet it can quietly destroy departments, careers, collaborations and even the quality of science itself. This devil is ego. Damage caused Every university department has tales of legendary battles between academics. Arguments over who should lead a project, whose name should appear first on a paper, who should chair a committee, whose research deserves funding, and who was invited to speak at a conference can slowly turn colleagues into adversaries. Departments that once functioned as intellectual communities can become divided into “clans” united less by scholarship than by loyalty to personalities. The tragedy is that the damage rarely ends with the academics involved. Promising academic careers have ended because of ego clashes. Students have suffered because supervisors refused to cooperate. Research collaborations have collapsed because scientists could not agree on credit. Sometimes, outstanding science does not see the light of day because researchers valued recognition more than discovery. Academic life rewards achievement. We compete for grants, publications, positions, awards, citations, and recognition. A certain amount of ambition, confidence, and intellectual independence is necessary. But, somewhere, healthy academic confidence becomes an inflated sense of self. A recent study, The Hidden Threat in Schools: Understanding and Managing Toxic Teacher Behaviors, offers a broad and useful warning for academia. Based on the views of 12 school principals in Türkiye, the study found that toxic behaviours could undermine organisational climate, teacher collaboration, trust, and motivation. Identified behaviours included destructive criticism, selfishness, dominance, gossip, resistance to change, cliquing, jealousy, and unwillingness to cooperate. Although the study focuses on schools rather than universities, its central message is highly relevant: when destructive individual behaviour becomes embedded in an educational institution, it can contaminate the culture around it. Consequences The most visible consequence is factionalism. One group supports Professor A. Another supports Professor B. A new faculty member quickly learns which camp to join. Meetings become political. Junior academics discover that intellectual merit alone may not always determine opportunities; relationships and loyalties can matter just as much. The study found that constant criticism and complaints could weaken collaboration and solidarity and foster factionalism, weakening the institutional structure. Gossip also damaged internal cooperation. Anyone who has spent enough time in academia will recognise the pattern. Once factions emerge, people can interpret every decision through the lens of allegiance. A legitimate academic disagreement becomes evidence of hostility. A colleague’s success is perceived as a threat. A new appointment becomes a victory for one camp and a defeat for another. Slowly, the institution loses its ability to think collectively. Perhaps the most disturbing consequence is what it does to students. A student should never have to become a diplomat between professors. Yet they find themselves caught between supervisors who refuse to communicate, laboratories that will not share facilities, departments fighting over ownership of projects, or faculty members competing for control over a student’s research. What can be done The antidote is not simply telling academics to “be humble”. Humility has to become a professional practice. Here are some ways to build humility First, remain a student. Read beyond your specialisation. Attend talks where you are not the expert. Ask questions of younger colleagues. Allow students to teach you. Second, find a larger purpose. When the purpose becomes better science, better students, and solving problems that matter, personal glory becomes less important. Third, build large teams. Collaboration is an antidote to academic narcissism. Shared credit and transparent recognition make it harder for individual egos to dominate. Fourth, cultivate people who can challenge you. The most dangerous professional environment is one in which everyone is afraid to disagree with you. Fifth, find role models. Look at accomplished scientists whose greatness is accompanied by generosity. Their real legacy is often visible not merely in their publications, but in the people they have inspired and mentored. Perhaps the greatest battle an academic will ever fight is not against a rival, a reviewer or a competing theory, but against the ego within. Publications will fade, citations will be forgotten, awards will gather dust, and positions will eventually be handed to someone else. What remains is the knowledge we created, the students we inspired, the colleagues we lifted, and the scientific possibilities we opened for others. A 12-point ego test Perhaps the first step is to recognise it in ourselves. Our academic ego may be spiralling out of control when we: Stop reading and learning from other people’s research. Stop seeking inputs from colleagues and students. Treat criticism as a personal attack. Stop citing others and increasingly make papers about our own work. Become unavailable to students and junior colleagues seeking advice. Attend conferences only when given a speaking role. Give disproportionately negative peer reviews, particularly when our work is not cited. Expect every grant to be funded and every manuscript to be accepted. Expect to be first or senior author on almost every paper. Become resentful when overlooked for awards or prizes. Offer authoritative opinions even outside our expertise. Become unable to leave the stage, refuse to retire gracefully or fail to mentor successors. Views are personal The writer is adjunct faculty at the National Institute of Advanced Studies, IISc campus, Bengaluru, and Dean -Academic Affairs, Garden City University, Bengaluru. headline: DMK backs 50% Lok Sabha seat increase, seeks to protect Tamil Nadu's share
content: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) MP A Raja on Saturday said the party has decided to support the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states, while reiterating that Tamil Nadu's existing share of representation in the Lok Sabha must remain protected amid the Centre's proposed delimitation exercise.Speaking to ANI after the DMK meeting, Raja said the party's consistent demand had been that Tamil Nadu's 7.18 per cent share in the Lok Sabha should not be altered, adding that the proposed arrangement appeared to preserve the state's representation."Our consistent demand is that the share of 7.18% (seat share in Lok Sabha) should not be altered. Now it is being maintained. Of course, procedural issues are there; we will address them. If necessary, we will give an amendment," he said.Addressing a press conference in Chennai, the DMK leader said the party had maintained a consistent position on protecting Tamil Nadu's representation, irrespective of whether it was in power or in the Opposition and whether it was part of an alliance or not.He said the party's position followed discussions involving political parties and Chief Ministers from different states at a Joint Action Committee meeting convened in Chennai by former Chief Minister and DMK president M. K. Stalin."During the last delimitation process, during the restructuring, Tamil Nadu's share was 7.18. In India, which consists of various states with various nationalities, various languages, and various cultures, that share was carried out the last time during Indira Gandhi's period in 1971 without causing harm to the culture and civilisation of each linguistic state," Raja said.He maintained that retaining the same share was central to the idea of fair delimitation and said the DMK had not deviated from this demand."That the same share should continue is what 'fair delimitation' means, and all parties in that alliance, including the Congress party, [said], 'We wanted to have a fair delimitation.' Nowhere, apart from the term 'fair delimitation'--apart from fair constituency delimitation--did anyone propose any new formula that day," he said.Raja also rejected allegations that the DMK had changed its position after moving away from the INDIA bloc, calling such claims politically improper."So far as DMK is concerned, we maintained full consistency when we were in power, and we were out of power. So notwithstanding the political entity, notwithstanding the political power, we maintained our consistency that the share of Tamil Nadu, 7.18, should not be affected," he said.Explaining the party's assessment of the proposed arrangement, Raja said Tamil Nadu had lost two seats during the 1971 delimitation exercise, but the current proposal did not entail a similar reduction. He said the state's share had instead reached 7.21 per cent from 7.18 per cent.He further said the party had examined the proposed legislation with legal experts and lawyers and that its leadership had authorised it to consult other parties and discuss possible amendments with the government."Beyond this number, we agree with the number 59. Beyond that, regarding the Delimitation Commission, other processes, and wherever else there are difficulties, wherever there is apprehension, wherever we have reservations, we asked if we can bring amendments in Parliament if needed," he said.Raja added that the party would raise its concerns in Parliament and seek changes to specific clauses if required. He also said the proposed arrangement would retain the existing state-wise representation ratio for another 25 years.The DMK's position is significant as the party has 22 MPs in the Lok Sabha and its support could influence the outcome of the proposed legislation. The party had earlier demanded that Tamil Nadu's 7.18 per cent share in the Lok Sabha remain unchanged and that the existing proportion of representation among states, based on the 1971 Census, be retained for another 25 years.The Union Cabinet has cleared a legislative package to facilitate delimitation and the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. The Centre is set to introduce the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, during the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.The proposed legislation provides for a 50 per cent increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and Union Territory, as well as the total number of seats in State Assemblies. If passed, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha would increase to 850, while that of State Assemblies would rise to 650.The Centre's proposal links the implementation of women's reservation, provided for under the 106th Constitutional Amendment in 2023, with the fresh delimitation exercise, with the government aiming to complete the process before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.The Opposition has supported women's reservation but objected to linking its implementation with delimitation. It has also demanded the use of the latest Census data instead of the 2011 figures. The Centre has proposed using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies and determining SC/ST-reserved seats, while retaining the 1971 population basis for state-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats until 2051.

headline: HC orders Hisar tech university to release 11-year-old sealed seniority list of Assistants
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology, Hisar, to immediately release the complete seniority list of Assistants that it has kept under a sealed cover for more than 11 years. The Bench held that selectively withholding the list without any intelligible basis was prima facie violative of their fundamental rights.“By withholding the seniority list without any lawful ground, the respondents have kept the petitioners from being considered for promotion for over a decade and have thereby, prima facie, infringed their fundamental right,” Justice Harpreet Singh Brar observed.The order is significant as the petitioners, promoted as Assistants in October 2004, had remained on the same post for over 22 years, with their consideration for further promotion held up in the absence of a final seniority list.Justice Brar found that the University had failed to honour its statement before the High Court in 2014 that the revised seniority list was likely to be finalised, as well as a subsequent Division Bench direction requiring its finalisation within four months. Although a committee had prepared the complete list within the stipulated period, the then Vice-Chancellor ordered that only the first eight names be displayed and the remaining portion be kept sealed.“Such conduct does not appear to be in keeping either with the statement made on behalf of the respondent-University before this Court or with the direction issued by the Division Bench of this Court,” Justice Brar observed.The court directed the varsity to release the complete seniority list prepared by the committee in pursuance of the Division Bench judgment dated May 14, 2015, subject to the final outcome of a writ petition filed way back in 2005. “In respect of the employees whose promotion falls due on the basis of the said list, the respondents shall act in accordance with law,” Justice Brar ordered.The directions by Justice Brar came on a petition filed against Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology and other respondents by Manju Gandhi and other employees through counsel Dhiraj Chawla. The Bench, during the course of hearing, was told that the petitioners were promoted as Assistants, now Assistant-cum-DEOs, on October 18, 2004. Their names figured in the tentative seniority list issued on January 3, 2013.Taking up the matter, Justice Brar observed that earlier writ petitions challenging the seniority list dated July 8, 2005, were dismissed on March 26, 2014, after the varsity counsel informed the court that the list had been recast through a tentative seniority list dated January 3, 2013, and that the same “was likely to be finalized”.A Division Bench in its decision dated May 14, 2015, on an appeal filed in the matter held “once such a statement had been made on behalf of the University, it was imperative upon it to honour the same”. It directed the Vice-Chancellor and Registrar to finalise the tentative list within four months, failing which the appellants would be at liberty to initiate contempt proceedings. Following the directions, the committee held meetings in November 2015, and prepared the complete final seniority list.However, on November 19, 2015, just two days before the deadline expired, the then Vice-Chancellor ordered that the list be displayed only up to the first eight names, it be shown to two appellants, for their satisfaction and the list be sealed “to avoid disharmony among the staff”.Finding the selective release arbitrary, Justice Brar observed: “The respondents have released the list for some officials and withheld it for others borne on the very same list, without disclosing any intelligible basis for such classification. Such cherry-picking is, on the face of it, violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India”.Rejecting the reasons for withholding the remaining names, the court noted that no stay order had been shown to have been passed. The varsity’s own advocate had expressed opinion on February 28, 2020, that there was no restraint order and the seniority list could be issued forthwith, subject to the outcome of the pending writ petitions.“The apprehension of disharmony among the staff is wholly extraneous to the determination of seniority, which is a matter of right governed by the applicable rules and principles. A seniority list is bound to leave some employees dissatisfied, and that is precisely why objections are invited and remedies are available to those aggrieved,” Justice Brar asserted. “The action of the respondents, therefore, seems to be arbitrary and based upon the whims and caprice of the authorities,” it observed.Explaining why the sealed-cover procedure could not be invoked in the present circumstances, Justice Brar referred to the Supreme Court's three-Judge Bench judgment explaining that the procedure was adopted when an employee due for promotion, increment or other service benefits was facing pending disciplinary or criminal proceedings, and the findings regarding entitlement were kept in a sealed cover until those proceedings concluded.Justice Brar directed the Registrar to file an affidavit specifically explaining three aspects: the statutory provisions or rules empowering the Vice-Chancellor to keep the seniority list sealed and release it in parts, along with justification; the reasons for not adhering to the University's statement before the High Court in 2014 and the Division Bench's direction in 2015; and the basis for releasing the names of only eight officials while withholding those of the remaining similarly situated employees. The matter will now come up on February 1, 2027.

headline: Gurgaon man's Rs 1.02 lakh health insurance claim rejected over 'missing documents'; consumer commission
content: GURGAON: A health insurance company cannot reject a medical reimbursement claim citing missing documents when the policyholder’s evidence of submitting the papers and responding to queries remains unrebutted, the Gurgaon consumer commission has ruled, holding the insurers guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed Oriental Insurance Company and its third-party administrator, Health Insurance TPA of India Ltd, to jointly and severally reimburse Rs 1,02,918 to Krishan Gopal, along with 9% interest from the date he filed the complaint on Nov 26, 2025, till payment.The commission also awarded Rs 30,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony, and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.Gopal had taken an Oriental Insurance Bank Saathi mediclaim policy with a sum insured of Rs 4 lakh for which he paid a premium of Rs 29,684. He underwent surgery for a urinary problem at Punshpanjali Hospital in Gurgaon in March 2025 and was admitted twice within a week. The treatment cost Rs 1,02,918.After submitting the claim along with the claim form, discharge summaries, bills, receipts, reports and other documents, he was asked by the insurer to respond to certain queries.Gopal told the commission that he had furnished the required clarifications but the company eventually rejected his claim on Oct 17, 2025, citing non-receipt of documents under a policy clause.The commission, headed by president Sanjeev Jindal and comprising members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur, observed that the complainant had specifically pleaded that he submitted the documents and responded to the insurer’s queries. His affidavit and supporting documents also corroborated his version.The insurer, however, failed to produce evidence to rebut the complainant’s submissions or establish that the required documents had not been received, the commission said.Oriental Insurance’s defence was struck off after it failed to file its written reply within the stipulated 45 days, while the TPA was proceeded against ex-parte for failing to appear despite service. Advocate Yathesht Vashisht appeared for Oriental Insurance, while Gopal argued his case himself.The commission directed the companies to comply within 45 days of uploading of the order. Failure to do so would attract 12% interest for the same period till realization, besides the possibility of execution proceedings and prosecution under the Consumer Protection Act.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. headline: 'Self-interest over national interest': Mayawati takes swipe at parties over delimitation, backs women's quota
content: NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Saturday welcomed the Centre's move to implement 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies but called for a separate quota for women from Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). She also took a swipe at parties over the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that those in power at the Centre prioritise their own interests over national interest.In a series of posts on X, Mayawati said the BSP had consistently supported women's reservation and welcomed the government's recent decision. However, she said providing a separate share for SC/ST women within the 33% quota would have made the move historic.She said women from these communities had faced exploitation, oppression and neglect for centuries and needed greater opportunities to participate in electoral politics.Taking aim at the proposed delimitation exercise, the BSP chief said allegations of political and electoral considerations influencing the process were not new. The Centre has proposed three bills providing for a 50% increase in the existing number of seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies."In fact, whichever party is in power at the centre tends, in most such cases, to care less about the interests of the country and its people and to give greater importance to its own interests and self-interest. This is no secret to anyone," Mayawati said.She also referred to concerns over the proposed increase in seats and the delimitation process, alleging that constituency limits could be determined to serve political and electoral interests.Mayawati urged voters not to be swayed by religious, caste-based or regional considerations while choosing their representatives.The BSP chief reiterated her party's support for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. She said the party had long demanded its early implementation.However, she said a separate reservation for SC/ST women within the proposed quota would have helped address their historical exclusion from electoral politics."This would have given them an opportunity to participate properly in the country's electoral politics, which is plagued by narrow-mindedness, casteism, money and muscle power, and to move forward a little," she said.Mayawati added that the Centre should consider the demand, calling it appropriate and just.What the Centre's bills proposeThe Centre's proposed legislation provides for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and Union Territory, as well as the total number of seats in state assemblies. If passed, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha would rise to 850, while state assemblies could have up to 650 members.The proposal links the implementation of women's reservation, provided for under the 106th Constitutional Amendment in 2023, with a fresh delimitation exercise. The government aims to complete the process before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.The Opposition has supported women's reservation but objected to linking its implementation with delimitation. It has also demanded that the exercise use the latest Census data instead of the 2011 figures.The Centre has proposed using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies and determining seats reserved for SC/ST communities, while retaining the 1971 population basis for state-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats until 2051.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: BJP, Akalis to hold first meeting after Punjab alliance; Kewal, Jakhar to meet Sukhbir today
content: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will hold their first formal meeting today since announcing their pre-poll alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections on Parkash Purab.It was a pleasure to welcome and host the senior leadership of the Bharatiya Janata Party — Punjab President S. @KewalDhillonPB, former President Shri @sunilkjakhar, former President Shri @AshwaniSBJP, and General Secretary Shri @anilsarinbjp — at lunch at my Chandigarh residence today.I am grateful to all of them for accepting my invitation and gracing the occasion.The Shiromani Akali Dal is committed to providing a pro-Punjabi government in the State in alliance with the BJP. We are already moving ahead in this regard and will soon come out with a joint action plan.Today’s meeting also discussed preparations for the December 8 conference to be held in Moga on the birth anniversary of former Chief Minister Sardar Parkash Singh Ji Badal, which will be attended by Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji and other senior leaders.— Sukhbir Singh Badal (@officeofssbadal) November 28, 2026Top sources confirmed to The Tribune that the BJP has deputed Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon and former state party president Sunil Jakhar to meet SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal.The meeting is scheduled to take place at Sukhbir Badal’s Sector 9 residence in Chandigarh.Sources said discussions would primarily focus on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s December 8 rally in Moga, including its planning and strategy. The leaders are also expected to hold preliminary discussions on seat-sharing arrangements between the two parties.The broad seat-sharing formula has already been worked out and is likely to be announced soon, The Tribune has learnt.Modi’s rally is being viewed as the formal launch of the BJP-SAD campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections in Punjab. The event assumes added significance as Moga was the venue where late SAD patriarch Parkash Singh Badal had announced the party’s alliance with the BJP in 1996.The outcome of Saturday’s meeting will be conveyed to the BJP’s central leadership, sources said.

headline: Election Commission revised SSR timeline for Bengal; clarifies on SIR appeals
content: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday further revised the schedule for special summary revision (SSR) of the electoral roll in West Bengal, with the draft roll now slated for publication on December 15 and the final roll on February 8, 2027.This is the second time that the SSR timeline for the state is being extended.As per the latest time-table, the polling station rationalisation would be complete by December 3. Claims and objections on the draft roll can be filed between December 15, 2026 and January 14, 2027, followed by their disposal latest by February 1, 2027.In yet another move, EC on Friday wrote to the West Bengal chief electoral officer (CEO), clarifying doubts relating to electors under adjudication by the judicial officers and tribunals appointed to hear appeals against SIR. Breaking up the cases in separate categories, EC clarified that cases of individuals marked 'under adjudication' in draft roll and still showing so as the judicial officers have not given their verdict, shall be referred to the electoral registration officer, who is the statutory authority, for appropriate decision. As for cases marked "under adjudication" that have been decided by the judicial officers but remain pending for e-signature, they may be treated as decided.No action is required regarding individuals who were deleted by judicial officers but have not filed any appeal with the SIR tribunals, said EC. As for individuals who were deleted by the judicial officers and filed appeals with the tribunals that are pending for a decision, these appeals should be prioritised in line with SC directions. EC specifically asked the EROs not to process any Form 6 applications submitted by the individuals until the tribunals give their decision.On what to do with appeals where the tribunal has decided to exclude the appellant from the roll, EC instructed that the said decision must be implemented.The above instructions, EC directed the CEO, may be brought to the notice of all concerned for necessary action and compliance.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
