headline: NBC pulls advertisement criticising US' Israel policy amid growing backlash | Hindustan Times
content: NBC has pulled a controversial advertisement criticising US financial aid to Israel after it aired during the network’s Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special. The ad received significant backlash from Jewish advocacy groups over media standards for politically charged advertising.The 30-second commercial, titled “Every Three Seconds,” was funded by the Institute for Middle East Understanding (IMEU) Policy Project.It contrasts a young American girl saving $400 to buy a bicycle with footage of a Palestinian girl using crutches amid destroyed buildings in Gaza. The narrator concludes, “Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to do this.”NBC confirmed it will no longer broadcast the advertisement. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr said in an X post, “NBC says they’re now pulling this ad, widely described as antisemitic, from the public airwaves and will no longer be broadcasting it.”Deadline reported that the network’s senior management had not reviewed the commercial before it aired and that NBCUniversal is evaluating its internal approval process to prevent similar situations. Ad sparks criticism from Jewish organisationsThe advertisement prompted immediate condemnation from several Jewish organisations. They argued that it unfairly portrayed Israel and echoed narratives promoted by Hamas.Anti-Defamation League (ADL) Chief Executive Jonathan Greenblatt described NBC’s decision to air the commercial as “indefensible.” B’nai B’rith International also criticised the network in a social media statement saying, “Shame on NBC.”The Israeli-American Council also condemned NBC, accusing the broadcaster of airing “anti-Israel propaganda” that pushes the Hamas narrative and said that it could fuel antisemitic hatred.According to Semafor, the IMEU Policy Project had planned to run the advertisement nationally during the Thanksgiving television audience. Network reviews approval processDeadline reported that NBC executives were unaware the advertisement would air until after the broadcast. The network has since decided it will not rebroadcast the commercial and is reviewing its advertising approval procedures.The IMEU Policy Project has defended its advocacy efforts. They argued that the advertisement highlights the humanitarian consequences of the war in Gaza and questions continued US military assistance to Israel.They wrote, “On Wednesday night, millions of Americans tuning into NBC had their living rooms lit up by the face of a beautiful nine-year-old Palestinian girl named Meral al-Babli. Meral’s leg was amputated after an Israeli bombing of her house in Gaza that also killed her mother and her grandmother. She is now one of the over 10,000 Palestinian children enduring life-altering injuries.”They added, “All of this is indisputable.”The campaign website noted that since 1948, the United States has provided Israel with more than $330 billion in inflation-adjusted aid. However, according to Jewish Insider, the Congressional Research Service's most recent estimate of US aid from 1946 to 2024 was roughly $298 billion, adjusted for inflation.In a statement they wrote, “[O]ur advertisement passed NBC’s stringent fact-checking requirements. We are disheartened to hear reports that NBC executives will no longer air our ad, which endorses a policy of ending taxpayer funding to Israel.”They added, “We hope, for the sake of NBC’s reputation, that these reports are not true.”

headline: Diljit Dosanjh in Mumbai: ‘In 2024, I was asked not to sing few songs; in 2026, there’s a bomb threat’
content: Actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh on Friday thanked fans for attending his Mumbai concert despite a bomb threat and said that their fearlessness gave him the courage to perform.Addressing fans at the Mahalaxmi Racecourse in South Mumbai, the singer talked about the challenges that he continues to face in his concerts.“When I performed in 2024, I felt I was being troubled quite a bit. I was asked not to sing this song or that song, and so on. But those were only small things. At this point in 2026, simply managing to hold my show is a cause for stress in itself.‘We will blow up Diljit with a bomb’, wow, wow, wow. If you people are not afraid, can I afford to be afraid? Hats off to all of you. Even if I were to take my heart out and place it before you, it would not be enough,” Dosanjh said to his fans midway through the concert.More than 500 Mumbai police personnel were deployed for the concert following a threat email warning of possible attacks on the venue and Metro stations, officials said earlier in the day.An email threatening blasts, grenade attacks and planting of IEDs at the mayor’s office, metro rail stations and Dosanjh’s concert was received on Thursday, the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 terror attacks.Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) teams have swept the venue, a police official said, adding that entry checks will be carried out across all five gates instead of three. Besides, private security personnel were also roped in to assist police, an official said.Dosanjh thanked the Mumbai Police for the adequate safety arrangements.“I know that as many people are here inside, there are that many people stranded outside. The police personnel are helpless too; they are checking everyone before allowing them in. My heartfelt thanks to the Mumbai Police,” he said.Expressing gratitude to his fans for refusing to bow down to intimidation, the 42-year-old singer said that the objective behind the threats was to intimidate concert goers and disrupt his events.“Their only objective is to ensure that people do not attend Diljit’s show, to frighten them, threaten them and stop them by any means possible.“I don’t know why this is happening to me, day after day. From my side, there is only love for you, even if you throw bombs,” Dosanjh said before reciting a couplet about the atmosphere of fear in cities and urging people to move towards the countryside.The concert began at around 8:00 PM and through a course of two hours, Dosanjh belted out several hit songs like ‘Clash’, ‘Hass Hass’, ‘Vibe’, ‘Pokito’, ‘Kinni Kinni’ and fan favourites like ‘Saanson ki Maala’, ‘Ikk Kudi’ and ‘Bhool Bhulaiyya’.The fans sang in unison and broke into bhangra and danced their hearts out. Dosanjh said his songs carried the fragrance of village life.“The songs I sing are about villages, and I come from a village myself. Even if you do not understand my songs, you will surely sense the fragrance of the soil,” he said.One of the evening’s memorable moments came when actor Sanya Malhotra joined him on stage as they grooved to the song ‘Water’. Dosanjh thanked Malhotra for popularising the song through her reels.As the evening drew to a close, Dosanjh performed ‘Main Hoon Punjab’, bringing thousands of fans together for one final sing along.With fireworks lighting up the venue and the audience cheering, dancing and singing along, the night ended on a high.The show was co-produced and promoted by BookMyShow Live and Live Nation.In order to ensure safety and security of people, BMS had issued a list of permitted and prohibited items for the concert. Flags, banners, posters, deodorants, makeup products, pens, knives, blades and sharp jewellery, along with lighters and laser pointers, were prohibited.Concertgoers were also prohibited from carrying items such as water balloons, eggs, empty bottles, umbrellas, professional cameras, tripods, selfie sticks, drones and recording equipment.The concert is part of Dosanjh’s AURA India Tour 2026. Following Mumbai, the singer is set to perform in Bengaluru on November 29, 2026.

headline: Saree, salwar suit and a BJP win: Rajasthan’s Bati Kumari’s triple nomination twist in pradhan election
content: In an unusual political drama in Rajasthan's Deeg district, Bati Kumari filed three nominations for the post of pradhan of Brij Nagar Panchayat Samiti — first as a Congress candidate, then as an Independent and finally as a BJP nominee. She was eventually elected unopposed on the BJP ticket.The sequence of events, which also involved a change of outfits, triggered a political controversy and prompted former Congress MLA Wajib Ali to resign as a member of the Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC), taking moral responsibility for the party's failure to secure the post.Bati Kumari initially arrived wearing a saree and filed her nomination as a Congress candidate in the presence of Ali. She later returned in a salwar suit and filed another nomination as an Independent. Subsequently, she arrived with BJP leader Jawahar Singh Bedham and submitted her nomination as the BJP candidate.With no other candidate in the fray, Bati Kumari withdrew her Congress and Independent nominations and was declared elected unopposed as the BJP candidate.Reacting to the development, Ali accused the BJP of using money power and misusing its position in government to secure the victory. He alleged that the ruling party had lured away the Congress candidate after she had filed her nomination."The Congress candidate came with us wearing a saree. But the BJP got her clothes changed and brought her back as its candidate to win the election," Ali told PTI.He alleged that the BJP had not won through a democratic process but had resorted to deception to capture the post."The Congress had the people's mandate to elect its pradhan, but the BJP scripted an entire drama to take away our candidate," he said.Taking moral responsibility for the setback, Ali announced his resignation from the PCC membership and apologised to Congress workers disappointed by the outcome.He said he would continue working for the Congress as an ordinary party worker without holding any organisational position.Rejecting the allegations, BJP district president Satish Bansal said Bati Kumari had filed her nomination as the party's candidate and was elected unopposed."It is a splendid victory for the BJP in Brij Nagar. Bati Kumari filed her nomination as our candidate and won unopposed," Bansal said.He dismissed Ali's allegations as baseless and advised him to use restrained language.PTI inputs

headline: Tata Sons files caveats after Bombay HC refuses relief to Tata trusts' plea
content: Tata Sons has filed caveats in the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court on Saturday, ensuring it will be heard if two Tata trusts file an appeal, according to sources.The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and RD Tata Trust could not get any relief from the Bombay High Court on Friday, which said it would not pass any order deferring or granting an injunction on the November 30 board meeting of Tata Sons.The trusts had sought for the meeting to be deferred and/or for an order restraining Chandrasekaran from exercising his casting vote."Caveats filed by Tata Sons Pvt Ltd in Bombay High Court and Supreme Court in relation to order dated 27 Nov 2026," as per a person in the know.The two Tata trusts can move the courts in appeal, and the caveats will help Tata Sons present their side in the matter.A bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja of the Bombay HC on Friday did not grant any immediate relief to the two Tata trusts and said that the meeting can go on as scheduled, but the same would be subject to the final orders of the court.The Tata trusts had sought to defer or stay the meeting, or an order that the chairman would not be allowed to exercise his casting vote.The bench ordered Tata Sons and the other respondents in the case, which include the board members, to submit their reply affidavits to two suits filed on Thursday (November 26) and posted the matter for further hearing on January 18, 2027.The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the RD Tata Trust (RDTT) had filed the suits in the High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term.The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore, while the RDTT has demanded Rs 15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest, from Tata Sons.As per the suits, the September 17 Tata Sons board resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association (AoA).The immediate relief sought was to prevent the chairman of Tata Sons from exercising his casting vote during the November 30 board sitting in the event of a split in opinion among nominee directors of Tata Trusts.On Friday, the trusts' counsels also sought for the meeting to be deferred, which was opposed by Tata Sons.Noel Tata, the chairman of Tata Trusts, is battling against Tata Sons, the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate in which the trusts have a 66 per cent ownership, over issues including the reappointment of Chandrasekaran and also trying to avoid a listing of the company.The RBI has mandated the listing of Tata Sons after classifying it as an NBFC-Upper Layer, and Noel has been pressing for a restructuring of the business to avoid the IPO.

headline: Delimitation explained: Will southern states lose political power? The numbers behind the 50% Lok Sabha expansion
content: The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a proposal to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha by 50% across all states, while keeping their existing relative share of parliamentary seats unchanged until the first Census conducted after 2051. The decision comes ahead of a special sitting of Parliament, called by the government from November 30 to December 3, Hindustan Times reported.During the special sitting, the Union government is expected to take up legislation linked to delimitation and the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies from 2029.The government has said the uniform expansion will preserve the existing share of seats held by each state. However, concerns remain over whether the exercise could affect the South's political influence at the Centre.Opposition questions timing and intentThe Opposition has questioned the timing and intent of the special sitting, alleging that the government is using women's reservation as a route to push through delimitation.Congress leaders have demanded that the existing strength of the Lok Sabha and the proportion of seats allocated to states be protected. Other Opposition parties have raised concerns about the numerical gap between northern and southern states, the redrawing of constituency boundaries and the functioning of a larger Parliament.The government, on the other hand, maintains that the uniform increase will preserve the existing relative representation of states. The revised proposal also seeks to use the 2011 Census as the basis for redrawing constituency boundaries, while keeping the inter-state allocation of seats unchanged until the first Census conducted after 2051, according to The Indian Express.The proposal is intended to address concerns, particularly among southern states, that a population-based delimitation exercise could reduce their share of representation in Parliament. Under the revised formula, each state and Union Territory would receive a uniform 50% increase in its existing Lok Sabha seats.If the proposed 50% increase is applied to the current strength of 543 seats, the Lok Sabha would have approximately 815 members. However, the proposed constitutional amendment provides for a maximum strength of 850 members.So, what does the 50% increase actually mean for each state? Will southern states retain their current share of Lok Sabha representation, even as the numerical gap between northern and southern states widens? Could a government be formed at the Centre without the support of southern states? And how would the proposed expansion change the majority mark in Parliament?Lets examine the numbers behind the delimitation proposal, comparing the current seat distribution across states with the mathematical projections under the proposed formula, and what they could mean for India's political arithmetic.What does the 50% formula actually mean?Under the proposed formula, every state would get a 50% increase over its existing Lok Sabha seats. The government says this would preserve the current relative distribution of seats among states, with their inter-state allocation remaining unchanged until the first Census conducted after 2051.Let's understand this with an example.Uttar Pradesh currently sends 80 MPs to the Lok Sabha. A 50% increase would take its projected strength to 120.In Tamil Nadu's case, the number of MPs would rise from 39 to 58.5 under the same calculation. The final number would depend on how the government handles fractional figures when allocating seats.The formula would apply uniformly to all states and Union Territories. It is different from a population-based delimitation exercise in which the distribution of seats could change according to population figures.Representation of five southern statesThe five southern states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu together have 129 seats in the Lok Sabha. This accounts for 23.76% of the lower House's current strength of 543.Tamil Nadu has 39 seats, accounting for 7.18% of the Lok Sabha; Karnataka has 28 seats (5.16%); Andhra Pradesh has 25 (4.60%); Kerala has 20 (3.68%); and Telangana has 17 (3.13%).If Puducherry is included, the southern states and the Union Territory together have 130 seats, or 23.94% of the Lok Sabha.What happens after a 50% increase?Under the proposed formula, the mathematical projections for the five southern states would be:Tamil Nadu: 39 to 58.5 seatsKarnataka: 28 to 42 seatsAndhra Pradesh: 25 to 37.5 seatsKerala: 20 to 30 seatsTelangana: 17 to 25.5 seatsTogether, their projected strength would rise from 129 to 193.5 seats. Including Puducherry, the combined figure would rise from 130 to 195.These half-seat figures are mathematical projections, not actual constituency allocations. The proposed legislation does not specify a rounding formula, so the final state-wise numbers will depend on the legal allocation process.Under a uniform 50% increase, the five southern states' combined share would remain at approximately 23.76%. Including Puducherry, their combined share would remain at approximately 23.94%.The final percentages could vary slightly depending on how fractional figures are handled and the final strength of the Lok Sabha.Doesn't the North already have more MPs than the South?The northern states already have a larger number of Lok Sabha MPs than the five southern states. Uttar Pradesh and Bihar alone currently account for 120 seats, compared with 129 across the five southern states.Uttar Pradesh has 80 seats, accounting for 14.73% of the Lok Sabha. Together, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar account for 22.10% of the House. By comparison, the five southern states account for 23.76%; the figure rises to 23.94% when Puducherry is included.Under the proposed formula, the 120 seats held by Uttar Pradesh and Bihar would mathematically rise to 180. The five southern states' combined projection would rise from 129 to 193.5.The important distinction is between having more MPs in absolute numbers and having a larger share of Parliament. The proposed uniform increase would raise the number of seats for both groups without changing their relative shares under the formula.Can a government be formed at the Centre without southern MPs?Yes. A political party or alliance can form a government by securing a majority of seats in the Lok Sabha, even without winning seats in a particular region. No geographical region is constitutionally required to be represented in a governing coalition.Under the current strength of 543 seats, the majority mark is 272. If the Lok Sabha's strength were to rise to 815, the majority mark would be 408. Lets understand with an example - a 50% increase on 543 gives 814.5, and the final strength and majority mark would depend on the allocation process. The proposed constitutional amendment sets the maximum strength at 850; it does not, by itself, confirm that the House will have exactly 815 seats.The five southern states, which currently have 129 seats, would have a mathematical projection of 193.5 under the proposed formula. Even with Puducherry included, the projected figure would be 195. This would not be enough to reach a majority on their own.But this is already the case under the current system. What matters for government formation is how seats are distributed among political parties and alliances across the country, not simply how many seats a region has.So, what changes then?The proposed expansion would increase the number of MPs in the Lok Sabha, but it would not necessarily change the share of seats held by each state. Since every state is expected to get a uniform 50% increase, its share of representation in Parliament would broadly remain the same.However, constituency boundaries within each state would be redrawn using the 2011 Census. This means the areas represented by individual MPs could change, even if the state's overall share of Lok Sabha seats remains unchanged.There could also be a change in the balance between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. The number of Lok Sabha MPs would increase, but the Rajya Sabha's strength would not automatically rise in the same proportion. As a result, the relative size of the two Houses could change.

headline: Man falls into open drain in Mansa, body taken to hospital on motorcycle cart
content: A 55-year-old carpenter died after falling into an uncovered drain on Court Road in Mansa on Friday night. His body was taken to the Civil Hospital on a motorcycle-drawn cart as no ambulance arrived despite repeated calls.The deceased, identified as Nikka Singh, was a resident of Mansa and was reportedly mentally unwell. The drain, two-three feet wide, was uncovered.His wife and some relatives came to the spot when his body was found on Saturday morning. The police, too, reached the spot, but no Health Department personnel arrived to shift the body.An eyewitness said that a policeman also made two phone calls to the emergency helpline 108 for an ambulance. However, after waiting for nearly 1.5 hours, the family and others had to arrange a motorcycle-drawn cart to take the body to the hospital.Congress leader Gurpreet Singh Vicky raised the issue on social media, questioning the civic arrangements and the response of emergency health services in the town. He said uncovered drains along roads and delays in emergency services raised serious concerns over public safety and the administration’s preparedness to deal with such incidents.Dr Gurmail Singh, Senior Medical Officer, Mansa, said the hospital does not provide an ambulance for transporting a body. “The 108 ambulance service is meant for patients. In cases where a person dies at home, it is the family’s responsibility to arrange transportation of the body. However, in cases requiring a post-mortem examination, the police should make arrangements to transport the body, either through an NGO or their own vehicle. A mortuary van should have been called in this case as the police were aware of the circumstances,” he said.

headline: TDI Infrastructure told to pay Rs 31.38 lakh interest for delay in handing over Sonipat plot
content: The Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (HRERA), Panchkula, has directed TDI Infrastructure Ltd to pay Rs 31.38 lakh as upfront interest for delay in handing over a plot to a Delhi-based buyer who has been waiting for possession of his property in the company's TDI City project at Kundli, Sonipat.The company will also have to pay an additional Rs 21,381 per month until it makes a valid offer of possession.In its order, Member Chander Shekhar held that the buyer, Sham Lal Goel, was entitled to interest at the rate of 10.95 per cent per annum on the Rs 23.76 lakh paid by him. The interest is payable from November 1, 2014, the deemed date of possession, until a valid offer of possession is made after obtaining an occupation or completion certificate.Goel owns Plot No. J-97B, a 250-square-yard corner plot. He had acquired the allotment rights in 2011 from an earlier allottee, who had booked the plot in 2005. The total sale consideration was Rs 22.03 lakh. Goel told the Authority that he was seeking possession of the plot and not a refund.TDI Infrastructure argued that the project predated the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act and was therefore not registered under it. The company also contended that the complaint was time-barred, that Goel was a subsequent allottee and that a dispute with landowners had prevented the delivery of possession. It further claimed that it was no longer developing the project.The Authority rejected these arguments. Citing the Supreme Court's ruling in the Newtech Promoters case, it held that ongoing projects without a completion certificate as on May 1, 2017, fell within the ambit of the RERA Act. It also observed that part-completion certificates could not be treated as proof of complete development.Rejecting the limitation plea, the Authority held that the Limitation Act did not apply to proceedings under RERA and that the cause of action continued as long as possession remained undelivered.The company had also relied on a letter dated June 5, 2018, offering Goel an alternative unit or adjustment of the amount paid against a property in another project. However, the Authority found no evidence that the letter had been dispatched or received by the buyer.It also noted that the offer did not identify any specific plot.The Authority held that the alternative offer, made nearly a decade after the original booking and without an occupation or completion certificate, was not legally valid.On Goel's status as a subsequent buyer, the Authority ruled that his entitlement to interest would be limited to the period following the transfer of allotment rights in his favour. Accordingly, it fixed the deemed date of possession at three years from the 2011 transfer.TDI Infrastructure has been given 90 days to comply with the order. Goel, however, will remain liable to pay any outstanding balance consideration when valid possession is offered. The company has been restrained from levying any charges beyond those stipulated in the agreed terms and conditions.

headline: Deepam row exposes TVK’s dilemma—minority support vs the rule of law
content: The Karthigai Deepam controversy in Tamil Nadu is not just about a temple ritual anymore. By defying a Supreme Court interim order and detaining Hindu activists and BJP leaders, the C Joseph Vijay government is testing party alliances, state authority, and political optics. On 27 November, the Supreme Court delivered a sharp judicial response and came down heavily on the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government, asking it to light the lamp at Deepathoon on Saturday, using the flame from the Karthigai Deepam lit at Uchi Pillaiyar temple. On 24 November at around 6 pm, the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam was lit at the traditional Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple on Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai. Despite the Supreme Court granting limited interim permission on 20 November for a restricted, one-time lighting at the Deepathoon by an authorised temple team—and the Madras High Court’s Madurai Bench reminding the district administration on Karthigai Deepam day that a pending review petition does not stay the order—the lamp was not lit at the Deepathoon. Last year, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagham (DMK) cited law and order issues as the concern, and despite a Madras High Court order, a lamp was not lit at the Deepathoon. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) followed the playbook, though a little differently, with the district administration shifting the onus on the temple authorities. Hindu activists and Hindu Munnani cadres gathered near the temple Tuesday, a scuffle broke out, and police forcibly removed the demonstrators, detaining around 300 people. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS had already been imposed across the district, backed by more than 5,600 police personnel, a temporary Red Zone, a drone ban, and barricades around the pillar. BJP leaders, including Tamilisai Soundararajan and Nainar Nagenthran, were stopped or detained while trying to reach the area. In that operational window, the Madurai administration functioned as both the non-executor of a Supreme Court direction and the uncompromising enforcer of public order against those protesting the non-execution. That real-time contradiction and the political calculations behind it make the Thiruparankundram Deepathoon controversy ThePrint’s Newsmaker of the Week. The final hearing of the case is scheduled for January 2027, and a contempt petition was filed by Rama Ravikumar, the original petitioner in the Deepam case and a Hindu Munnani leader.

headline: Delhi man killed after being hit by gas cylinder thrown by neighbour from third floor: Police
content: A 28-year-old man died after a cooking gas cylinder allegedly thrown from the third floor of a residential building in southwest Delhi's Bindapur Extension hit his head on Friday evening, police said. The cylinder was thrown by a 24-year-old resident of the same building following a quarrel between the two.The victim has been identified as Sahil, who lived with his wife Ritu (21), one-and-a-half-year-old son and mother on the first floor flat of Radhika Apartment in Bindapur Extension. He worked at a weekly market for a living, police said.The Dabri police station received a call regarding an incident at Bindapur Extension at around 7:15 pm on Friday, where a man threw a cylinder from a building's third floor, injuring another person who was taken to a nearby hospital, Deputy commissioner of police (Dwarka) Kushal Pal Singh said.A police team reached the scene and conducted a local enquiry. The personnel learnt that the injured man was declared dead at the hospital by the doctors.The accused has been identified as Shivam Sharma, a third floor resident of the same Radhika Apartment. Sharma, who works in tailoring and stitching at a factory in Bindapur, had been drinking since Friday morning, and did not go to work, police said."The incident began with a quarrel in the building's parking area with the other occupants, where an argument took place around 7pm. Thereafter, Sharma went upstairs in anger and threw the cooking gas cylinder down. The cylinder hit Sahil, who was standing below, causing serious injuries that proved fatal. Necessary legal action is being taken. Further investigation is underway," added DCP Singh.Sharma has been arrested and a case of murder has been registered under section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

headline: Sach Pass route, gateway to Himachal’s Pangi valley, shut for winter season
content: The Sach Pass road, the gateway to the remote and tribal Pangi valley, has been closed to vehicular traffic for winter season in view of falling temperatures, possible snowfall and the risk of icy conditions on the road.Chamba District Magistrate Mukesh Repaswal has issued the closure orders under Section 115 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, with immediate effect following a report by Pangi administration.According to the report submitted by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Pangi, temperatures at Sach Pass have started dipping below the freezing point, increasing the likelihood of snow accumulation and slippery conditions on the road. The administration has cited the potential danger to motorists and travellers while ordering the closure.The DC has directed the SDM, Churah, to make necessary arrangements to regulate the movement of tourists visiting snow tourism destinations located towards Sach Pass. The orders will remain in force until further directions or their modification by the competent authority.Located at an altitude of around 4,414 metres above the sea level, Sach Pass is one of the highest motorable mountain passes in Himachal Pradesh. It serves as a vital road link between Chamba and the remote Pangi valley, significantly shortening the distance compared to the longer alternative route via Kullu and Manali.The 170-km-long Chamba-Killar road via Sach Pass is also a major attraction for adventure travellers, bikers and tourists, particularly during the summer and early autumn months. The route offers spectacular views of snow-clad mountains, glaciers and rugged Himalayan terrain.However, the pass remains highly vulnerable to heavy snowfall, freezing temperatures, landslides and slippery road conditions. Its closure during winter isolates Pangi from direct road connectivity with Chamba, making the seasonal opening and maintenance of the route crucial for the region's residents, tourism and transportation.With the closure of Sach Pass, residents of Pangi will have to take the longer detour via Manali (650km) or Kishtwar of Jammu and Kashmir (650km) and reach Chamba involving a much longer and arduous journey to reach the district headquarters. This significantly increases travel time, distance and cost, particularly affecting patients, government employees and residents who need to visit Chamba for administrative and other essential work. The route through Sach Pass remains the shortest direct road link between Pangi and the district headquarters, but remains inaccessible during the harsh winter months due to heavy snowfall and freezing conditions.

headline: Karunadotsava | List of prominent companies founded by Kannadigas
content: This year, Karnataka is celebrating the 70th anniversary of its formation. It was formed as Mysore State on November 1, 1956, and renamed Karnataka on the same date in 1973.While Bengaluru has rightfully earned its reputation as India's technology and startup capital, the State's business legacy is equally reflected in companies founded by Kannadigas outside the metropolis..As Karnataka marks a historic milestone, here is a look at some iconic legacy businesses whose origins are deeply rooted in the Karunadu and whose reach extends well beyond its borders..Infosys Ltd was founded in 1981 by seven engineers: N R Narayana Murthy, Nandan Nilekani, S Gopalakrishnan, S D Shibulal, K Dinesh, N S Raghavan and Ashok Arora.Narayana Murthy and his colleagues started the business with an initial capital of just Rs 10,000, reportedly supported by his wife, Sudha Murty. Though it was first set up in Pune, the company moved its headquarters to Bengaluru and built its brand reputation on software exports, professional management and the global delivery model. Its growth helped establish Bengaluru as a major global technology hub.Today, Infosys is among India's largest IT services exporters, offering consulting, cloud, artificial intelligence, engineering and digital transformation services.Employee strength: Approximately 3.29 lakh.Approximate clients (national and international): Included in 1,965 active clients in around 59 countries..It was established on November 29, 1978, by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw. She began operations in the garage of a rented house at Koramangala, a suburb of Bengaluru.A trained brewer, she initially faced considerable challenges entering the biotechnology industry, which was then relatively unfamiliar in India. Her determination to build a science-led Indian enterprise eventually transformed Biocon into a major biotechnology company.In partnership with Ireland-based Biocon Biochemicals, it has grown to become a global powerhouse in the biotechnology industry.Today, Biocon operates in biopharmaceuticals, biosimilars, generics and research-based healthcare solutions. Its products serve patients and healthcare systems across international markets.Employee strength: Around 16,500 worldwideGlobal presence: Around 120 nations.The Manipal Group traces its origins to Dr T M A Pai (Tonse Madhava Ananth Pai ), who established several pioneering institutions in Karnataka.A doctor by profession, his entrepreneurial journey began with banking and community development before moving into education and healthcare. In 1953, T M A Pai founded Kasturba Medical College in Manipal, operating as a public-private collaboration with government hospitals in Mangaluru.For his outstanding contribution to society, T M A Pai was awarded the Padma Shri by the Government of India in 1972.His son Ramdas Pai subsequently expanded the institution's academic reach, strengthened its university structure and helped establish Manipal as a recognised international education and healthcare brand.The first branch of Manipal Hospitals was established on HAL Airport Road, Bengaluru, in 1991.For his philanthropic works, Ramdas Pai was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2011.Today, the wider Manipal ecosystem includes education, healthcare, research and other business interests. Manipal Hospitals alone has grown into a major healthcare network.It should be noted that Ramdas Pai's son Ranjan Pai, a medical doctor by qualification, also runs his own businesses, including educational institutions and hospitals. Ranjan Pai is the founder and chairman of the Manipal Education and Medical Group, which runs seven universities and 29 hospitals across the globe..Vijayanand Roadlines Ltd (VRL) Group was founded in 1976 by Vijay Sankeshwar in Gadag, Karnataka. His entrepreneurial journey began with a single truck and a vision to build a dependable goods transportation business.Over the years, it gradually expanded into Bengaluru, Hubballi and Belagavi before developing a nationwide transportation network.Now, VRL has diversified into parcel transportation, courier services, priority cargo, passenger transportation and logistics solutions.Employee strength: 20,000-plus with approximatelyNational reach: 1,249-plus goods transport branches and franchise locations with 5,745 owned goods transport vehicles..Narayana Health (previously known as Narayana Hrudyalaya) was founded by Devi Prasad Shetty, a legendary cardiac surgeon. The core theme of the organisation was to make high-quality healthcare accessible to common citizens of the country.After gaining medical experience in India and the United Kingdom, he returned to India and became known for his work in cardiac surgery. In 2000, he established Narayana Hrudayalaya in Bengaluru. The organisation subsequently expanded into a multispecialty healthcare network and adopted the Narayana Health brand in 2013.Narayana Health operates hospitals, heart centres, clinics and other healthcare facilities. Its services cover cardiac care, cancer treatment, neurology, orthopaedics, renal sciences and other specialities. It operates across 11 Indian cities, including Bengaluru, and has two hospitals in the Cayman Islands.Employee strength: Approximately 21,150.Captain Fresh was founded by Utham Gowda, a first-generation entrepreneur from Mysuru who identified an opportunity to modernise India's fragmented seafood supply chain. Traditionally, seafood procurement involved multiple intermediaries, inconsistent quality standards, limited traceability and complex international distribution. Gowda saw the potential to use technology, supply-chain integration and branded seafood products to connect fishermen, suppliers, processors, distributors and retailers. With an aim to develop a technology-driven seafood platform, he established Captain Fresh that could compete in international markets.Captain Fresh has expanded beyond the Indian market through acquisitions, international sourcing and branded seafood distribution.Its portfolio includes brands such as CenSea, Koral, Senecrus, ChopServe and Ocean Garden. During FY2025, the company reported serving 1,291 customers across 34 countries, with a sourcing network of 659 suppliers across 35 countries.As per the company's LinkedIn profile, it has 200-500 employees with 405 associated members..Zerodha Broking Ltd was founded by brothers Nithin Kamath and Nikhil Kamath as a discount brokerage firm in August 2010.The company's name has a very interesting meaning: it is a mix of 'zero' and 'rodha', the Sanskrit word for barrier. A barrier-free platform for people to make retail trading of stocks, derivatives, currencies, commodities, mutual funds, and bonds.The company started with six employees and Rs 2 crore in seed money drawn from Nithin Kamath's personal savings and contributions from a Singapore-based friend.By mid-2020, it became a unicorn with a one-billion-dollar valuation and has more than 13 lakh customers. The subscriber base soon rose to one crore by the end of 2022. Currently, it has over 1,200 employees and is valued at more than $3.5 billion..Cafe Coffee Day was founded by V G Siddhartha, an entrepreneur from Chikkamagaluru who came from a family associated with coffee cultivation. He studied economics and initially worked in the financial markets before entering the coffee business.In the early 1990s, he began building a coffee procurement and trading business, subsequently expanding into coffee plantations and retail. In 1996, he opened the first Cafe Coffee Day outlet on Brigade Road in Bengaluru. His aim was to create a welcoming social space where young Indians could meet, work and enjoy affordable coffee.Cafe Coffee Day became one of India's pioneering organised café chains, helping popularise the café culture among students, professionals and urban consumers. Its business evolved to include cafés, coffee vending machines, packaged coffee and other retail offerings. Its historical success was built around a large domestic store network and a recognisable Indian coffee brand.Following Siddhartha's death in 2019, his wife, Malavika Hegde, took over the reins.After years of losses and store closures, the company reported its first annual profit since 2019-20 in FY26. It registered net profit of Rs 28 crore on Rs 269 crore in revenue in Q1 FY-26..Akshayakalpa Organic was co-founded by Shashi Kumar and G N S Reddy in 2010.Shashi Kumar's entrepreneurial journey is particularly interesting because he moved from a successful technology career into agriculture.After completing his engineering education and spending approximately 17 years in the technology sector, including 13 years at Wipro, he became interested in the structural challenges faced by Indian farmers. He recognised that small dairy farmers needed better incomes, scientific farming support and a dependable route to market. The company was established to develop a farmer-led organic dairy model that could improve rural livelihoods while supplying consumers with quality organic food.Akshayakalpa works with farmers to develop sustainable dairy operations through training, animal care, organic farming practices and direct procurement systems. Its product portfolio includes milk, curd, paneer, ghee, butter and other dairy products.As per reports, Akshayakalpa Organic's network has around 2,800 farmers across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh..Robosoft Technologies was founded in 1996 by Rohith Bhat in Udupi, Karnataka. His entrepreneurial journey began when he identified an opportunity in software development for Apple Macintosh computers. At a time when India's software industry was largely focused on outsourced IT services, Bhat wanted to build a company specialising in digital products and user experiences.Starting with a small team, Robosoft gradually expanded its capabilities into mobile applications, user experience design and enterprise technology In 2022, the company was acquired by Japan's TechnoPro Group for around Rs 805 crore.Also, it should be noted that Rohith Bhat founded 99Games in Udupi, in 2008. The company emerged during the early growth of Apple's App Store, when smartphones were beginning to create new opportunities for independent game developers. Just like Rajesh Rao, who pioneered game development with Dhruva Interactive (which later acquired by Grand Theft Auto-maker Rockstar Games) in Bengaluru, Rohith Bhat recognised that Indian developers could create games for international audiences rather than simply developing software for outsourcing clients. .From Dhruva to Rockstar: How Bengaluru helped shape GTA and Red Dead.99Games began with a small team of developers and launched its early games, including chess titles, on Apple's App Store. Its early success demonstrated that a technology company from a small Karnataka city could stand out in the global mobile gaming industry..Karunadotsava | Kannada identity must be felt, understood, not just expressed, says actor Shivarajkumar.Karunadotsava | From ragi mudde to pandi curry, authentic dishes from Karnataka that every foodie must try.99Games is credited to development of mobile games, casual entertainment products and original gaming intellectual property. Some prominent titles include Dhoom:3 The Game and Star Chef.There are many more companies worth mentioning, including Air Deccan (founded by Capt G R Gopinath), and new and upcoming firms such as Wellbi (by Supreeth Kashyap), Xpheno (by Kamal Karanth), The Good Doll (by Suhas Ramegowda), Bounce Infinity (Vivekananda Hallekere), Real Fast AI (by Sidu Ponnappa), Sonic Lamb ( by Navajith Karkera), and Cuzor Labs (by Sachin Naik) that inspire thousands of new generation of Kannadigas to take up the enterprenuership with confidence and bring laurels to Karnataka.

headline: HC tells Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh to submit monthly reports on stray dog sterilisation, vaccination
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh to undertake sterilisation and vaccination measures for stray dogs in every district and submit monthly affidavits detailing the progress. It has also allowed NGOs, animal welfare associations and volunteers to offer land and other facilities for setting up dedicated centres for housing the animals.The Division Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor directed the States and the Union Territory to ensure “scrupulous compliance with the provisions of the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023” by undertaking sterilisation and vaccination measures in each district. The monthly affidavits must specify “the total number of drives undertaken in a district as well as the number of dogs which are subjected to sterilisation/vaccination and are housed in the ABC (Animal Birth Control) centres”.“The NGOs/animal welfare associations/volunteers and the State will also make the requisite endeavours to create dog adoption centres so that the rehabilitation of stray dogs is facilitated in an orderly manner. Those who adopt the stray dogs will ensure that such dogs are not then left to roam around on the streets and are properly cared for,” the Court asserted.The Bench further directed the States and Chandigarh to create designated websites “where such information would be uploaded on a monthly basis”. The information was also directed to be placed before the court through affidavits.Addressing the twin concerns of animal welfare and public safety, the High Court observed one was the well-being of stray dogs required to be “regulated and monitored in accordance with the provisions of the Animal Birth Control Rules and the provisions contained in the various Municipal laws providing for creation of centres for habitation of such dogs and for their treatment”.The second and “equally serious concern” was the well-being of citizens and children to move freely on public roads and public places without the fear of street dogs mauling them. “Only day before yesterday, the newspaper reports highlighted an incident occurring in district Amritsar, where an 8-year-old boy was mauled to death by street dogs. Such incidents are shocking and need immediate attention,” the Bench noted.The court noted that the States had been filing affidavits claiming on undertaking requisite measures to deal with “the menace of stray dogs and for their well-being”. But it was accepted “on both sides that such measures have failed to fully address the concern”.The Bench also took note of submissions by advocate Anurag Chopra’s submissions on behalf of one of the NGOs that such organisations, animal welfare associations/volunteers were willing to provide land to the State authorities for establishing dedicated centres for housing stray dogs. They were also willing to provide other support and facilities. But the authorities were not willing to accept assistance from them.The court, however, observed that “there is nothing on record to indicate that any of these NGOs/Animal Welfare Associations/volunteers have actually offered any piece of land or other facilities” which could contribute to the available resources for handling the situation.The Bench accordingly permitted the petitioners and any other NGO, animal welfare association or volunteer to offer land or other facilities to the Deputy Commissioner concerned and inform the court through an affidavit. The Bench said this would enable it to issue appropriate directions, if required, “for the increase in available resources to handle the situation”.The court also directed NGOs, animal welfare associations, volunteers and the States to make efforts to establish dog adoption centres to facilitate the orderly rehabilitation of stray dogs. Those adopting the animals must ensure that they are not subsequently left to roam the streets and are “properly cared for”.The matter will now come up for further hearing on January 11, 2027.

headline: NEWS RECEIVED FROM PB BJP PRINT MEDIA AT CHANDIGARH
content: Ambulance Fails to Reach in Mansa, Body Carried on Handcart; AAP’s ‘Sehat Kranti’ Reality Exposed: Kewal Singh Dhillon Crores spent on advertisements, but no ambulances on roads; Mann govt put to shame: Dhillon CHANDIGARH, NOVEMBER 28:Taking strong exception to the heart-wrenching incident in Mansa, Punjab BJP President Kewal Singh Dhillon today put the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in the dock. On Mansa’s Court Road, a 55-year-old man named Nikka Singh lost his life after falling into an open drain, yet despite repeated calls by the family and passersby to the 108 ambulance helpline and a wait of one and a half hours, no ambulance reached the spot. The helpless family was forced to place the body on a handcart attached to a motorcycle to take it to the Civil Hospital. This scene exposes the true face of the Aam Aadmi Party’s much-hyped 'Sehat Kranti' (Health Revolution), said Dhillon. Emergency Health Infrastructure Has Completely CollapsedDhillon stated that even when a police official present at the scene dialled 108, no ambulance turned up. This is not an isolated lapse, but proof of the complete collapse of Punjab’s emergency healthcare infrastructure. In a state whose government spends crores of rupees printing advertisements across India claiming a 'Health Revolution', not even an ambulance or dead body van is available to transport a deceased person to the hospital. This is utterly shameful. Dhillon added that the Mann government’s 'Sehat Kranti' is confined solely to newspaper advertisements and social media reels. Ambulance services across rural and semi-urban areas of Punjab are in a dismal state: in several districts, the number of ambulances falls far short of requirements, many existing vehicles are lying out of order, and there is an acute shortage of staff. When a poor family is forced to carry the body of a loved one on a handcart, it is the biggest matter of shame for any government. Dhillon demanded that the Mann government redirect the crores of rupees being squandered on publicity toward strengthening Punjab’s ambulance service and emergency health infrastructure, order a high-level inquiry into the Mansa incident, and grant compensation to the bereaved family. headline: Punjab ETT teachers stage protest outside Manish Sisodia's residence in Chandigarh, demand action on pend
content: Punjab Elementary Teacher Training (ETT) teachers on Saturday staged a protest near Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Manish Sisodia's residence in Chandigarh, demanding action on their pending grievances.Heavy police deployment was witnessed at the protest site.A protester said the teachers had been raising their concerns with the Punjab government for the past five years, but their demands remained unaddressed despite repeated assurances."We are a group of ETT teachers from Punjab. For the past five years, we have been pleading with this government to address our issues, but they have only offered one false promise after another. Harpal Singh Cheema had promised us that as soon as their party came to power, the matter concerning these 180 teachers would be resolved on a priority basis. Yet, even after five years, not a single one of our demands has been met. Instead, we are being subjected to high-handedness and mistreatment. They are treating every section of society in Punjab this way," the protester said.Another protester said the teachers intended to hold a peaceful demonstration but were prevented by police from moving further."We intend to hold a peaceful protest. We have been stopped here to prevent us from moving any further. We have no other demands; we simply want the clerk who committed the malpractice to be suspended," the protester said.Meanwhile, in a separate development, the Himachal Pradesh University Teachers' Welfare Association (HPUTWA) on Thursday met the Governor of Himachal Pradesh and raised concerns over the university's autonomy, academic freedom and institutional structure, seeking protection of its established governance framework in the wake of the proposed University Amendment Bill.The association's peaceful and democratic agitation against the proposed amendment has continued for 85 days, with teachers staging a daily sit-in outside the Vice-Chancellor's office at Himachal Pradesh University (HPU).During the meeting, the HPUTWA executive committee delegation discussed several issues concerning the university's existing statutory framework, the Vice-Chancellor's appointment process, and its academic and administrative autonomy.The delegation urged the Governor to ensure that future decisions concerning the university preserve its historic institutional structure and autonomy. The Governor heard the delegation's concerns and assured them that the issues raised would be considered.Explaining the significance of university autonomy, the delegation said that while autonomy literally means self-governance, its broader meaning lies in the ability of an institution to make independent decisions to achieve its objectives without external, particularly political, interference.In the context of universities, autonomy means freedom to take academic, research, administrative and policy-related decisions independently to fulfil their core institutional objectives, the association said.The delegation maintained that university autonomy was fundamental to academic freedom, research, innovation and institutional development and should not be weakened under any circumstances.The representatives further argued that the problems faced by the university should be addressed by providing adequate resources, qualified manpower, regular leadership and a robust academic system rather than restricting its autonomy.They said HPU must retain the freedom to make its own academic and research-related decisions to effectively fulfil its role in higher education and research.The delegation met the Governor under the guidance of former HPUTWA office-bearers and senior academicians Prof. D. D. Sharma, Prof. Chandra Mohan Parshira and Prof. Duni Chand.The delegation included HPUTWA President Nitin Vyas, Vice-President Yograj, Secretary Ankusha Bhardwaj, Joint Secretary Anjali Sharma, Treasurer Ram Lal, Rajesh Sharma and B R Thakur.Prof. Nitin Vyas, President of HPUTWA, said, "The autonomy of the university is not an issue concerning any one section alone. It is an important question linked to the future of the entire university community, including teachers, non-teaching staff, research scholars and students. Any adverse impact on autonomy could directly affect academic freedom, the quality of research, innovation and the university's institutional decision-making process."The association expressed hope that the issues raised before the Governor would receive positive consideration and that appropriate steps would be taken to safeguard the university's autonomy and academic freedom.HPUTWA reiterated that its peaceful and democratic movement against the University Amendment Bill would continue to protect HPU's institutional dignity, autonomy, academic freedom and democratic values.The association maintained that strengthening the university required developing it as an independent and capable institution rather than curtailing its autonomy.(with ANI inputs)Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Patiala MC re-poll: Voting underway in 30 wards under High Court watch amid poll rigging allegations
content: Voting began in 30 wards of Patiala on Saturday, where a re-poll was ordered following Supreme Court directions. The polling is being monitored by the High Court after opposition candidates highlighted violence and the partisan role of the police during the previous election.As many as 1,49,768 voters are eligible to cast their votes in the 30 wards where re-polling is being held.Meanwhile, police have been deployed in heavy numbers to ensure there is no untoward incident.Unlike last time, when polling booths were captured and unidentified and identified men roamed the streets, the police are under strict surveillance of the State Election Commission, which has deployed senior officers as observers to ensure fair polling.While not much rush was seen in the wards going for re-polling, the numbers are expected to go up as the day proceeds.Polling is being held in Ward Nos. 1, 4, 6, 12, 14, 15, 16, 22, 26, 28, 32, 33, 34, 36, 37, 38, 40, 41, 43, 44, 45, 46, 48, 50, 51, 52, 53, 55, 57 and 58, following the Supreme Court’s directions.A total of 1,49,768 voters, including 77,419 men, 72,338 women and 11 third-gender voters, are eligible to exercise their franchise.The contest would be a litmus test for the AAP cadre in the city as the party bagged most of these wards amid allegations of poll rigging. The election will also test the political landscape of Patiala, where the Congress is eager for its political revival while the SAD-BJP too wants to win after their coalition announcement.

headline: NHRC seeks report from Punjab Chief Secretary, DGP over alleged removal of Nishan Sahib in Gurdaspur
content: Gurdaspur (Punjab) [India], November 28 (ANI): The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has taken cognisance of a complaint regarding the alleged removal of the sacred Nishan Sahib at DallaMor Qadian village in Punjab's Gurdaspur district and issued notices to the state's Chief Secretary and Director General of Police (DGP), seeking an Action Taken Report (ATR) within two weeks.The Commission on Friday, in a Bench presided over by its Member Priyank Kanoongo, observed that the allegations prima facie appeared to constitute violations of human rights and directed the state authorities to conduct an inquiry into the matter.Sharing the development, Kanoongo alleged that the sacred Nishan Sahib was removed under suspicious circumstances during the night and that a government JCB machine was allegedly used for the purpose. He also raised concerns over the alleged lack of police action. पंजाब के गुरदासपुर ज़िले में पवित्र निशान साहिब को रात के अंधेरे में कथित तौर पर धोखे से हटाए जाने और इस कृत्य के लिए सरकारी JCB मशीन के इस्तेमाल किए जाने के गंभीर आरोप सामने आए हैं। यह अत्यंत गंभीर मामला है,और पुलिस कार्रवाई करने को तैयार नहीं है। हमने DGP और मुख्य सचिव (CS) को औपचारिक नोटिस जारी कर राज्य सरकार के संबंध में विधिसम्मत कार्रवाई की प्रक्रिया प्रारंभ कर दी है। @BhagwantMann In a post on X, Kanoongo said, "Serious allegations have emerged in Punjab's Gurdaspur district that the sacred Nishan Sahib was allegedly removed deceitfully under the cover of darkness at night and that a government JCB machine was used for this act."This is an extremely serious matter, and the police are not ready to take action. We have issued formal notices to the DGP and the Chief Secretary (CS) and initiated the process for taking action against the state government in accordance with the law."According to the complaint received by the NHRC, a local farmer had donated 10 marlas of his personal land for the construction of a Gurdwara Langar Hall. Subsequently, the Sikh congregation installed the Nishan Sahib at the site in accordance with Sikh traditions and Gurmat Maryada.However, certain miscreants allegedly belonging to an opposing group, with the backing of political individuals and through the alleged misuse of government machinery, removed the sacred religious symbol. The complaint stated that the incident deeply hurt the religious sentiments of the Sikh community.Taking cognisance under Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Commission directed the Punjab Chief Secretary and DGP to inquire into the allegations and submit an ATR within two weeks.The NHRC has also sought a certified copy of the order or application issued by the competent authority authorising the removal of the Nishan Sahib. In case no such authorisation was issued, the authorities have been asked to submit a detailed report explaining how government machinery was deployed for the removal and what action has been taken in the matter.The Commission has further called for accountability and a proper investigation into the incident, along with preventive safeguards to ensure respect for Sikh religious symbols, sentiments and the right to religious freedom. (ANI)

headline: Waris Punjab De eyes Punjabi diaspora support with rally in Canada’s Brampton
content: At a time when political parties in Punjab are yet to see any visible mobilisation of Non-Resident Indian (NRI) supporters overseas, Akali Dal Waris Punjab De (AD-WPD) appears to be reaching out to the Punjabi diaspora, with its supporters organising a rally in Brampton, Canada, on December 20.The political outfit, which is still awaiting registration as a political party, has shared the rally poster on its official social media handles, inviting Punjabis living in Canada to participate in what it has described as a gathering for Punjab's rights.Titled 'Punjab Rally', the poster carries the message: “The time has come to stand together. For Punjab, for the Panth, and for the voice of Punjab's youth, we will come together once again.”The organisers have urged participants to bring along their families, friends and children, describing the event as a platform to raise their voice for Punjab's rights.The poster features a larger picture of Khadoor Sahib MP Amritpal Singh, who is currently in Dibrugarh jail, followed by pictures of Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale, human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra and Sikh activist Sandeep Singh alias Deep Sidhu.The proposed rally, however, has also come under scrutiny over the political affiliations and ideological positions of some of its organisers.The proposed overseas mobilisation comes amid the outfit's efforts to expand its organisational presence in Punjab. AD-WPD has previously organised rallies at Chhapar Mela in Ludhiana district and during Rakhar Puniya at Baba Bakala in Amritsar district, drawing supporters from different parts of the state.The outfit has also witnessed a show of public support during the recent three-hour visit of its patron and Khadoor Sahib MP Amritpal Singh to Amritsar, where he had arrived to attend the funeral of his grandmother, Charan Kaur (84). A large number of supporters gathered during his visit.Meanwhile, AD-WPD leader and Dakha MLA Manpreet Singh Ayali has urged the government to facilitate Amritpal Singh's participation in parliamentary proceedings, reiterating the demand that the elected MP be allowed to raise issues concerning his constituency and Punjab in the Lok Sabha.The Brampton rally could provide an opportunity for the outfit to assess and consolidate its support base among the Punjabi diaspora, particularly in Canada, where Punjab-related political and Panthic issues have traditionally drawn considerable community interest.

headline: Punjab Pavilion bags gold medal at India International Trade Fair
content: Punjab has won the gold medal for best thematic presentation among all participating states at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 13 to 27.Conceptualised and developed by the Punjab Small Industries & Export Corporation Limited (PSIEC), the 450-square metre pavilion was selected by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) jury for its theme “Vikas aur Virasat”, which blended Punjab’s cultural heritage with its modern industrial capabilities and technological advancements.Addressing the fair in New Delhi, Punjab industries and commerce minister Aman Arora said the theme “Vikas aur Virasat” reflected a state where heritage and enterprise had always gone together, noting that Punjab’s industrial base – from Ludhiana’s hosiery and bicycles and Jalandhar’s sports goods and hand tools to Mandi Gobindgarh’s steel and Batala’s foundries – was built by families over generations and now comprises 18.12 lakh registered MSMEs.“This is our industrial virasat,” he added.He said between March 16, 2022, and November 10, 2026, the state received 10,673 investment proposals (CAFs) worth around ₹2 lakh crore, promising employment for 6,63,410 people.Global majors such as Tata Steel, Nestle, PepsiCo, Unilever, Cargill, Danone, Linde, Yanmar, Freudenberg, Sunjin, Toppan and Sanathan Textiles have already established operations in the state. He added that investor outreach in India and abroad was now converting commitments into projects on the ground.Arora further said the state government’s FastTrack Punjab digital single window brought more than 300 services from over 20 departments under one login, with approvals to be granted within 45 working days.If a department does not decide within the deadline, the approval will be treated as automatically granted. To shape policy around industry needs, the state government constituted 24 sectoral committees that formulated the Industrial and Business Development Policy (IBDP) 2026 and sectoral policies, he added.These reforms earned Punjab the Top Achiever rating in Ease of Doing Business for 2022 and 2024, Arora said, while adding that Punjab was building industries of the future — auto components, electric vehicles, defence and aerospace, electronics, textiles, food processing, IT and GCCs, and sports goods.In defence and aerospace, Invest Punjab’s Aerospace and Defence Advisory Forum was matchmaking MSMEs with large buyers, encouraging sourcing and manufacturing from Punjab and supporting technology upgradation. The HUNAR Punjab Portal connects industry with about 1,750 educational and training institutions for jobs, internships and industrial training, the minister detailed.After his visit to the Punjab Pavilion, he said, “I invite every investor visiting this fair to visit the Punjab Pavilion and meet the Invest Punjab team. The government of Punjab stands with every entrepreneur, from the smallest MSME to the largest investor. I wish all our exhibitors and artisans good business and new partnerships.”

headline: ED questions two more Punjab officials; more summons likely
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday questioned two more Punjab government officials in connection with its money laundering probe originating from a graft case against suspended deputy inspector general of police (DIG) Harcharan Singh Bhullar and his alleged middleman Kirshanu Sharda.The two officials — Ropar Range DIG Swapan Sharma (IPS) and retired IAS officer Gurpreet Kaur Sapra — were among seven serving and retired administrative and police officers summoned by the agency for questioning this week. The remaining five have already appeared before the agency and recorded their statements on different dates between November 23 and 26.These include Kumar Rahul (IAS), administrative secretary, health and family welfare department; Neeru Katyal Gupta (IAS), special secretary, general administration and coordination; Anand Sagar Sharma, staff officer to the commissioner, Faridkot division; Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh (PPS); and Arun Sekhri, a retired IAS officer.The ED is likely to summon more serving and retired government officials for questioning as it widens its investigation into Sharda’s alleged network of contacts within the Punjab government, officials familiar with the probe said.“We have been scrutinising the digital record recovered from Bhullar’s aide Kirshanu Sharda. During his interrogation, the names of several serving and retired officials came to fore. Their statements are being recorded to ascertain the nature of their alleged associations with him,” an ED official said.In October 2025, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested 2009-batch IPS officer Harcharan Singh Bhullar, then DIG, Ropar Range, and his alleged middleman, Kirshanu Sharda, a national-level hockey player, in a ₹8-lakh bribery case.The CBI action came on a complaint by Akash Batta, a Mandi Gobindgarh-based scrap dealer, who alleged that Bhullar demanded illegal gratification through Sharda for favourable treatment in an FIR registered at the Sirhind police station and to ensure that no coercive action was taken against his business.Following massive cash and asset recoveries during subsequent searches, the CBI also registered a separate disproportionate assets (DA) FIR against Bhullar later that month.Based on these two CBI FIRs, the ED initiated a parallel money-laundering investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). As part of its probe, the ED arrested Sharda on September 18, 2026, and Bhullar on October 9, 2026. Currently, both remain in judicial custody.Sharda acted as middleman: EDOn November 20 this year, the ED filed a prosecution complaint before the special PMLA court in Chandigarh, alleging that Sharda acted as a middleman for several government officials, facilitating transfers, postings and other official work in exchange for money.The agency stated that Sharda had developed a network of contacts in the police, civil administration, revenue authorities and other government departments. According to the ED, he acted as a conduit between people seeking official favours and public servants who could influence or decide such matters.The ED investigation attributed around ₹1 crore in alleged proceeds of crime to Sharda. It also found that ₹1 crore had been credited to eight bank and post office accounts held by him and his wife between 2013 and 2025. A significant increase in transactions was noticed from 2023 onwards, when credits of nearly ₹86 lakh were recorded, including cash deposits of around ₹59 lakh. Before 2023, the total credits stood at around ₹14 lakh, the ED said.Sharda has claimed that the money came from hockey coaching and tournament-related activities, while his wife earned through home tuition. However, the agency said they failed to produce documentary evidence to substantiate these claims. Their income tax returns also did not reflect earnings corresponding to the amounts deposited in their accounts, said the ED.The agency is also probing UPI transactions worth ₹17 lakh received in Sharda’s Bank of Baroda account, allegedly in connection with facilitating transfers, postings and other official work.
