headline: After Patiala collapse, Punjab orders safety audit of all bridges
content: Taking note of the recent collapse of a bridge in Patiala district, public works minister Harbhajan Singh has ordered all senior field engineering officers of the Public Works Department (B&R) to inspect all bridges under their respective jurisdictions across the state.Chairing a review meeting, the minister directed the field officers to pay special attention to the structural condition of bridges, including foundations, piers, abutments, decks and other critical components. “Any signs of cracks, deterioration or structural distress must be promptly assessed and necessary preventive measures taken. Wherever required, specialised agencies, reputed technical institutions or structural engineering experts may be engaged to conduct detailed structural safety audits and non-destructive testing, particularly for old and vulnerable bridges,” he said.The directive came days after a 60-metre-long steel truss bridge over the Bhakra Main Line Canal near Pasiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur highway collapsed on November 19. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) built the bridge in 2016, raising questions about its structural safety and maintenance.During the meeting, the minister also assessed the constituency- and division-wise status of the ongoing works related to state highways and link roads.

headline: Warring, Bains lead ‘Insaaf March’
content: The factional battle within the Congress in Atam Nagar intensified on Friday with two factions holding parallel programmes. One, led by MP and former state president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, along with ticket-aspirant former MLA Simrajeet Singh Bains, organised an ‘Insaaf March’. The second, led by another contender, Kamaljit Singh Karwal, continued its ward-wise ‘Jawaani Sambhaal Cycle Yatra’, backed by senior Congress leaders Bharat Bhushan Ashu and Kapurthala MLA Rana Gurjeet Singh.Friday was the third day of the Karwal’s yatra, an extension of a similar campaign launched by Jalandhar MP and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi.The Warring-Bains event was attended by several Congress leaders, including Capt Sandeep Sandhu (retd), Ludhiana Urban Congress president Sanjay Talwar, former MLAs Rakesh Pandey and Kuldeep Singh Vaid. Former MLA Balwinder Singh Bains, Simarjeet’s brother, was also present.Bains merged his Lok Insaaf Party with the Congress ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and was inducted into the party by Warring.Addressing the gathering, Warring targeted the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, accusing it of betraying the people of Punjab despite securing a massive mandate in the 2022 assembly elections.“Gangster violence had crossed all limits and people no longer felt safe in the state. The audacity of gangsters to openly commit murders reflected the deteriorating law and order situation in Punjab,” he alleged.Warring also launched a sharp attack on the BJP-led central government, holding it responsible for the prevailing situation in the state and accusing it of patronising gangster Lawrence Bishnoi, who is lodged in the Sabarmati Jail in Gujarat.Meanwhile, Karwal, along with Ashu and Rana Gurjeet, held a parallel programme to build support for his bid to secure the party ticket.

headline: Govt rolls out ‘Mission Clean Punjab 3.0’ to fix civic woes
content: Stepping up sanitation efforts in urban spaces, the Punjab government on Friday launched “Mission Clean Punjab 3.0” across all 166 urban local bodies (ULBs) in the state to tackle eight key civic issues in every ward.Local government minister Harjot Singh Bains, who launched the campaign, said it builds upon the “resounding success” of earlier cleanliness drives by moving beyond routine garbage collection.Addressing a press conference, Bains said eight critical day-to-day civic problems would be identified and resolved across every urban ward in all 166 ULBs.He said municipal teams would work on a mission mode to create cleaner, safer and brighter wards by targeting specific civic issues, including garbage vulnerable points, hotspots of construction and demolition (C&D) waste dumping, waterlogging, open or broken manholes, potholes, broken or missing kerbstones, non-working street lights, and dark stretches currently lacking street lights altogether.He said personnel from the Punjab Ex-Servicemen Corporation (PESCO) had been deployed to actively patrol wards and log civic defects directly onto the Punjab mSeva App and web portal.Simultaneously, citizens are encouraged to report any of these eight issues on the mSeva platform, where every complaint will be geo-tagged, recorded and tracked in real time until final resolution, he said.He directed senior government officials to conduct daily field visits for at least two hours, while elected representatives would closely monitor the campaign in their respective constituencies.Sharing the outcomes of the previous phase, the minister said “Mission Clean 2.0”, conducted from August 29 to September 30, 2026, across all 166 ULBs, recorded a 90% complaint resolution rate.Of the 31,802 complaints received during the campaign, 28,686 were resolved, while 2,935 remained pending and 181 were declared invalid or rejected, he said.Making a direct appeal for public participation, the minister said, “Mission Clean Punjab demonstrated what Punjab can accomplish when the Bhagwant Mann government and citizens work hand-in-hand; 9 out of every 10 complaints were resolved.””With Mission Clean Punjab 3.0, we are stepping into every single ward. Whether you spot a garbage dump, an open manhole, a pothole, waterlogging, or a dark street, simply report it on the mSeva App or website, and our teams will act promptly. Together, let us make every ward of Punjab a model Swachh Ward,” he added.

headline: Bystander injured in exchange of fire between police, suspects in Hoshiarpur
content: A bystander was injured in an exchange of fire between the police and suspected criminals during a chase at Balagan Chowk in Dasuya on Friday afternoon.Mohammad Rafi, 30, sustained a bullet injury in his arm while he was at his dry-cleaning shop near the chowk. He was admitted to the Dasuya civil hospital and was stated to be out of danger, police said.Deputy superintendent of police (Detective) Parneet Singh said the Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) had been probing a firing incident for which an FIR was registered at the Garhdiwala police station on November 15.Acting on leads developed during the probe, the police team reached the Dasuya area and spotted the suspects’ vehicle near Balagan Chowk.Noticing the police team, the occupants attempted to flee, ramming their vehicle into the CIA team’s vehicle and damaging several other vehicles amid traffic, he said.To evade arrest, the suspects opened fire at the police party, prompting the personnel to retaliate, Singh said. A shot fired at the police vehicle hit Rafi in the arm.Police managed to apprehend one of the accused, Jaswinder singh, a resident of Bodal, while the other, Harkamalpreet Singh of Makhu, managed to escape.Dasuya station house officer (SHO) Gursahab Singh said, “We have rounded up one of the accused while the hunt for the rest is on.”

headline: Sampat slams state govt for ‘pushing universities into debt’
content: Former Haryana minister, Sampat Singh on Friday criticised the state government for allegedly pushing 22 state universities into an “unprecedented debt” burden of ₹16,052 crore over the past four years.At a briefing in Chandigarh, the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) leader said the conversion of grants-in-aid into repayable loans was a calculated withdrawal from public higher education and threatened to trigger the commercialisation, closure, or private takeover of public institutions.Singh noted that the government initially replaced grants with loans on April 29, 2022 before rolling back the order on May 22, 2022 following academic protests. However, he described the rollback as an eyewash. After releasing grants for only two quarters in 2022-23, the government continued disbursing funds under alternative labels such as non-recurring expenditure while quietly booking them under budget head 6202 (loans for education, sports, art, and culture) instead of budget head 2202 (grants for education).“Consequently, the 22 universities have accumulated ₹16,052 crore in liabilities and have been told to self-finance their academic activities through alumni donations, CSR funds, patents and the commercial use of surplus land,” the former minister said.The INLD leader said this has crippled university staffing and academic standards. “Out of 6,290 sanctioned regular teaching positions, only 2,733 (43.5%) are filled, leaving 3,557 posts vacant,’’ he maintained. Singh demanded that the state government should immediately restore full grant in aid (under head 2202), halt all loan conversions, waive existing university liabilities and release adequate funds to fill vacant teaching and non-teaching positions.

headline: Punjab clears  ₹100 crore grant for 500 gaushalas, 20 cattle pounds
content: The Punjab government on Friday approved a ₹100 crore grant for 500 registered gaushalas and 20 government cattle pounds across the state.Announcing this, industries and commerce minister Aman Arora said the funds would be transferred to gaushalas in a single instalment over the next two to three days.He said that with this, the government fulfilled a long-pending demand of social organisations working for animal welfare. “For the first time, the state government has decided to extend financial assistance uniformly to every registered gaushala across the state, irrespective of whether it is located in an urban or rural area, or whether it is government-run or privately managed,” he claimed at a press conference.Arora said the financial aid was earlier restricted to 228 gaushalas located within urban municipal limits, while 272 gaushalas operating in rural areas received no government funding. He said that during a recent review meeting chaired by chief minister Bhagwant Mann, it was observed that while urban gaushalas often received community donations and fodder support, rural gaushalas faced serious difficulties in sustaining stray cattle.Arora said the state government had already provided free electricity to all 518 gaushalas in the state and waived outstanding electricity bills worth more than ₹100 crore.

headline: BJP eyes bigger share in Punjab, stakes claim to SAD strongholds
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are heading for tough seat-sharing negotiations, with the former eyeing a significantly larger share of the 117 assembly seats, including several constituencies it used to cede to its ally under their previous arrangement.BJP leaders familiar with the matter said the party’s claim of 42-46 seats, nearly double the 23 it contested earlier, was driven by its assessment of its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. This would leave the SAD with roughly 72-75 seats.During its 24-year partnership, the saffron party contested 23 seats and the SAD 94. The reunion was formalised on Gurpurb on November 24—six years after the split over the three farm laws—at a joint press conference in New Delhi attended by Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin, and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal.“Even though the saffron party didn’t win any seat in the Lok Sabha elections, it secured a 19% vote share and is now eyeing several urban and semi-urban segments, which might lead to a turf battle with the ally,” a senior party leader said, requesting anonymity.The leader added that the party was keen to secure the Dera Bassi, Kharar, Mohali, Garhshankar, Balachaur, Jalandhar Cantonment, Bathinda, Kartarpur, Khanna, Barnala, Patiala Rural, Sahnewal and Mansa seats based on its assessment of its electoral prospects.Also Read: Even together, SAD, BJP won’t cross single digit: Pargat“In the three seats in Mohali district— Kharar, Mohali and Dera Bassi — the BJP secured over 35,000 votes in each segment in the Lok Sabha polls. The demographic changes in these constituencies over the past few years, driven by significant migration from other states, including Himachal Pradesh and Haryana, have added to the party’s confidence,” the leader said.In Dera Bassi, Darshan Singh Saini, an influential businessman and close aide of Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini, is being seen as a frontrunner. However, he faces a strong claim from two-time former MLA NK Sharma, a close aide of the SAD chief.In Kharar, another seat traditionally contested by the SAD, the BJP got over 38,000 votes in the 2024 LS polls. In Mohali, the BJP wants the seat for its district president Sanjeev Vashisht. The SAD had contested the constituency under the previous alliance arrangement but never won it.The BJP is also staking a claim to Balachaur, citing the sizeable Hindu Gujjar electorate. Garhshankar in Hoshiarpur is another seat where the two parties could have competing claims. It was represented by senior BJP leader Avinash Rai Khanna before the SAD claimed it in 2012 in exchange for Ludhiana Central.In Jalandhar Cantonment, the BJP is pushing for Ravneet Bittu as its candidate. The seat has been represented by Bittu’s grandfather, former chief minister Beant Singh, in the past.Kartarpur also figures among the constituencies the BJP is keen to take from the SAD. Former SAD MLA Avinash Chandar, a follower of Dera Sachkhand Ballan, is eyeing the seat, which has a sizeable Ravidassia voter base.In the Malwa belt, the saffron party is looking to secure Bathinda Urban, Barnala, Mansa, Khanna and Sahnewal, citing the presence of a large number of Hindu voters.Bathinda Urban is considered a Badal family stronghold. However, in the 2024 LS polls, the BJP got more votes in the assembly segment than the SAD candidate and present MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal. SAD candidate Sarup Chand Singla had won this seat twice before joining the BJP.The BJP is also claiming Khanna and Sahnewal in Ludhiana district as well. In Sahnewal, the BJP had secured over 41,000 votes, while in Khanna, the party is eyeing the seat because of the presence of the business community and the Hindu urban electorate.The saffron party is also expected to get Patiala Urban and has sought Sanaur and Samana seats for sitting MLAs Chetan Jauramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra. Both are sitting AAP MLAs who recently joined the BJP, the leaders said.“The seat-sharing issue will come up in talks when the joint panel of both the parties is announced. The BJP wants to play a larger role in the alliance and is keen to test its support base. There is no denying that the BJP’s vote share has improved, and it is putting in efforts to expand its base. The joint panel will ultimately take the final call on seat-sharing,” the leader said.

headline: Civic body re-elections today, political heavyweights face test
content: With 1.49 lakh voters set to decide the fate of 165 candidates in 30 wards of the Municipal Corporation (MC), Patiala, on Saturday, the stage is set for a keen electoral battle, with the prestige of several political heavyweights at stake.While the district administration has made elaborate arrangements to ensure free, fair and peaceful polling, intense contests in several wards have added to the political significance of the civic elections. The district administration is all set to conduct polling in 30 wards on November 28, Election Observer Senu Duggal said on Friday.The randomisation of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for 123 polling booths was conducted under her supervision in the presence of returning officers and other civil and police officials. ADC (Rural Development)-cum-Additional District Election Officer Sunil Phogat, SP (City) Mohit Aggarwal and representatives of various political parties were also present.Phogat said polling would be held in Ward No. 1, 4, 6, 12, 14, 15, 16, 22, 26, 28, 32, 33, 34, 36, 37, 38, 40, 41, 43, 44, 45, 46, 48, 50, 51, 52, 53, 55, 57 and 58, following the Supreme Court’s directions.A total of 1,49,768 voters, including 77,419 men, 72,338 women and 11 third-gender voters, are eligible to exercise their franchise.As many as 165 candidates, including 45 Independents, are in the fray. The administration has put in place arrangements for smooth polling and peaceful conduct of the elections.On the political front, Ward 38 has emerged as one of the major battlegrounds. AAP has fielded Yuvraj Juneja, son of PRTC Chairman Harpal Juneja, while BJP’s Rukatsha Bansal and Congress’ Dr Karamjit Dhillon are also in the contest. Harpal Juneja and Mayor Kundan Gogia have been campaigning extensively for the AAP candidate in this ward.The Ward No. 40 is witnessing a close contest between AAP’s Sanjeev Kakkar and BJP candidate Anuj Khosla. The ward remained in the spotlight during the campaign following allegations by rival parties that watches and women suits (dresses) having been distributed to woo voters.In Ward No. 34, AAP has again fielded District Planning Board Chairman Tejinder Mehta after his previous poll victory was cancelled by the apex court. He is facing a strong challenge from BJP candidate Sushil Nayyar in the civic polls.The electoral fortunes of former Senior Deputy Mayor Harinder Kohli in Ward 28 and former Deputy Mayor Jagdeep Jagga in Ward No. 12 were also at stake. Kohli faces a challenge from SAD candidate Amarjit Singh Bathla, while Jagga is up against BJP’s Shamsher Singh and an SAD candidate. Jagga has been campaigning by travelling in an auto-rickshaw.The outcome will also be significant for other ruling party AAP candidates, including Jasbir Gandhi (Ward No. 6), Ranjit Singh (Ward No. 32), Meenakshi Kashyap (Ward 43) and Jyoti (Ward No. 45).For the political parties, the verdict of these polls will serve as a test of their organisational strength and voter connect ahead of the larger electoral battle Assembly elections due by March next year.

headline: Ferozepur teacher turns home into museum, makes it to record books
content: At a time when music libraries have shifted to smartphones and streaming platforms, a primary school teacher from Lalchhian village in this border district is holding on to a world that many have forgotten.Karanveer Singh Sodhi (37) has turned his home into a fascinating museum, preserving more than 55,000 old Punjabi and Hindi music cassettes, along with vintage television sets, tape recorders, cast-iron griddles and other objects that offer a glimpse into a bygone era.Talking to The Tribune, Karanveer said his fascination with collecting old objects began in childhood. Whenever he came across something unusual or old, he would preserve it. Initially, he visited scrap shops in search of discarded items and bought anything that caught his attention. Gradually, this childhood hobby turned into a passion, prompting him to set up a museum at his home in 2016.Over the years, he has painstakingly built a collection of rare objects, purchasing old cassettes, griddles and other articles whenever he comes across them. His collection has now become a major attraction, drawing visitors from far-off places. Even people from abroad have shown keen interest in exploring his unusual museum.“Several people approached me seeking old objects from my collection for use in films and music videos. Some of them even offered me handsome amounts in return. However, I never accepted any such offer,” Karanveer said, adding that he would be deeply hurt if any of the articles were damaged or lost after being taken away.Karanveer believes old objects are not merely discarded belongings but carry memories of a particular era, reflecting its culture, music and lifestyle. Through his collection, he wants younger generations to experience and understand a world that existed before the digital age.His dedication to preserving this heritage has also earned him recognition, with his name finding a place in the London Book of World Records. For Karanveer, the museum is not just a collection of old things but a treasure trove of memories that he hopes to preserve for generations to come.

headline: Fazilka youths don police uniforms in Canada
content: Two youths with roots in the sleepy sub-tehsil of Arniwala have brought laurels to their native town and Fazilka district by joining police forces in Canada, inspiring local youth aspiring to build careers abroad.Neeraj Singh, a native of Arniwala, has earned a place in the prestigious Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) as a police officer after completing a rigorous recruitment process and training at the RCMP Academy in Regina, Saskatchewan. His achievement is particularly remarkable given the challenges he faced during childhood.Sarbjit Kaur, Neeraj’s mother, said he was just four years old when his father separated from the family. Despite financial and personal hardships, she single-handedly raised him and ensured he received a quality education.Neeraj moved to the UK in 2009 to pursue higher studies and obtained a master’s degree in International Business and Management from the University of Bedfordshire. After working with multinational companies, he relocated to Canada in 2019. Following the loss of his job as a property agent in 2023, he decided to pursue his long-cherished dream of joining police force.The RCMP selection process took nearly 18 months. Neeraj credits his wife’s unwavering support and encouragement, along with the motivation provided by their young son, for helping him overcome the challenges along the way. He eventually completed the demanding training programme and earned the RCMP badge.In another achievement for the region, Gurpreet Singh, whose family hails from Arniwala and is now settled in Amritsar, has joined the Toronto Police Service after completing his training.Gurpreet is the grandson of Dr Balbir Singh Sekhon, a retired Border Security Force (BSF) personnel, while his father, Harbans Singh, serves as a Sub-Inspector in the Punjab Police.The Sekhon family has a long tradition of service in the security forces, with more than 10 members currently serving in the police and armed forces. Gurpreet’s induction marks the continuation of this legacy into the fourth generation. He was recruited in June this year.The successful completion of his training recently sparked celebrations in the family, with relatives distributing sweets, beating drums and performing bhangra to mark the occasion.

headline: Studies hit as 70K Punjab teachers assigned Census duties
content: The deployment of nearly 70,000 government schoolteachers for Census 2027 duties across Punjab is set to disrupt academic activities in government primary, middle and senior secondary schools for the next 45 days, with teachers being asked to divide their working hours between classrooms and door-to-door enumeration.With the exercise scheduled from November 25 to January 9, 2027, nearly 60 per cent of the state’s 1.30 lakh government schoolteachers are reportedly being involved in the Census-related work, raising concerns over the availability of teaching staff and the likely impact on students’ studies.An official communication issued by the District Education Officer (Secondary), Faridkot, on November 25 directs school heads to ensure that teachers appointed as Census enumerators and supervisors perform half-day duties in schools and spend the remaining half of the day on Census work. The arrangement is intended to ensure that both academic activities and Census-related assignments continue simultaneously.However, teachers say the arrangement is impractical in several cases, particularly when their schools and assigned census areas are located far apart. A teacher posted in a village around 30 km from Faridkot town, for instance, has been asked to complete school duties by 12.15 pm and begin Census work in Faridkot from the same time. Reaching the assigned area within the stipulated time is practically impossible, a teacher pointed out.The scale of deployment is evident in Pucca village of Faridkot, where five of the nine teachers posted at the government primary school have reportedly been assigned Census duties. This leaves only four teachers to manage the entire student strength and academic workload.In Faridkot district alone, around 1,600 teachers are estimated to have been deployed for the exercise. Each enumerator has reportedly been assigned a target of covering 190 to 200 households, involving door-to-door visits and collection of household details.Teachers’ organisations fear that the arrangement will effectively deprive students of regular classroom teaching for nearly one-and-a-half months. They argue that even if teachers are technically required to attend school for half a day, the time spent travelling to their assigned Census areas, conducting household surveys and completing related formalities will leave little scope for maintaining normal academic activities.“Punjab has around 1.30 lakh government schoolteachers, of whom nearly 70,000 have been assigned Census duties. The biggest casualty of this arrangement will be students, who will be left without adequate teachers for almost one-and-a-half months,” said Mohinder Singh Kaurianwali, general secretary of the Democratic Teachers’ Front, Punjab.He said teachers were already burdened with several non-teaching assignments, including election duties and other government surveys and administrative exercises. Repeated deployment of teaching staff for such activities was adversely affecting classroom teaching, he added.The teachers’ union has questioned how schools, particularly those in rural areas already facing staff shortages, will manage their academic schedules when a substantial proportion of their teaching strength is engaged in Census work.The official communication from the district Census authorities acknowledges the need to maintain both school functioning and Census operations, but teachers say the half-day arrangement does not adequately address the practical difficulties.

headline: Woman dies after son burns her alive over money demand in Haryana
content: JHAJJAR: Police have arrested a man for allegedly setting his mother on fire in Bagpur village under the jurisdiction of Beri police station in Jhajjar district. The woman, identified as Bimla, later succumbed to her burn injuries while undergoing treatment at PGIMS Rohtak.The accused has been identified as Sumit, a resident of Bagpur village. Beri police station SHO, Sub-Inspector Yogesh Kumar, said the case was being investigated thoroughly under the direction of DCP Dharna Yadav.Police received information about Bimla suffering burn injuries on November 26, 2026, following which a police team reached the hospital. During the proceedings, Chetan, a resident of Bagpur and Bimla's nephew, lodged a complaint alleging that Sumit had assaulted his aunt and set her on fire.Based on the complaint and medical report, a case was registered against the accused at Beri police station. After Bimla died during treatment at PGIMS Rohtak, Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), pertaining to murder, was added to the case.Police arrested Sumit and questioned him. During interrogation, the accused allegedly took investigators to his house in Bagpur village and identified the spot where the incident had taken place. He also got the matchbox allegedly used in the crime recovered from his kitchen. Police seized it following the prescribed procedure.Investigators said preliminary findings indicated that the accused was addicted to intoxicants and frequently demanded money from family members. He allegedly committed the crime after his family refused to give him money.The accused was produced before a court in Jhajjar, which remanded him to judicial custody.

headline: Saharanpur Showdown: For Congress MP Imran Masood It's Both Personal And Political
content: Saharanpur connects four states. The northernmost district of Uttar Pradesh shares its borders with Haryana to the west, Uttarakhand to the north and east, and Himachal Pradesh to the north. Haryana and Uttarakhand, interestingly, do not share a direct border with each other. Saharanpur is the geographical link between the two. The district that connects has today become the source of the biggest disconnect between two INDIA bloc allies - the Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP). Seat-sharing talks between the two parties have hit a deadlock after the SP announced five candidates, including two from Saharanpur, where the Congress was hoping to contest. The SP has named candidates for the Saharanpur and Behat Assembly constituencies, renominating its sitting MLAs. Congress MP Imran Masood had his eyes on these seats as part of his effort to expand his influence in the Western UP region. Of the district's seven Assembly seats, the BJP won five in 2022 - Deoband, Gangoh, Nakur, Rampur Maniharan (SC) and Saharanpur Nagar - while the SP won the remaining two, Behat and Saharanpur.

headline: Woman killed during celebratory firing at her brother's wedding in Haryana's Jhajjar
content: Chandigarh | A 30-year-old woman was killed in celebratory firing at her brother's wedding in Bahadurgarh in Haryana's Jhajjar district, police said on Saturday. The incident took place on Thursday night when Manisha and other relatives were dancing during the 'Ghurchari' ceremony before the wedding procession at Kuber Colony. The groom's friend Deepak, a resident of Jhajjar, allegedly fired a few rounds in celebration and one of the bullets hit her head. Manisha was rushed to a hospital where she was declared brought dead. Manisha, a resident of Rewari, had come along with her husband and two children to attend the marriage of her brother. Following the incident, Deepak fled from the spot. Station House Officer Sector-6 police station Satyavir said Deepak has been arrested. Police said Deepak had a licensed weapon. An FIR was registered under relevant Sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Arms Act, they said

headline: Haryana’s anaemia battle far from over as 1 in 2 women, nearly 4 in 10 adolescent girls and 1 in 3 young
content: GURGAON: One in two women of reproductive age in Haryana continues to be anaemic, while nearly four in 10 adolescent girls and one in three young children are also affected, according to a new national nutrition survey.The findings point to a persistent public health challenge even as the state govt highlights a substantial improvement in anaemia estimates since the previous National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5).Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition between 2023 and 2025, found that 51.4% of women aged 15-49 years who were neither pregnant nor lactating were anaemic. The prevalence was 38.1% among adolescent girls aged 10-19 years and 34.1% among children aged 12-59 months.The Haryana health department, in a press note issued on Nov 27, described the findings as evidence of substantial improvement since NFHS-5, conducted in 2019-21. It cited a fall in anaemia prevalence among children under five from 70.4% to 34.1%, adolescent girls from 62.3% to 38.1%, adolescent boys from 29.9% to 18.2%, women aged 15-49 years from 60.4% to 51.4%, and men from 19% to 14.7%."We have intensified efforts under the 100-day Anaemia Prevalence Reduction Campaign as part of Anaemia Mukt Bharat. The campaign focuses on screening, testing, treatment, iron and folic acid supplementation, dietary counselling and inter-departmental coordination," an official from Haryana health department told TOI.However, these comparisons need to be interpreted with caution because the surveys did not use identical age categories. NFHS-5 covered children aged six-59 months, while SAMPADA covered those aged 12-59 months. For adolescents, NFHS-5 used the 15-19 age group, while SAMPADA covered 10-19 years. The male age categories also differ. The figures therefore show a decline in reported estimates but are not a strictly like-for-like measurement of change in the same population.SAMPADA, which covered more than two lakh individuals across 183 districts in 35 states and Union territories, analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples. SAMPADA also applied the World Health Organization's 2024 haemoglobin cut-offs, specific to age, sex and physiological status.Haryana's estimates were below the national average across all nine age and sex categories reported in the SAMPADA state annexure. Among females aged 15-49 years, the national prevalence was 55.9%, compared with 51.4% in Haryana. Among adolescent girls, it was 46.3% nationally against 38.1% in Haryana.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. headline: Whistleblower Protection in India: A Law Stalled Since 2014
content: ANTI-CORRUPTION On October 27, when Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer Sanjiv Chaturvedi asked the Supreme Court, through an additional affidavit in a petition pending since 2012, to take up the non-operationalisation of the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, he did so on the basis of his own harrowing experience as a whistleblower. https://frontline.thehindu.com/social-issues/social-justice/supreme-court-expansion-2026/article71312532.ece Chaturvedi’s is a case study highlighting the urgent need for a law to protect whistleblowers. As described in detail in his petition before the Supreme Court and corroborated by various independent authorities, including judicial forums, his is a tale of a whistleblower who took on the establishment, exposing corruption and violations of norms, but paid for it dearly in the form of a series of retaliatory actions taken against him by the state. According to the sequence of events detailed in the petition, Chaturvedi’s travails began in 2007, when the 2002-batch IFS officer was posted as Divisional Forest Officer in Kurukshetra, Haryana. He had objected to the felling of trees and the movement of heavy machinery in the Saraswati Wildlife Sanctuary by contractors of the Irrigation Department, insisting that the Supreme Court’s order of February 14, 2000, which made the court’s prior permission mandatory for such work, be followed. This was the starting point of Chaturvedi’s troubles with the powers that be. On May 30, 2007, he was transferred out of Kurukshetra, and on August 3, 2007, he was placed under suspension. His suspension, however, was overturned by the President on January 3, 2008. Over the next five years, Chaturvedi was issued 12 posting orders, two major-penalty charge sheets were initiated against him, his Annual Performance Appraisal Report (APAR) was downgraded, and the State government delayed relieving him for Central deputation. He faced criminal cases and a vigilance complaint, which were later closed by the State’s own investigators. On June 29, 2012, Chaturvedi joined his posting at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi, where he was designated Deputy Secretary and sent on Central deputation. This came after the Haryana government had declined to relieve him for the deputation. The officer approached the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), which granted him interim protection, and finally, the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) relieved him directly on the directions of the Department of Personnel and Training. In August 2015, his cadre was changed from Haryana to Uttarakhand after he sought the change on grounds of extreme hardship and threat to life. https://frontline.thehindu.com/environment/controversy-will-the-new-cec-be-able-to-protect-indias-forests-forest-conservation-act-amendments-supreme-court-moefcc/article67295803.ece The 51-year-old Chaturvedi is presently posted as Chief Conservator of Forests and Director, Uttarakhand Forestry Training Academy, in Haldwani, Nainital district. We want to enlarge the scope of the Act' We want to enlarge the scope of the Act' story We want to enlarge the scope of the Act' Prithviraj Chavan: Ministry is trying to sensitise different sections of society about how the RTI Act functions."-G.P. SAMPATH KUMAR 20100910271801001.jpg In July 2015, Chaturvedi was named a winner of the Ramon Magsaysay Award, with the award foundation noting the anti-corruption stance he took while in Haryana and later at AIIMS, and stating, “Chaturvedi is not a circumstantial whistleblower, but one genuinely seeking to reform the system from within.” Since 2007, the IFS officer has approached the President, the CAT, the State Information Commission, the Central Information Commission (CIC), three High Courts, and the Supreme Court to seek protection against reprisals. The President issued orders on four occasions to overturn action taken against him by the Haryana government. The action included his suspension in 2007; a charge sheet for major penalty proceedings in 2007; a second charge sheet, again involving major penalty proceedings, issued in 2012 and quashed in 2013; and the downgrading of his APAR for 2010-11 and 2011-12. Findings in his favour Independent authorities that examined his case, including judicial bodies, supported Chaturvedi. They agreed that he faced acute harassment and emphasised the need for an independent investigation into the issues he raised with regard to his victimisation and the corruption and other wrongdoing that he had highlighted. A two-member inquiry committee was set up by the MoEF in response to a communication from the Cabinet Secretariat on September 1, 2010, after Chaturvedi approached the Cabinet Secretary. In its report dated December 8, 2010, the committee noted: “This is a case which shows the level of degradation that has crept into our administrative system. In the said case, a junior officer of an All India Service was harassed through all the means available with the concerned authorities of the State Government, which include frequent transfers, long spells without posting, arbitrary suspension, issuing a fabricated charge-sheet, keeping the charge-sheet pending for long period to stall the promotion, registration of false cases, spoiling the ACR, etc., only for doing his statutory duties.” It further said: “On the basis of the available documents, it is proved beyond doubt that the only cause for the harassment of the officer was his stand in protecting a Wild Life Sanctuary against destruction from powerful contractors opposing the illegal expenditure of public funds to create private assets on the private land of politically influential persons in the name of development of the Herbal Park and exposing large scale financial irregularities in plantation projects, funded by the Central Government, as well as International Donor Agencies.” In August 2014, the MoEF sought a report from the Intelligence Bureau (IB) to assess the threat to Chaturvedi after he sought a change of cadre from Haryana. The IB’s findings, as recorded in the ministry’s file, read: “…there appears to be truth in the contention of Sh. Sanjiv Chaturvedi regarding alleged harassment meted out to him by Haryana Government. His request for change of cadre from Haryana to Uttarakhand merits consideration.” Chaturvedi approached the CIC when the IB refused to give him a copy of the report. On April 21, 2016, the commission concluded: “It is factually proved that appellant was put to extreme hardship by the corrupt political rulers and corrupt public servants in retaliation of his unstinted implementation of rule of law.” It also ordered the IB to provide the report to him. A single judge of the Delhi High Court dismissed the IB’s challenge to the CIC order in August 2017. In the IB’s appeal, a Division Bench directed the agency on July 27, 2023, and August 21, 2024, to produce the report, but according to Chaturvedi, those directions have so far not been complied with. The CAT’s Principal Bench in Delhi, ruling on May 6, 2015, on Chaturvedi’s application for a change of cadre, said that although the instances he had cited prima facie bore out extreme hardship and had been substantiated by the report of the MoEF’s two-member committee, it was refraining from going into the merits of the case because counsel for the respondents had not argued on them. It added: “We would also like to conclude here by stating that even without going into the merits of the case and only on the basis of a cursory reading, the instances of harassment cited appear to be on the extreme side and deserve to be taken serious note of.” Disputed CBI probe The Haryana government opposed an investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into the issues arising out of the Chaturvedi matter despite the Union government and the Central Vigilance Commission recommending it and the CBI also twice recording its willingness to take over the probe. In its report, the two-member committee had stressed the need for a CBI probe, especially because the role of top functionaries, including the Chief Minister, the Forest Minister, and senior bureaucrats, needed to be probed. Bhupinder Singh Hooda was the Chief Minister during the period in question, while Kiran Choudhry was the Forest Minister. https://frontline.thehindu.com/politics/lok-sabha-election-2024-bjp-social-engineering-challenges-hooda-dynasty-hold-on-haryana/article68001430.ece Chaturvedi approached the Supreme Court in November 2012, seeking a CBI probe into the harassment meted out to him and the scams and wrongdoing highlighted by him during his stint in Haryana. However, the Haryana government approached the Punjab and Haryana High Court, challenging the committee’s report, which formed the bedrock of Chaturvedi’s plea before the apex court. A single judge of the High Court dismissed the State government’s plea as not maintainable on August 13, 2019, holding that a dispute between the Centre and a State fell within the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction under Article 131 of the Constitution. A review petition filed by the State was dismissed by the High Court on March 3, 2020. The missing file Meanwhile, the file noting on the State government’s decision on the opinion of the Additional Advocate General, Haryana, who had recommended withdrawal of the State’s petition before the High Court, went missing. Chaturvedi had filed an application under the Right to Information (RTI) Act for the file noting on March 1, 2018, before the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), Haryana. The file came to the Forest Branch from the CMO without the original noting, with the Secretary, Forests, directing on April 25, 2018, that an FIR be registered if it was not found. However, only a lost article report was lodged by the custodian, Superintendent Rajinder Singh Chhillar, on May 21, 2018. Chhillar was transferred out of the Forest Branch on June 13, 2018. In a written submission to the Additional Chief Secretary and Financial Commissioner, Revenue, on December 5, 2018, he claimed that he had received threatening calls from some State government officials, had been transferred shortly thereafter, and had been issued a major charge memorandum over the lodging of the lost article report. Chhillar retired on January 9, 2019. He died on October 23, 2020, aged 59, with his dues remaining unpaid, according to Chaturvedi’s filing. His plea before the top court says that the sequence of events leading up to Chhillar’s death itself calls for an independent investigation. The reliefs sought by the IFS officer from the Supreme Court include a direction to the CBI to investigate, under the court’s monitoring, the retaliatory actions taken against him since 2007; the irregularities and corruption highlighted by him during his stint in Haryana; the circumstances in which the State persisted with its petition in the Punjab and Haryana High Court despite the Additional Advocate General advising its withdrawal; and the transfer, charge-sheeting, and death of Chhillar. The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear the matter next on December 10. A law in limbo Chaturvedi’s plea highlights the gap that exists for whistleblowers like him in the institutional framework because the Whistle Blowers Protection Act has been in a state of limbo for 12 years since its enactment. Chaturvedi has sought from the court an expansion of the scope of his writ petition to convert it into redressal of an issue of constitutional importance, which is the failure of the government to operationalise the whistleblowers law. The plea says the delay is “…resulting in incessant misery of Petitioner and many other similarly placed whistleblowers”. The plea argues that Chaturvedi’s record is itself a conclusive indictment of the absence of whistleblower protection. “This continuity of institutional persecution in the absence of any protective framework is not an exceptional case—it is the systemic norm. The absence of the Whistle Blower Protection Act’s operational framework means there is no single institutional mechanism to which a whistleblower in the Petitioner’s position can turn for protection, and no authority charged with the specific task of preventing and investigating retaliation,” it said. Describing the non-implementation of the law as a “structural vacuum”, the plea said the relief sought is not merely personal but systemic. It urged the court to intervene under Article 142 of the Constitution, along with the powers available under Article 32, to frame and issue appropriate directions to the Union government “for creating an effective mechanism for protection and incentivisation of whistleblowers, till the time the present statutory vacuum is filled up by way of notification of statutory rules”. Chaturvedi’s plea also urges the court to direct the Union government to bring the law into force forthwith. Enacted, then stalled The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in 2014 against the backdrop of public furore over growing instances of persecution of whistleblowers, including violence against them and many of them even losing their lives. The two cases most notable in this regard are those of Satyendra Dubey, an engineer working with the National Highways Authority of India, who was murdered in Gaya, Bihar, in November 2003 after he exposed corruption in the Golden Quadrilateral Project; and Manjunath Shanmugam, a sales officer with the Indian Oil Corporation, who was killed in Uttar Pradesh in November 2005 after he cracked down on adulteration of fuel. In Dubey’s case, a special CBI court convicted three men in 2010 of killing him during a robbery, an account his family disputed. The Act provides a framework for reporting corruption or wilful misuse of power or criminal offences by any public servant, while safeguarding whistleblowers. It has provisions for the protection of whistleblowers against victimisation, witness protection, and a penalty for revealing the identity of the complainant. It prohibits anonymous complaints. The Whistle Blowers Protection Bill was debated and passed by the Lok Sabha on December 27, 2011, and by the Rajya Sabha on February 21, 2014. It received the President’s assent on May 9, 2014. It was published in the Gazette of India on May 12, 2014. However, the law remains non-operational because under sub-section (3) of Section 1 of the Act, its provisions shall come into force on such date as the Central government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and the government has made no such notification so far. The Union government’s explanation, as provided in replies to questions in Parliament, is that the notification has not been made because the Act requires amendments “aimed at safeguarding against disclosures affecting sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, etc.”, before it is brought into force. To make these amendments, the government introduced a Bill in the Lok Sabha on May 11, 2015, which the House passed on May 13, 2015. It was then sent to the Rajya Sabha. However, the Bill lapsed upon the dissolution of the 16th Lok Sabha. Activists fault governments Transparency rights activists decry this delay in the implementation of the law, saying it exposes a lack of intent on the part of the Narendra Modi government to set up an institutional framework that supports and protects anti-corruption activists. The scam story: When proof rests in the polls The scam story: When proof rests in the polls The March 27 Delhi special court acquittal in a coal allocation case revives questions about a decade-old corruption narrative that shaped elections but struggled to meet judicial standards of proof. PERSPECTIVE The scam story: When proof rests in the polls storyline 1 “It is a complete lack of will on the part of the government to give effect to a law passed by Parliament. The present regime does not even want to comprehend the possibility that there is corruption happening and that there are people who are conscientious, public-spirited and who want to blow the whistle on corruption,” said Venkatesh Nayak, Director, Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative (CHRI), India. Nayak also criticised the opposition-ruled States for not bringing in laws at the State level to protect whistleblowers. “There is nothing that prevents the opposition-ruled states, particularly those under the Congress, because it was the UPA [United Progressive Alliance] government which brought the law, from enacting their own laws to protect whistleblowers with regard to matters that concern the affairs of the State government,” he said. According to CHRI’s documentation of attacks on RTI users, around 500 attacks on transparency activists have been reported since the RTI law came into force in 2005, with over 100 activists killed. “The lives of whistleblowers are so vulnerable. I am reminded of the murder of RTI activist Satish Shetty. He was killed in Pune, Maharashtra, on January 13, 2010. He had requested police protection because he had exposed major land scams near the Pune-Mumbai highway. The police did not take cognisance, and he was killed in broad daylight,” said senior journalist and RTI activist Vinita Deshmukh. About Chaturvedi’s plea before the top court, Deshmukh said: “I am so happy to know that an honest civil servant has gone ahead and filed this petition for the larger good of all whistleblowers in the country. I really hope the court intervenes in the matter and gives orders for the setting up of an institutional mechanism for whistleblowers.” In the meantime, new chapters have been added to Chaturvedi’s story, as he has had run-ins with the establishment even during his tenure at AIIMS and also in the assignments given to him in Uttarakhand, as he took a stance against corruption and insisted on norms being followed. There have also so far been 17 recusals by judges and tribunal members in litigation involving him. Two Supreme Court judges—Justices Ranjan Gogoi and U. U. Lalit—who later went on to become Chief Justice of India, recused themselves from hearing Chaturvedi’s petition in the top court in 2013 and 2016, without recording any reasons. Chaturvedi’s ordeal provides an apt case for the Supreme Court to intervene on the need for a law to protect whistleblowers.

headline: Police suspect mistaken identity in killing of 24-year-old youth during Rohtak dhaba shooting
content: Two days after a gang-related shootout at Milan Dhaba near Kharawar on the Delhi-Rohtak highway claimed four lives, preliminary police investigations have suggested that a 24-year-old youth with no criminal antecedents was killed after being mistaken for a member of a rival gang. The youth was reportedly chased upstairs by armed assailants and shot multiple times while attempting to escape the indiscriminate firing.The victim, Naveen alias Himanshu, was a resident of Beri in Jhajjar district. The other three victims were identified as Rinku (28), Vineet alias Vinny (22) and Yash alias Ganju, also known as Harsh (22), all residents of Dighal village in Jhajjar.According to police, the three men from Dighal had criminal cases registered against them and were allegedly associated with the Sunny Ritolia faction. Sunny Ritolia, believed to be the principal target of the attack, managed to escape.Sampla deputy superintendent of police (DSP) Rishi Kant said Himanshu had no criminal record. However, preliminary investigations revealed that he had shaken hands with the other men at their table. His association with the deceased or any criminal gang has not yet been established, and the matter remains under investigation.According to family members, Himanshu had visited Bhaloth village, where his sister was married, to help with agricultural work on nearby fields. After attending a wedding function, he went to the dhaba around midnight to collect food for himself and his brother-in-law.At around 1am, at least five armed assailants entered the premises and opened indiscriminate fire. Himanshu reportedly ran upstairs in an attempt to save himself. The attackers followed him, mistaking him for Sunny Ritolia or one of his associates, and fired several rounds. He sustained eight bullet injuries and died on the first floor, the family said.Himanshu’s maternal uncle Omveer and other relatives maintained that he had no connection with any criminal gang and had never been involved in a police case. They said he had run upstairs only to save his life.Himanshu was the only son of farmer Rajbir. He had recently purchased a tractor and started helping his father with agricultural work. A BA student at Jat College, Rohtak, he aspired to join the armed forces, inspired by his grandfather, who had served in the army. He had cleared the physical recruitment test but failed the medical examination due to an ear-related problem. He was subsequently preparing for a clerk’s post.Police have registered a case and formed multiple teams to identify and arrest the assailants. CCTV footage shows the attackers entering the hotel, loading their weapons and chasing the victims.An Instagram account reportedly linked to the Himanshu Bhau gang has claimed responsibility for the attack, citing revenge for previous killings. Police are verifying the claim.Investigators are probing the incident against the backdrop of the longstanding rivalry between the Himanshu Bhau and Sunny Ritolia, alias Baba, gangs, which have roots in the Ritoli area of Rohtak. Further investigations are underway.

headline: Sugarcane prices satisfactory for farmers: Haryana agri minister
content: Agriculture and farmers welfare minister Shyam Singh Rana on Friday toned-down the ongoing protests against the state government over sugarcane state advised price (SAP) and said the prices decided by the government are satisfactory, but the farmers have every right to object.“There is a system in which the prices are decided in consultation with the union government like for other crops as well. Chief minister Nayab Singh Saini has given ₹430 and ₹450 for next season, which is satisfactory. Even if the farmers demand more, this is their right. If Punjab is giving ₹1 extra, this is due to the elections,” the minister told reporters in Karnal.Farmers have been protesting at sugar mills across the state, demanding ₹600 SAP and have stopped supplying the crop for crushing at the mills.Congress party led by former CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda will also stage a sit-in outside Shahabad sugar mill on December 1, while farmers will gherao the chief minister’s residence in Kurukshetra the next day.Rana was in Karnal to chair a meeting of the district public relations and grievance redressal committee at the panchayat bhawan.The meeting agenda included three old and 10 new complaints, of which 10 were resolved. Two old and one new complaint remained pending.Earlier in the day, he held a similar meeting at the auditorium of the Kaithal mini secretariat and heard a total of 11 complaints, both old and new.Eight of these complaints were resolved on the spot, while three were kept pending.

headline: Haryana BJP youth wing announces executive committee | Hindustan Times
content: The Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), Haryana, has announced its new state executive committee, comprising state office-bearers, executive members and district presidents.The appointments include four state vice-presidents, two state general secretaries, four state secretaries, a treasurer, heads of media and social media wings and IT coordinators. The appointments take effect immediately, said state BJYM president Akshit Dahiya.Among the appointed vice presidents are Rahul Mundhal (Bhiwani), Aditya Dhankar (Jhajjar), Hardik Kumar Diwan (Ambala), and Manish Raghav (Gurugram), while Mayank Nirmal (Gurugram) and Karan Goel (Faridabad) have been appointed as state general secretaries.Expressing gratitude to the party leadership for reposing faith in him once again, Aditya Dhankhar said he will discharge his responsibilities with utmost dedication, sincerity and commitment. He said his endeavour will be to strengthen the organisation and engage an increasing number of young people with the party.“We will work collectively to bring more and more young people into the organisation and strengthen the Yuva Morcha at every level,” Dhankhar said.

headline: AI-assisted cyberattack suspected in Haryana’s public fund siphoning | Hindustan Times
content: The alleged fraud involving over ₹100 crore in public funds siphoned from bank accounts linked to Haryana’s development and panchayat department has assumed a new dimension. This follows recent cybersecurity advisories issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) which warned of sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) assisted attacks targeting financial and government linked payment systems.Cyber experts from Haryana Police said AI-powered tools could have been used to identify vulnerabilities and gain unauthorised access to computer systems. Police investigation has so far identified 523 fraudulent bank accounts and 1,897 such transactions. Eight arrests primarily of those whose accounts were used to route the siphoned funds, have been made so far. Police officials have described them as four mule account holders and four mediators.Also Read: Noida call centre bust: 9 trafficked foreigners still missingPolice are also investigating the role of a private company “Austere Systems Ltd,” the technology service provider associated with the development and panchayats department’s payment portal, and the possible lack of due diligence on the part of the bank involved.Two recent advisories issued by the CERT-In highlighted the growing threat of AI-assisted cyberattacks in India, including attacks on financial institutions, government organisations, technology service providers and academic institutions.In a November 4 advisory, CERT-In warned about an AI-assisted threat actor identified as “Crafty Falcon” which has been targeting banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) organisations. The advisory said the cyber attackers used machine intelligence to identify targets and operate at high speed, exploiting payment and disbursement systems to carry out unauthorised financial transactions.The advisory also identified other AI driven offensive security tools, including ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI. These tools can automate different stages of a cyberattack, generate customised attack scripts and modify their techniques depending on how the targeted systems respond.Also Read: Haryana mandates tighter financial security checks after suspected cyberattack on panchayat department ERP systemIn a second November 20 advisory, CERT-In highlighted the use of AI-driven Agentic Offensive Frameworks in cyberattacks across different sectors. These AI powered frameworks were being used to scan computer networks for weaknesses, identify possible entry points, attempt credential attacks and gain unauthorised access to systems and data, CERT-In said.The case has also brought the role of Austere Systems which provided payment portal services to the Haryana development and panchayats department into focus. In its November 25 disclosure under regulation 30 of SEBI (listing obligations and disclosure requirements) Regulations to the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Austere Systems referred to an investigation into the reported transfer of approximately ₹74.70 lakh from six bank accounts of the Haryana development and panchayats department to a private company. It stated that it would cooperate with the investigating authorities and provide the required information and documents. In a subsequent disclosure on November 26, the company acknowledged providing payment portal services to the department and referred to media reports concerning an investigation involving approximately ₹100 crore across multiple accounts. The company stated that the matter was under investigation and that no final findings had been reached.Police officials investigating the case said the role of Austere Systems in operating and maintaining the payment portal, its access controls, and security arrangements were likely to be examined. “So will be the development and panchayats department’s supervision of the portal, authorisation of payments and reconciliation of bank accounts and role of Punjab National Bank (PNB) in account verification, transaction monitoring and execution of payment instructions,’’ said a police official. The police have been able to freeze an amount of over ₹25.20 crore so far, officials said.Meanwhile chief secretary Anurag Rastogi on Friday directed the information technology, electronics and communications department, National Informatics Centre (NIC) and departments to prepare a comprehensive list of government schemes involving financial disbursements. “Multidisciplinary committees comprising four to five members, including technology experts, NIC representatives, finance officials and senior administrative officers, will be constituted to examine these schemes and identify security gaps,” he said during a review of cyber security controls, digital payment infrastructure and cloud deployment.Rastogi said the assessment will cover digital payment platforms, technology service providers, software applications and their security audit records.Additional chief secretary, finance, Sudhir Rajpal said that the state’s financial operations exceed ₹2 lakh crore, making robust technological safeguards and continuous vigilance essential. Even brief lapses in digital security could expose government receipts and disbursements to significant risks, the finance secretary cautioned.

headline: Haryana approves additional Rs 1.70 crore for five healthcare projects in Karnal, Yamunanagar
content: Chandigarh: The Haryana govt has approved an additional Rs 1.70 crore for the construction of five healthcare facilities in Karnal and Yamunanagar districts, citing revised project costs and site-specific requirements.The additional allocation will facilitate the construction of three Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in Karnal district, a Sub-Health Centre (SHC) at Chamrori and a Block Public Health Unit (BPHU) at Pratap Nagar in Yamunanagar district.Health minister Arti Singh Rao said strengthening rural healthcare infrastructure was a priority of the state government, adding that improved facilities at the primary and block levels would ensure better access to healthcare closer to people's homes. She directed officials to maintain construction quality and adhere to completion timelines.According to the health department, revised estimates were submitted by the respective civil surgeons after being prepared by executive engineers of the Zila Parishads, taking into account site-specific requirements and updated cost assessments.The biggest additional allocation of Rs 57.30 lakh has been approved for PHC Uplana in Karnal. Similarly, PHC Jalmana's construction cost has been revised from Rs 4.3 cr to Rs 4.6cr. In Yamunanagar, the SHC at Chamrori will require an additional Rs 33.21 lakh, taking its estimated cost from Rs 55.50 lakh to Rs 88.71 lakh. The BPHU at CHC Pratap Nagar has received an additional Rs 5.85 lakh, with its revised cost pegged at Rs 55.85 lakh against the earlier approval of Rs 50 lakh.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Haryana Tightens Norms for Government College Faculty Travelling Abroad
content: Chandigarh, November 28: The Haryana Department of Higher Education has introduced streamlined verification protocols for government college teachers planning personal or official foreign travel, making a 30-day advance notice and complete documentation compulsory. Addressed to all government college principals on Friday, the directive from the Director General of Higher Education mandates strict adherence to the Finance Department’s norms dated October 15, 2025. Principals have been tasked with scrutinising every application thoroughly before sending their recommendations to the Directorate, with exemptions to the one-month timeline permitted only in unavoidable situations. Covering professors, associate professors, and assistant professors statewide, the directive addresses recurring procedural delays triggered by incomplete submissions reaching the headquarters. To secure clearance, teachers must submit an affidavit, a copy of their passport, complete leave details, and service history covering their initial government joining and current posting, alongside a declaration confirming the status of any pending complaints or inquiries.

headline: Petrol, diesel prices today: Check rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Noida and other cities on November 28
content: Petrol and diesel prices remained largely stable across major Indian cities on November 28, although Gurgaon and Noida recorded reductions in the prices of both fuels. Thiruvananthapuram, meanwhile, saw a marginal increase in diesel prices.According to data from Goodreturns, petrol prices in Gurgaon fell by ₹0.20 per litre to ₹102.77, while rates in Noida declined by ₹0.16 to ₹101.96. Diesel prices in both cities also came down, with Gurgaon recording a reduction of ₹0.20 to ₹95.44 per litre and Noida seeing a decline of ₹0.12 to ₹95.44.Diesel prices in Thiruvananthapuram increased marginally by ₹0.01 to ₹104.41 per litre.Petrol and diesel prices in major cities on Nov 28 Crude oil prices rise amid Middle East supply concernsInternational crude oil prices remained volatile as attacks on energy infrastructure and oil tankers in the Middle East heightened concerns about potential supply disruptions.According to Bloomberg, Brent crude fell around 1% to settle near $95 a barrel on Friday but still recorded a weekly gain. Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, located near the Red Sea coast, was attacked again by Iran-backed Houthi militants, days after the kingdom's Ras Tanura oil export hub on the Persian Gulf was targeted.Attacks on tankers and around the Strait of Hormuz have also continued as the Iran war entered its tenth month, raising questions about the sustainability of the recovery in Gulf oil shipments.The International Energy Agency (IEA) expects the global oil market to move into a surplus this quarter. However, persistent geopolitical tensions have kept supply concerns in focus."Traders are still focused on the escalation of Strait of Hormuz attacks, and that's keeping a bid under prices," Dennis Kissler, senior vice president for trading at BOK Financial Securities Inc., told Bloomberg.He added that oil volumes moving through and around the Strait of Hormuz continued to indicate the possibility of an oversupplied market.Traders are also monitoring an upcoming OPEC meeting, where the alliance is considering retaining its existing output quotas through January as members remain divided over sustainable production levels.Bloomberg also reported that diesel futures in Europe and retail fuel prices in the US have declined from peaks recorded earlier in the war, offering some relief to oil-product markets.High energy prices add ₹6-7 lakh crore to India's annual burdenRising international energy prices are also increasing India's import bill, given the country's continued dependence on imported crude oil and natural gas.Tarun Kapoor, adviser in the Prime Minister's Office, said high crude oil and natural gas prices have added an estimated ₹6-7 lakh crore annually to the financial burden on the Indian economy.Speaking at the 16th Energy Security Conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Kapoor called for a structural shift towards electric vehicles in both freight and passenger transportation to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels.He warned that India's heavy reliance on energy imports leaves the economy vulnerable to international price shocks.India imported 122.7 million tonnes (MT) of crude oil during the first half of the 2026-27 financial year, marginally higher than the 121.8 MT imported in the corresponding period a year earlier.

headline: Haryana banks on grassroots talent as 18,000 athletes gear up for Khel Mahakumbh
content: Chandigarh: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday unveiled the blackbuck-inspired mascot for the Khel Mahakumbh Haryana-2026, positioning the state-level sporting event as a platform to identify and groom grassroots talent, with 18,000 sportspersons set to compete in 30 disciplines across 11 cities.The mascot, inspired by Haryana’s state animal, is intended to symbolise agility, alertness, balance and determination—qualities govt says define the state’s sporting culture.The competitions will be held in two phases. Activities under the annual sports calendar began on Nov 16, with district-level selection trials already conducted across Haryana.Unveiling the mascot, Saini said the enthusiasm and sporting ability of Haryana’s youth remained the state’s greatest strength. He said the event would provide emerging athletes from villages, towns and smaller cities an opportunity to sharpen their skills and eventually represent the country in international competitions.During the event, the CM felicitated former India hockey captain Sardar Singh, Asian Games medallist Parveen Hooda and boxer Narender. Saini also extended his wishes to the junior hockey team leaving for Egypt.Highlighting govt’s sporting initiatives, Saini said 260 outstanding sportspersons had been provided Group A, B and C govt jobs under the state’s recruitment policy, while 17,676 athletes had received cash awards totalling Rs 931 crore over the last 12 years. Medal winners at international competitions are eligible for cash incentives of up to Rs 6 crore, he said.The state has established 2,000 sports nurseries, where around 40,000 children are training, and 25 residential sports academies offering diet assistance of Rs 500 per day. Around Rs 1,100 crore has been spent on sports infrastructure during the period, he said.A-STAR, an advanced scientific training and rehabilitation centre, has also been established at Panchkula’s Tau Devi Lal Sports Complex at a cost of around Rs 10 crore, the CM said.Saini cited Haryana’s contribution of 30 medals, including 14 gold, to India’s total haul of 85 medals at the Asian Games. The state’s para-athletes also won 31 medals, including nine gold, at the Asian Para Games.Sports minister Gaurav Gautam said the budget for the 2026 edition of Khel Mahakumbh had been doubled. He also highlighted ‘Mission Olympic-2036’, under which Haryana has set a target of winning 36 medals at the 2036 Olympics.Govt said its focus was on strengthening grassroots training, modern infrastructure and transparent athlete selection to sustain Haryana’s position as a leading contributor to India’s sporting achievements.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: CM Saini unveils mascot of Haryana Khel Mahakumbh
content: Chandigarh: As many as 18,000 sportspersons will showcase their talent across 30 sports disciplines during the state-level competitions of Khel Mahakumbh Haryana-2026, which will be organised in two phases across 11 cities of the state. Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday unveiled the mascot of Khel Mahakumbh Haryana-2026, inspired by the blackbuck, the state animal. The mascot symbolises Haryana’s identity and cultural heritage, as well as the agility, alertness, balance and determination of its sportspersons.Addressing sportspersons, Saini said their passion and enthusiasm were the state’s greatest strength and that Haryana consistently figured among the top performers in medal tallies. He said the Khel Mahakumbh would provide a major platform to budding sportspersons to hone their talent and bring laurels to the state.The chief minister said 2,000 sports nurseries had been established across Haryana, where around 40,000 children were undergoing training in morning and evening sessions. In addition, 25 residential sports academies had been established, where sportspersons were being provided diet money at the rate of Rs 500 per day.During the event, Saini said village grounds, school playgrounds and early training played a crucial role in the success of every sportsperson. Commenting on the mascot, the chief minister said the blackbuck was known for its remarkable speed, agility, alertness, balance and grace, qualities also reflected in Haryana’s sportspersons. Through the mascot, a message of environmental conservation, sensitivity towards wildlife and preservation of natural heritage was also being conveyed to the youth and people of the state.As per the annual sports calendar, activities under the Khel Mahakumbh commenced on November 16, and district-level selection trials were conducted across the state ahead of the state-level competitions.Saini said sports not only promoted physical fitness and mental concentration, but also kept youth away from social evils such as drug abuse.Sports infrastructure and incentivesThe chief minister said several significant steps had been taken over the past 12 years to strengthen sports infrastructure in Haryana. Under the Haryana Outstanding Sportspersons Recruitment Rules, 260 outstanding sportspersons had so far been provided Group A, B and C government jobs. He said sportspersons winning medals at international competitions, including the Olympic Games, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games, were awarded cash prizes of up to Rs 6 crore. Over the past 12 years, 17,676 sportspersons of the state had been awarded cash prizes amounting to Rs 931 crore.The CM said a monthly scholarship of Rs 1,500 was provided to sportspersons in the age group of 8 to 14 years and Rs 2,000 to those in the age group of 15 to 19 years.Haryana’s contribution to India’s medal tallySaini said Haryana’s sportspersons had consistently brought laurels to the country through their performances in international competitions. India secured fourth position at the Asian Games with 85 medals, of which Haryana’s sportspersons contributed 30. Of the 21 gold medals won by India, 14 were secured by sportspersons from Haryana.Similarly, India registered its best-ever performance at the Asian Para Games by winning 114 medals, of which Haryana’s para-athletes secured 31, including nine gold medals. At the Commonwealth Games, Haryana’s sportspersons won 11 of the 39 medals secured by the country. Sports Minister Gaurav Gautam said that under the leadership of Saini, the state government was working with the resolve to take Haryana’s sportspersons from soil to medals.He said the Khel Mahakumbh would witness the participation of 18,000 sportspersons across 30 disciplines, with competitions being held in 11 cities.Haryana CM honours Youth Olympic gold medallistCM Nayab Singh Saini on Friday honoured boxer Gunjan, a resident of Dhana Kalan village in Hansi, with a cash award of Rs 1 crore for winning a gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games 2026 in Dakar, Senegal. Gunjan won the gold medal in the 48 kg weight category. She had earlier secured silver medals at the 2026 U-19 Asian Boxing Championships in Jakarta, Indonesia, and the 2026 World Boxing Futures Cup in Bangkok, Thailand.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: BJP MP Harsh Mahajan Seeks Railway Survey for Pathankot-Chamba Rail Line
content: BJP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Harsh Mahajan has urged the Union Government to initiate a detailed feasibility survey for the proposed Pathankot-Chamba railway line and include the ambitious project in the Railways’ future development plans on a priority basis. In a letter to Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, Mahajan highlighted the lack of railway connectivity in Chamba district, describing it as one of the most remote and underdeveloped regions of Himachal Pradesh. He pointed out that despite being approximately 125 kilometres from Pathankot, Chamba remains disconnected from the railway network due to its challenging geographical terrain. Mahajan said extending railway connectivity from Pathankot to Chamba would be a historic step towards accelerating the district’s development and integrating the region with the national transport network. He stated that the proposed railway line would benefit the entire district, including Dalhousie, Khajjiar, Bharmour, Pangi, Churah and Bhatiyat. Improved connectivity would make it easier for tourists from across the country to visit these destinations, giving a significant boost to tourism and strengthening the local economy. The BJP MP further emphasised that the project would create new employment and self-employment opportunities for local youth while making travel to major cities across the country more convenient for residents. Highlighting Chamba’s natural beauty, rich historical and cultural heritage, religious tourism potential and strategic geographical importance, Mahajan said strengthening transport infrastructure was essential to bring the aspirational district into the mainstream of development.

headline: Six suspended after video of Class 9 student’s assault surfaces in Himachal’s Kinnaur
content: Shimla, Nov 28 (PTI) Six students have been suspended after a video showing a Class 9 student being assaulted in Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Reckong Peo, in Himachal Pradesh’s Kinnaur district surfaced, officials said on Saturday. The administration issued a show-cause notice to the school principal, and the role of the school management and the responsibility of teachers and wardens on duty at the time of the incident are also being examined, said Kinnaur Deputy Commissioner Sonakshi Tomar.
