headline: Thakur slams Sukhu govt’s 4 years in office
content: Shimla: Leader of the opposition in Himachal Pradesh assembly, Jai Ram Thakur, on Friday criticised the state govt for preparing to celebrate four years in office, alleging that the state was grappling with administrative failures, deteriorating public services and mounting financial distress.Thakur said govt had no justification for spending crores of rupees on celebrations when disaster-hit roads remained unrepaired and basic facilities were being withdrawn.He alleged that Post-Disaster Need Assessment (PDNA) funds meant for restoring damaged infrastructure were being misused to benefit govt’s favourites.Accusing the state govt of turning its ‘Sukh Ki Sarkar’ promise into a regime of charges, the LoP said even free X-ray facilities had been withdrawn from hospitals.More than 50,000 students have withdrawn from govt schools, while over 70% of essential medicines are unavailable in hospitals, he added.Thakur also flagged deteriorating law and order, citing murders, crimes against women, rape, extortion and thefts. He alleged that govt had failed to appoint a regular DGP and chief secretary.Questioning the proposed celebrations under the banner of ‘Vyavastha Parivartan’ (system change), he said the Congress high command should ask chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu what his govt had achieved in these four years. headline: Himachal to set up centre of excellence for apple cultivation
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh govt will establish a modern Centre of Excellence for apple cultivation to promote advanced horticultural technologies, improve productivity and increase orchardists’ income.Horticulture minister Jagat Singh Negi, while chairing a meeting with a technical delegation from New Zealand on Friday, said the proposed centre would provide high-quality, disease-free apple planting material developed on rootstocks. It would also facilitate the introduction of improved apple varieties, high-density plantation systems and modern cultivation techniques suited to changing climatic conditions.The centre would serve as a dedicated training facility to help orchardists from Himachal Pradesh and other states adopt advanced horticultural practices. Negi said the project would be implemented under the Centre’s Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), which would provide one-time financial assistance of Rs 15 crore. New Zealand experts would extend technical assistance in establishing the centre, technology transfer and its management.The state horticulture department would provide land, infrastructure, resources and staff. The minister directed officials to expedite the project so that production and distribution of quality apple planting material could begin from next year. He said the collaboration would bring advanced technologies to the state and strengthen its apple economy through better productivity and sustainable horticultural practices. The New Zealand delegation was led by Ishan Jayawardhana, lead adviser, ministry for primary industries, New Zealand High Commission. Secretary, horticulture, Sudesh Kumar Mokhta and other officials attended the meeting.

headline: Patients’ medical records to go digital under HMIS
content: Shimla: Patients’ medical records and reports will soon be accessible to doctors at the click of a button as Himachal Pradesh prepares to implement the Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) across health institutions.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said on Friday the state govt had approved the engagement of 661 junior office assistants (IT) data entry operators to ensure smooth implementation of HMIS and strengthen e-Governance initiatives in the health sector.Of these, 561 personnel will be deployed in the directorate of medical education and various govt medical colleges, while 100 will be engaged in other health institutions across the state, the CM added.Sukhu said the proposed deployment includes 100 posts each at Indira Gandhi Medical College, Shimla, and Dr Rajendra Prasad Govt Medical College, Tanda; 90 at Dr Radhakrishnan Govt Medical College, Hamirpur; 70 at Atal Institute of Medical Super Specialities, Chamiana; 61 at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Govt Medical College, Nerchowk; 50 each at medical colleges in Chamba and Nahan; 20 each at the directorate of medical education and Rajeev Gandhi Govt Dental College, Shimla.The personnel will handle HMIS operations, patient data management, e-Office, online correspondence, govt portals, e-salary work, recruitment-related activities and procurement through the govt e-Marketplace (GeM).The system will facilitate digitisation and efficient management of patient records, hospital information, data entry and report generation, improving transparency and accountability in healthcare delivery.Sukhu said the state govt was committed to modernising health institutions through adequate manpower, advanced technology and improved infrastructure, enabling people to access quality and specialised healthcare within the state.

headline: 114 posts vacant in Himachal jails, HC steps in
content: Shimla: Expressing concern over staff shortages in Himachal Pradesh prisons, Himachal Pradesh high court has directed that the issue of filling vacant posts in the prisons department be placed before the state-level monitoring committee constituted for overseeing the management of open correctional institutions.A division bench comprising Chief Justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhawalia and Justice Bipin Chander Negi observed that out of 769 sanctioned posts in the state’s jails, 114 were lying vacant. The biggest shortage was among male warders, with 70 posts vacant. The vacancies also include one post of deputy superintendent jail, two senior assistants, five junior office assistants (IT), six junior assistants clerks, three dispensers, two male head warders and four female head warders.Besides, two female warders, one male and one female social worker, two junior technicians (weaving masters), one TGT, one JBT, two peons, two turnkeys and two sweepers’ posts were vacant.The court was hearing a suo motu public interest litigation concerning vacancies in the prisons department. In its order, it referred to an affidavit filed on March 28, 2026, in compliance with its earlier order of Aug 14, 2025, when it had taken note of the vacancies. The court was informed about an earlier proposal to create 44 posts of various categories following the conversion of District Jail Mandi into a District and Open Air Women Jail, while the jail had subsequently been shifted to the newly constructed facility at Ner Chowk.However, the proposal was deferred following a letter dated Feb 6, 2024, from the special secretary (Home), citing the state’s financial situation. The court was further informed that the process of engaging a counsellor at Model Central Jail, Kanda, Shimla, was under consideration.Taking note of state govt’s notification dated March 25, 2026, constituting Himachal Pradesh Monitoring Committee for management of open correctional institutional setups, the bench said prison staff vacancies should also be placed before the committee for supervision and follow-up action. The case would now come up for next hearing on Feb 23, 2027.

headline: High Court in urgent need of additional infra: HC
content: Chandigarh: Observing that its functioning is “severely curtailed” due to inadequate infrastructure, the Punjab and Haryana high court said it is in “urgent need of additional infrastructure”. The court urged the Union govt to expedite action on its “Holistic Development Plan“ and warned that the administration of justice may suffer unless the plan is implemented.A division bench comprising Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Sanjiv Berry made the observations while hearing a petition filed by Vinod Dhatterwal, secretary of the Punjab and Haryana High Court Employees Association, seeking implementation of the plan.The Bench observed, “We are faced with a peculiar situation where the functioning of the Court is severely curtailed on account of lack of requisite infrastructure required for the efficient and smooth running of the Court. Though this Court has a sanctioned strength of 85 Judges, the Court Halls available as of now is much less. Space for Bar offices and parking facilities are all proving to be inadequate. The High Court is thus in urgent need of additional infrastructure.”The Holistic Development Plan envisages the construction of multi-storey buildings to meet the requirement for additional space.During the hearing, Additional Solicitor General of India Satya Pal Jain informed the court that a meeting had been convened at the level of the Union home secretary to discuss approval of the plan.Minutes of the meeting recorded that the Chandigarh administration would share the proposal with the govts of Punjab and Haryana, including details of expenditure-sharing among stakeholders, and seek their views. It also proposed obtaining high court views on the plan and convening another meeting on priority to finalise the future course of action.The Bench, however, observed, “We do not find any need for the administration to obtain the views of the high court when the project itself has been initiated under its provisions.”The court noted that the High Court is part of the Capitol Complex, which has been accorded UNESCO World Heritage Site status, and that development within the complex is subject to various limitations.It observed that “any proposed development has to be consistent with the concept of Le Corbusier, who had initially conceived the Capitol Complex”.The Bench said the Holistic Development Plan had been conceived and forwarded by the High Court in this context, following which it was processed and forwarded by the Chandigarh administration.On the issue of sharing expenditure, the court observed, “So far as the sharing of costs is concerned, appropriation of costs, as per the terms settled by the Union govt, will have to follow. These are aspects which can be taken note of and adequately addressed at the appropriate stage.”The court emphasised the need for expeditious action to ensure that the required infrastructure is made available at the earliest.The Bench also requested the Additional Solicitor General to personally meet the Union home secretary and impress upon the officer the need to take up the matter at the earliest.The matter has been listed for further hearing on Dec 11.

headline: Make mental health a priority: PU V-C
content: Chandigarh: Panjab University vice-chancellor Prof Tankeshwar Kumar expressed concern over the death of a UIET student and directed officials to focus on the well-being of hostel residents. headline: U'khand: Villagers threaten indefinite protest against relocation of Jageshwar sculptures to Delhi | Hindustan Times
content: Pithoragarh, Villagers in Uttarakhand's Almora district have threatened an indefinite protest at the Jageshwar Museum if the Archaeological Survey of India goes ahead with its proposed move to shift more than 274 ancient sculptures housed there to a museum under construction in Delhi.A large number of residents from surrounding villages gathered at the museum on Saturday after learning that an ASI team had arrived to collect the precious artefacts, and strongly opposed their relocation.The protesters warned the team that any attempt to remove the sculptures would trigger a public agitation, including an indefinite dharna at the museum entrance.Hari Mohan Bhatt, a priest at the Jageshwar temple, said villagers united in opposition as soon as they learnt about the ASI team's arrival to collect the sculptures.He said the residents had made it clear that they would launch an indefinite sit-in if the ancient artefacts were taken away.Naveen Bhatt, former vice-president of the Jageshwar Temple Committee, said they had written to the Director General of the ASI in Delhi, requesting that the sculptures not be relocated."If any law-and-order situation arises as a result of this public agitation, the department will be held responsible," he said.According to sources, the Jageshwar Museum houses more than 274 rare and ancient sculptures, including those of Lakulisha Shiva and 'Paun Raja'.Located around 35 km from Almora, Jageshwar Dham is a renowned complex of ancient temples dedicated to Lord Shiva in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand.The sculptures are proposed to be shifted to 'Yuge Yugeen Bharat', a museum being developed by the central government in Delhi's North and South Blocks. Once completed, it is set to be the largest museum of its kind in the world.Spread over one lakh square metres, the museum will showcase various facets of India's 5,000-year-old history, including architecture, urban civilisation, mathematics, astronomy, languages and scripts, religion, spirituality, as well as the country's trade and cultural ties.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Air in Delhi NCR: The future looks smoggy | Hindustan Times
content: After having lived and worked in Delhi NCR for 15 years, I relocated to a cleaner city earlier this year, a city which just had cleaner air. My professional experience and education gave me this privilege and, therefore, my family members and I could make this choice. However, not every citizen living in Delhi NCR has this luxury. For some, it is the lure of a lucrative job, quality education for children, ancestral home or just a sense of belonging to this city which has been the ‘melting pot’ of cultures and civilisations, a fortress everyone wanted control over. Ironically, many are now considering moving away from it as it is no longer ‘liveable’. For many in the smaller towns, it still remains the land of opportunities and supposedly a city which would provide a better quality of life. Little do people realise that this better life is dependent on air-conditioners in the summers and air purifiers during winters. If we factor in the health disorders, the opportunity cost, as also the cost of living in the capital city has clearly increased manifold. Article 21 of the Constitution of India provides for the right to life and personal liberty to every citizen of this country. This means every citizen has the right to live with dignity and this includes living in a clean and healthy environment, as laid down by the Supreme Court, through a number of its judgments. Not to forget, the citizens also have a fundamental duty under Article 51A(g) of Constitution of India to protect the environment. The directive principles of state policy under Article 48A provides that the state shall endeavour to protect the environment. While it is the duty of the citizens to live responsibly and ensure that they cause minimum damage to the environment, it is not just a duty but also an obligation of the state, that is the government, to ensure that it provides a clean and healthy environment to its citizens, as it is their fundamental right. If citizens have to move out of a city they once called home, our government has clearly failed to fulfil its obligation and responsibility. We look up to our elected representatives and our government, to ensure that they provide good living conditions to all the citizens. It is the responsibility of the state to ensure that the industries which are allowed to operate do so in a non-polluting manner. The statutory authorities like the Central Pollution Control Board and more importantly the state pollution control boards and the pollution control committees, like in Delhi, have to ensure that only non-polluting industries are allowed to operate. The environmental consents and clearances granted by the statutory authorities are all conditional and could be revoked by them whenever there is a violation of the prescribed emission standards and related norms. Even in the plethora of judgments passed by the Supreme Court and various high courts, a number of directions have been issued to the governments to prevent and curb air pollution but there has been minimal improvement on the ground. Especially for Delhi NCR, there have been numerous judgments passed by the high court and more importantly the Supreme Court but like always implementation is the challenge. If countries like China could solve their air pollution woes through strict emission caps, coal-to-gas/electric heating shifts, factory upgrades, public transit expansion, and stricter enforcement, why can’t we in India or Delhi NCR do it? We had EPCA earlier, which was replaced by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), a permanent statutory body constituted by the Central Government to solve the pollution crisis of NCR. CAQM was constituted in 2021 and in five years it is still struggling to find the cause of Delhi’s pollution. Probably, this is why it constituted a sub-committee in October this year to identify areas where pollution sources adversely affect air quality and also the major polluting activities in these areas. So many writs have been filed under Articles 226 and 32 of the Constitution of India. So many original applications have been filed before the National Green Tribunal (NGT). The Supreme Court, the high courts, the NGT keep passing judgments, the committees and authorities keep submitting reports and recommendations, the citizens keep filing writs but the ground reality remains unchanged. If the courts are also helpless, should the citizens stop paying taxes or should they just elect governments which shall be sensitive to the environment and make the national capital and the country clean and liveable? (The views expressed are personal) This article is authored by Nawneet Vibhaw, senior director and head, School of Law, UPES.

headline: MCD adds 10 mechanical road sweepers to Delhi fleet to curb dust pollution
content: New Delhi: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Friday (November 27) flagged off 10 mechanical road-sweepers (MRS) at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) headquarters, taking the civic body’s fleet to 76 from 66. The machines are the first 10 of a batch of 70 large MRS machines that the Delhi government had told the Commission for Air Quality Management would be deployed by the end of July to curb dust pollution. The remaining 60 machines are yet to be delivered and will be deployed in phases across the MCD’s 12 zones, taking its fleet to 136. Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa had told The Hindu in October that, after a prolonged delay, a work order had been issued for the 70 machines, with some expected to arrive by the end of November. Ms. Gupta said road dust is a major source of air pollution in Delhi, particularly during winter. “The inclusion of modern road-sweeping machines in the Corporation’s fleet is an important step towards strengthening the fight against pollution and improving dust control,” she said. The MCD currently cleans around 2,100 lane-kilometres of roads daily in an eight-hour shift. It has set a target of increasing this to 5,000 lane-kilometres a day once all the new machines are deployed, according to a press release. The machines flagged off on Friday comprise one CNG-powered sweeper, with a hopper capacity of more than four cubic metres, and nine electric machines, each with a capacity of two cubic metres. The MCD also launched five water tankers and four dust-dump vehicles to support the sweeping operations. Each of the new sweepers is expected to cover at least 40 lane-kilometres in a single shift. They are equipped with artificial intelligence and sensors that will enable the MCD control room to monitor their operating hours, distance covered and quantity of dust collected. The tender also provides for a 10-year maintenance arrangement. The expansion is part of a broader initiative to mechanise road cleaning in the city. First announced by the previous Aam Aadmi Party government on January 28, 2023, as part of its plan for the “world-class transformation” of Delhi’s roads, the project missed its initial deadlines. The Bharatiya Janata Party government, which came to power in February 2025, revived the project through a fresh Cabinet decision. Subsequent structural revisions, however, led to further delays. Air quality remains poor Delhi’s air quality remained in the ‘poor’ category on Friday, with the air quality index (AQI) settling at 226. Of the 57 monitoring stations that recorded data, two reported ‘very poor’, 41 reported ‘poor’ air quality and 14 reported ‘moderate’.

headline: A right swipe, a first date & a Rs 55,000 bill. The dating-app extortion trap lurking in Delhi cafés
content: New Delhi: A polyester banner hangs loosely over the glass entrance to a mall in Delhi’s Shahdara. It’s no advertisement; printed on the banner is a warning message that seems to draw attention with every gust of wind. Nobody really stops to read, but eyeballs swivel up to catch the words: “Be cautious if someone insists you meet at a cafe for a date. It may be a scam where you are forced to pay an inflated bill. Stay alert and avoid such situations.” A moment later, and inside the mall, the buzz from the packed pubs and cafes that largely make up its ground floor has drowned the already fading memories of the warning. It’s going to be business as usual, caution sign included. Shahdara is no standalone scam zone. Such caution signs have become commonplace in the bazars and bylanes of Delhi, for the latest dating app scam is an in-the-flesh version, where prospective online matches lure searching hearts to colluding cafes or pubs and run up massive bills. The desi cream on the cake is that such scams usually end in shouting matches, and, less frequently, public beatings delivered on the spot by the muscle department of the scamming side. ThePrint went across the Capital to social hotspots from where such scams have been reported—Hauz Khas, Cross River Mall and Karkardooma Community Centre—to find if these hair-raising tales are true. They are. “This has become a big issue, hence there are caution signs citywide. We want to warn the people, and want them to know that in case of such dating app scams, they can always report such issues without thinking they’ll be judged,” says a senior Delhi Police officer aware of the matter. Lonely at 26, Vishal Singh couldn’t but help downloading a popular location-based dating app one night. I wanted to find a companion, he says. “Sometimes it gets very lonely, and you want someone to share mundane things with. I tried dating apps earlier as well but it never seemed to work out,” says Singh.

headline: Delhi government spent 37.4% of budget in first 7 months of 2026-27
content: The Delhi government has so far spent 37.4% of its budgetary allocation for schemes and projects in the first seven months of the 2026-27 financial year, utilising ₹23,391 crore of the ₹62,550 crore set aside for planned expenditure by various departments, according to official data accessed by HT.The figures show wide variations in spending across departments, with some having used more than three-fourths of their allocations while others had barely begun utilising their funds.Also Read | Man stabbed to death after asking car occupants to drive slowly in Delhi's ShakurpurDepartment-wise breakdownThe department of industries recorded the lowest expenditure at ₹5.67 crore, or 2.07% of its ₹274-crore allocation. It was followed by labour and labour welfare, which spent ₹7.12 crore (7.66%) of its ₹93-crore allocation, and agriculture and allied services, which used ₹10.67 crore (10.46%) of its ₹102-crore budget.The Women and child welfare department had spent ₹776.67 crore, or 10.85% of its ₹7,161-crore allocation, while the nutrition department had utilised ₹67.93 crore (11.55%) of its ₹588-crore budget. At the other end, irrigation and flood control recorded the highest proportion of expenditure, using ₹259.96 crore, or 78.78%, of its ₹330-crore allocation. The energy department followed, spending ₹3,069.39 crore, or 77.98%, of its ₹3,936-crore budget. The welfare of SC/ST/OBC department spent ₹113.46 crore (53.27%) of its ₹213-crore allocation, while general education utilised ₹3,402.76 crore (52.41%) of its ₹6,493-crore budget. Urban development spent ₹1,913.01 crore, or 48.14%, of its ₹3,974-crore allocation.In absolute terms, the transport department recorded the highest expenditure at ₹4,863.02 crore, accounting for 41.09% of its annual allocation of ₹11,834 crore. General education and energy followed, with spending of ₹3,402.76 crore and ₹3,069.39 crore, respectively.Government projectsOfficials aware of the matter said lower spending in the first half of a financial year was not unusual, as departments generally accelerated expenditure in the second half. However, they attributed a significant portion of the current shortfall to delays in rolling out high-value schemes such as the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana.“An amount of ₹62,550 crore was allocated for planned expenditure by various departments. The implementation of the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana faced glitches, resulting in the non-utilisation of its ₹5,110-crore allocation. Had the scheme been rolled out smoothly, a substantial portion of this amount would have been spent. However, expenditure by other departments is picking up pace,” an official said.The labour department, meanwhile, was allocated ₹2,000 crore for the construction of industrial training institutes, but no expenditure had been recorded under this allocation, according to officials.Also Read | Delhi court frames charges against 4 teens for gangraping, killing 16-year-oldUntil October last year, the Delhi government spent 32.72% of the ₹59,300 crore allocated for plans and schemes. This was lower than the 37.67% expenditure recorded during the corresponding period in 2024-25, when ₹39,000 crore was allocated.The expenditure was 40.88% of the ₹43,700 crore allocation in 2023-24, 31.44% of ₹43,600 crore in 2022-23 and 37.65% of ₹37,800 crore in 2021-22. The figures show that spending till October has remained below 41% of the annual allocation in each of the past five years.Estimates vs actual expenditureThe slow pace of spending comes despite the finance department having issued directions in September asking departments to make realistic assessments of their funding requirements and ensure that projected allocations could be utilised within the financial year. It also cautioned against significant variations between budget estimates and actual expenditure, noting that unrealistic projections had attracted adverse audit comments in the past.The government has now begun preparing the budget estimates for 2027-28 and revised estimates for the current financial year. Chief minister Rekha Gupta has been holding meetings with departments to discuss their proposals and review expenditure.“The revised estimates will be tabled in the Delhi Assembly during the Winter Session, scheduled from December 18 to 23. The budget estimates for the next financial year will be finalised in January,” an official said.In March, Gupta presented a ₹1,03,700-crore budget for 2026-27, focusing on infrastructure, health, education, green initiatives and social welfare. Of the total, ₹62,550 crore was earmarked for schemes and projects, while the remaining amount was allocated towards establishment expenditure.

headline: Delhiwale: This way to Gali Hospital Wali
content: Intro: As part of the Walled City encyclopaediaSee the bicycle. It is standing well above the ground, in front of a rusting iron grille. The tyres are grey with dust, but you can still see the blue of the frame. Down below, pipes are running along the broken paving. Up above, wires are looping from one side of the street to the other. In between, there is just enough room to walk through.This dead-end Old Delhi gali opens onto Urdu Bazar. It is the 237th stop in a weekly series on the streets of the Walled City, their names and the life going on in them. What is this street called? Some are calling it Gali Hospital Wali, after the nearby Kasturba Hospital. Others are calling it Gali Peer Wali, after a Sufi mystic said to be buried nearby. Which peer baba? Nobody can say. The twin shrines of Hazrat Sarmad and Hazrat Hare Bhare Shah are about ten minutes away on foot.A man in a blanket is passing through. He calls it Gali Jagat Cinema Wali, after the long-shut cinema nearby. Actually, that name belongs to another street already visited in this series. Now look at the blue nameplate beside a brown iron door. It gives the house number and says GALI HOSPITAL WALI. The blue plate is the best clue so far.The brown door is ajar. Inside, tiles cover the walls and the fronts of the steps. Nobody is about. It is afternoon, but in here it could as well be midnight.Very little daylight is reaching the gali either. Yet there is more room here than you might think. Signs are pointing to Neha Guest House and Mustafa Guest House. Actually, it is a wonder that two guest houses can fit into this gali. One more arrow is pointing to Qureshi Kabab Corner. Where can an eatery possibly fit in here? A counter, perhaps, with a teeny-weeny space for a man to stand behind it.Now follow that arrow and step inside. Turns out it is no mere corner. It is a whole dining hall. Brown chairs with patterned backs stand around rows of tables, with room to walk between them. A red board displays newspaper clippings and photographs of the founder posing with famous people, including a former prime minister. On another wall, an old black-and-white photo of Jama Masjid shows a vast sweep of open ground in front of the mosque. It’s hard to imagine such emptiness in front of the mosque today.As you come out of the darkened gali into Urdu Bazar, a realisation suddenly hits you. In a medical emergency, an ambulance would have to stop right here, at the mouth of Gali Hospital Wali.

headline: Noida call centre bust: 9 trafficked foreigners still missing
content: At least nine foreign nationals – six Malaysians and three Indonesians – who were allegedly trafficked into India, confined in a paying guest (PG) accommodation and forced to participate in cyber fraud are still missing, Delhi Police officers said on Friday, a day after announcing the rescue of 164 people from what they described as a “cyber slavery and human trafficking network” operating out of a fake international call centre in Noida.Investigators privy with the case details said that 174 passports were recovered during raids at the building housing the PG accommodation and the call centre. Of these, 164 belonged to the rescued victims, while one belonged to 25-year-old Malaysian national Tan Guan Wei, who was arrested for allegedly running the operation on behalf of two absconding Indian handlers, Sunil Kumar and Sushil Kumar Bhati. Six Malaysians and three Indonesians remain untracedThe remaining nine passports belonged to six Malaysian and three Indonesian nationals who were also allegedly confined and forced to work as cyber fraudsters, an officer familiar with the investigation said. Sunil is suspected to be based in Malaysia, police said.“While efforts to locate the missing foreigners are ongoing, we will also approach the embassies of the two countries to know if they have any knowledge about their whereabouts. We have informed the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) and the Union ministry of external affairs (MEA) about the rescued foreigners and those still missing. We have sought information related to dates of the arrival of the nine individuals in India,” the officer said, requesting anonymity.The network, akin to syndicates operating in southeast Asia where Indians are often trafficked into cyber-scam compounds, is among the first of its kind busted in India involving foreign nationals allegedly brought into the country and forced to participate in cyber fraud, police said.Also read: Noida PG owner, broker booked after rescue of 164 foreign nationals from alleged cyber slaveryRescued victims to be repatriated after legal formalitiesThe 164 rescued Indonesians and Malaysians will be repatriated to their respective countries through the MEA and FRRO after the completion of the requisite legal formalities, a second officer said. They were handed over to the FRRO after medical examinations and other formalities. The agency has arranged accommodation and food for them in the city until their repatriation, the officer added. The embassies of both countries will also be involved in the process.On Thursday, the Delhi Police crime branch said the foreign nationals were allegedly made to carry out cyber fraud activities at a fake international call centre in Noida’s Sector 136. The crime branch’s inter-state cell (ISC) raided the facility on Wednesday night.“The racket was busted after ISC received a tip-off about a fake international call centre operating from a commercial tower in Noida. After verifying the information, a team raided the facility and rescued 164 Indonesian and Malaysian nationals,” special commissioner of police (crime) HGS Dhaliwal said.Also read: 164 foreigners rescued as Delhi Police bust cyber slavery racket in NoidaWhistleblower alerted policeInvestigators said the tip-off came through an email sent around 10 days ago by a 40-year-old Malaysian national, who was also allegedly trafficked into India on the promise of employment but was being forced to work without pay as a cyber fraudster. He was also asked to surrender his passport.“The person refused for both. He contacted some people known to him, who asked him to inform the Delhi Police about the syndicate. He found the crime branch’s email ID on the internet and sent an email, detailing everything about the syndicate’s activities. We approached him and sought a written complaint, based on which we registered a case, conducted the raid, rescued 164 victims and arrested his compatriot, Tan Guan Wei. The whistleblower is a key witness in our case,” joint commissioner of police (crime) Surender Kumar said.Also read: Fake job offers, seized passports: Inside Delhi's international human trafficking, cyber fraud racketVictims allegedly lured with job offers and brought to India on business visasThe rescued foreigners told investigators that they had been brought to India on the pretext of employment and other lucrative opportunities. They had arrived on business visas over the past four months, police said. Members of the syndicate allegedly seized their passports soon after their arrival.The victims were confined in a 65-room PG accommodation in a six-storey residential building in Noida’s Sector 128, which the two absconding Indian handlers had rented for ₹12.24 lakh a month. Their movements were restricted and access to phones controlled, police said.A senior officer associated with the operation said members of the network frequently assaulted those who resisted or refused to participate in the fraudulent activities. The victims were not allowed to leave the premises and were occasionally permitted to speak to their families back home only under close supervision.“They were served substandard food and forced to follow written scripts to cheat unsuspecting people in Indonesia and Malaysia through fraudulent investment platforms. They were tortured, harassed and threatened,” the officer said.

headline: Delhi civil defence holds emergency preparedness drill
content: New DelhiThe Delhi Civil Defence Corps on Friday conducted an emergency preparedness drill, set off by air raid warnings and blackouts, across all 13 districts of the national capital, officials said on Friday.A total of 4,217 civil defence volunteers participated in the exercise, which was conducted under the supervision of the director of civil defence and the divisional commissioner, in coordination with the Delhi State Disaster Management Authority and district disaster management authorities.The exercise simulated scenarios involving an enemy air strike, building collapse, resultant fires and unexploded bombs (UXB). Volunteers practised evacuation, search and rescue, first aid, firefighting, casualty management and blackout procedures, officials said. The drills were conducted at Indraprastha Apollo Hospital in Jasola, Dhaula Kuan Metro station, Kashmere Gate interstate bus terminal (ISBT), Gaffar Market, Reliance Mall in Vikaspuri and DLF Mall, among others.The exercise aimed to familiarise the public with safety measures during air raid warnings and blackouts, and emphasised the need to remain calm rather than panic during emergencies, officials said. The objective was to test coordination among the administration, civil defence personnel and the public, and simultaneously strengthening the city’s readiness to respond to potential emergencies, officials said.

headline: Delhi air quality may hit ‘very poor’ by Nov 29
content: The air quality in Delhi remained in the “poor” category on Friday, with the 24-hour average air quality index (AQI) recording at 226, as per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).Of the 57 monitoring stations that recorded data on Friday, 16 lodged “very poor” air, 26 saw “poor” AQI, and 15 were in the “moderate” category.The 24-hour average AQI on Thursday was 224 and on Wednesday, it was 220 -- both in the “poor” zone.The CPCB classifies an AQI between zero and 50 as “good”, between 51 and 100 as “satisfactory”, 101 and 200 “moderate”, 201 and 300 “poor”, 301 and 400 “very poor”, and 401 and 500 “severe”.Meanwhile, Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) chairperson Rajesh Verma on Friday reviewed the progress of the Emission Inventory and Source Apportionment (EI and SA) study for Delhi-NCR at IIT Delhi.The review covered updated emission factors and sector-wise inventory work for the 2026 base year, including transport, industries, open burning, households, road dust, construction, diesel generators, agriculture and other pollution sources.The Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), along with The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) and IIT Delhi, presented the progress of the emission inventory. IITM Pune presented the integration of the study with the Decision Support System (DSS).The India Meteorological Department’s Air Quality Early Warning System has forecast that Delhi’s air quality will remain in the “poor” category on November 28 before deteriorating to “very poor” on November 29. It is expected to return to the “poor” zone on November 30.Besides, Safdarjung recorded a maximum temperature of 28.6 degrees Celsius, 2.6 degrees above normal, while the minimum settled at 9.3 degrees Celsius, one degree below normal.

headline: MCD House clears 132+ proposals; 112 public spaces set to be renamed
content: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), at its House of Councillors meeting on Friday, approved more than 132 policy proposals, including naming and renaming 112 public spaces, and a proposal to recruit 2,500 additional sanitation workers, officials said.The House cleared proposals to name and rename 112 public spaces, including parks, roads, schools, and intersections. For instance, the entry point of Mehrauli near Adam Khan tomb (Bhool Bhulaiya) has been named Banda Singh Bahadur Chowk; the road near the Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital will be called DP Gupta Road; Bangla Chowk in Mehrauli has been renamed Heera Lal Chowk; the road outside Laxmi Narayan Mandir in Kalkaji has been named Laxmi Narayan Mandir Marg, among others.The House unanimously approved a proposal for recruiting 2,500 substitute sanitation workers to strengthen civic sanitation services in the city.”To ensure transparency, the entire recruitment process will be recorded on video. Furthermore, officials from various departments will be assigned on a rotational basis to prevent any bias in the process,” mayor Pravesh Wahi said.The corporation will soon issue advertisements, followed by the distribution of application forms at zonal offices on specified dates for the recruitment process, Wahi added.MCD is responsible for manual sweeping of 6,127 kilometers of roads and currently employs 57,000 sanitation workers. After two decades, the civic body will now recruit sanitation personnel directly.Councillors also raised issues of encroachment, pollution, pending funds and installation of LED streetlights in wards, demanding that responsibility for issuing pensions and other welfare subsidies be transferred to the MCD from the Delhi government.Leader of Opposition Ankush Narang, however, said the civic body needed to recruit more sanitation staff as many workers were retiring every month.Narang also questioned officials over recurring incidents of building collapses in the city and demanded action against those responsible. “Incidents of building collapse due to illegal construction activities have become regular. While people are losing their lives, the officials are hardly being punished,” he said.During the meeting, MCD approved the proposal to hand over the management of the Charti Lal Goel Heritage Park near Jama Masjid-Red Fort to the Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC) for 10 years.Other proposals cleared by the House include changes in the toll tax bylaws to upgrade the toll collection system with multi-lane, free-flow, barrier-less systems, procurement of 70 mechanical road sweepers, and allowing medical diagnostic imaging services in municipal hospitals on a PPP basis.

headline: Aadhaar authentication mandatory for Lakhpati Bitiya: Delhi govt
content: New Delhi: The Delhi government has made Aadhaar authentication mandatory for people to avail of benefits of its Lakhpati Bitiya scheme, and has also provided a slew of alternative mechanisms to potential beneficiaries who either do not possess an Aadhaar card of face difficulties in biometric verification.According to a notification issued by the women and child development department on November 18, a copy of which was accessed by HT , beneficiaries must furnish proof of possessing an Aadhaar number or undergo Aadhaar authentication to avail of benefits under the scheme.“Those who do not have an Aadhaar number must apply for enrolment before registering for the scheme. The department will also facilitate Aadhaar enrolment through its district offices for beneficiaries who have not yet enrolled,” it read.Under the Lakhpati Bitiya scheme, financial assistance—ranging from ₹11,000 at birth to ₹25,000 on admission to a four-year graduation course—is deposited in the girl child’s name at different educational milestones.Until an Aadhaar number is assigned, beneficiaries can receive benefits by producing their Aadhaar enrolment slip along with alternative documents: a bank or post office passbook with photograph, PAN card, passport, ration card, voter ID, MGNREGA card or driving licence.For biometric authentication failure, the government listed alternatives of iris scanning, face authentication and Aadhaar-based one-time passwords. “If these options are unsuccessful, benefits can be provided using a physical Aadhaar letter, with its authenticity verified through the QR code printed on it,” the notification read.The notification came into effect from the date of its publication in the official Gazette.

headline: Delhi, Bihar sign pact to expand bus services across 18 routes
content: New Delhi: The Delhi and Bihar governments on Friday signed a transport agreement to expand interstate bus services across 18 routes, aiming to provide year-round connectivity and make travel easier for nearly 2 million people from Bihar and Purvanchal living in the national capital.The agreement was signed in the presence of Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta. Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh and Bihar Transport Minister Damodar Rawat were also present.Under the agreement, Delhi has issued 216 permits to Bihar for operating buses on 18 routes connecting the national capital with Bihar. A quota of 12 permits each has been allocated to Delhi and Bihar for every route.The services will connect Delhi with 13 cities and regions in Bihar, including Patna, Gaya, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Bhagalpur, Muzaffarpur, Purnia and Kishanganj. Some cities, including Patna, Gaya and Muzaffarpur, will have more than one route connecting them to Delhi.Gupta said the initiative would benefit workers, labourers and students who frequently travel between the two states. She said the agreement reflected growing cooperation between Delhi and Bihar and would ensure better transport facilities for passengers.Singh said the services would provide relief to people who face difficulties travelling home during festivals such as Chhath, Diwali and Dussehra. He added that the number of buses would be increased according to passenger demand.The move follows increased demand for interstate travel. During Diwali and Chhath this year, 155 buses operated on routes connecting Bihar with Delhi and other states. Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 149 buses, including 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses, and plans to operate another 150 through the public-private partnership model.

headline: DU announces 2 new scholarships for regular students
content: Delhi University (DU) has introduced two new scholarships, proposals for which were approved by the university’s Academic Council at its 1028th meeting held on Friday.The Professor PS Grover Meritorious Scholarship, worth ₹50,000, will be awarded to regular students enrolled in the Master of Computer Applications and Master of Science (Computer Science) programmes.The Professor GC Maheshwari Annual Memorial Scholarship will be awarded to one male and one female student pursuing the Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) programme. Each recipient will receive ₹51,000 annually for the first 11 years, from 2026 to 2036. The amount will subsequently be doubled to ₹1.02 lakh per student per year for the next 10 years, from 2037 to 2046.Additionally, DU vice-chancellor Yogesh Singh, who presided over the meeting, directed all principals to ensure that regular appointments against all vacant posts are completed by March 31, 2027. Singh directed colleges to introduce Research Excellence Awards to further push for research-based learning in alignment with the National Education Policy.The council also gave approval to several syllabus frameworks, including Masters courses according to the Postgraduate Curriculum Framework 2024.Professor Maya John, a member of the council, submitted a dissent note raising concerns over several issues. Referring to changes in the MA History papers, John said the Standing Committee on Academic Affairs’ directives to department heads to revise the syllabus undermines the academic autonomy of individual departments.

headline: SC seeks report on NBCC progress in completing stalled Supertech projects
content: The Supreme Court on Nov 27 sought a report on progress achieved by NBCC in completing stalled Supertech housing projects to assess whether it should continue with the construction, amid allegations of slow progress by homebuyers.The court will also assess proposals from interested developers before making a decision.A bench of justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “There are some allegations by homebuyers on the speed of implementation of projects by NBCC. We would like to have a report from the amicus curiae advocate Rajiv Jain giving a prima facie opinion on the viability of other proposals and the stage of development achieved so far by NBCC.”The court passed the order while hearing pleas filed by homebuyers complaining about the NBCC for not finishing 16 stalled Supertech projects entrusted to it by the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) in December 2024.On October 27, the top court indicated that it would dissolve the Apex Court Committee (ACC), presently overseeing the construction of the 16 Supertech projects, and appoint a receiver or a court-appointed committee as had been done for the stalled Amrapali and Unitech projects. In the same hearing, the court had pulled up NBCC, observing that “nothing is happening” with regard to the stalled Supertech projects.The court asked amicus Jain to examine an alternative proposal submitted by homebuyers, suggesting an infusion of ₹1,500 crore for completing the stalled projects. “We need to know how viable these proposals are,” the court said.The court also said that if NBCC is to continue with the work, there is a separate petition, wherein NBCC has demanded enhanced fees for implementing the project. “By now, we have got some experience and history in these matters as we would like to emulate the Amrapali model and appoint a receiver,” the bench said.Attorney general (AG) R Venkataramani, who is also the receiver in the Amrapali matter, told the court that if NBCC is to continue, it would be seeking exemptions under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) Act.The bench indicated it may ask the AG to act as a receiver in case of a court-monitored committee to implement the construction plan, following which the AG said that the Amrapali matter has reached its fag end and he has asked the bench concerned to relieve him.The bench said, “It is very important that we have an independent receiver as the matter will involve preservation of assets, valuation of assets, distribution and allotment of assets.”Also Read: Centre seeks early Supreme Court hearing on uniform builder-buyer agreements to protect homebuyersA group of homebuyers, led by senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, suggested appointing the ACC chairperson and former top court judge justice Krishna Murari as the receiver. However, the court said, “We will cross that bridge later,” as it adjourned the matter awaiting the report from the amicus.Also Read: Noida Sports City: Supreme Court clears registry for 7,802 flats, bringing relief to homebuyersNearly 50,000 housing units are stuck in the 16 distressed Supertech projects in Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Karnataka.While taking over the 16 projects, the NBCC sought a separate 1% marketing fee over and above the 8% PMC fee as a condition for undertaking the work. However, the NCLAT order restructured the fee matrix as a consolidated 8% (7% PMC + 1% marketing), which, according to NBCC, undermined project viability and disincentivised the implementing agency.

headline: BJP government displays items ‘worth lakhs’ at house of former-Delhi CM | Latest News Delhi
content: The Delhi government on Friday organised a tour for mediapersons of the former official residence of former chief minister and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convener Arvind Kejriwal at 6, Flag Staff Road, announcing that the bungalow will soon be opened to the public.Dubbed “Sheesh Mahal” by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the residence was at the centre of a political controversy over the alleged exorbitant expenditure on its renovation and furnishing.Chief minister Rekha Gupta urged people from Delhi as well as Punjab to visit the bungalow, accusing the AAP of misusing public money during its tenure in the Capital. “Just as the people of Delhi wanted to see this ‘Sheesh Mahal’, the people of Punjab should also see it. They (AAP) looted Delhi first, and now they are looting Punjab,” Gupta said.Public Works Department (PWD) minister Parvesh Verma said the residence would be opened for public viewing after an inspection by the Delhi Assembly’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC). “We have decided to open the bungalow for public viewing to show how taxpayers’ money was spent on building this luxurious residence. Construction work at the bungalow did not stop even for a day during the Covid pandemic, when people were scrambling for oxygen,” Verma alleged.AAP did not respond to HT’s request for comment on the matter on Friday. However, AAP has consistently denied the allegations of expenditure and also questioned the veracity of allegations in the past.Also read: Delhi govt opens Kejriwal’s former residence as ‘Sheesh Mahal’ row returns to focusEntry plans and items on displayMeanwhile, officials said the government plans to introduce an online ticketing system, with entry likely to be priced at ₹20. Free entry may be offered to senior citizens and college students.Price tags have been placed across the residence to highlight the cost of various items, officials said. These include a dining table priced at ₹13.07 lakh and a television set with its console costing ₹12.36 lakh. A board installed outside the bungalow puts the renovation cost at ₹58.83 crore.Also read:₹20"> Delhi government to open Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ for public visits, tickets likely at ₹20Political controversy and audit findingsThe bungalow became a major political flashpoint ahead of the February 2025 Delhi Assembly elections. Kejriwal and his family lived there for nearly a decade, from 2015 until October 2024.The controversy gained fresh momentum after a Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report, tabled in the Delhi Assembly in March this year, pegged expenditure on the renovation and construction at ₹33.66 crore, against an initial preliminary estimate of ₹7.91 crore.The audit flagged procedural lapses, cost escalation and gaps in documentation. It noted that the built-up area increased from 1,397 square metres to 1,905 square metres, while the Public Works Department revised its preliminary estimates four times.The report also found that ₹18.88 crore was spent on items involving superior specifications, artistic and antique features, and ornamental works. It flagged the award of additional works worth ₹25.8 crore to the existing contractor without inviting fresh tenders.

headline: Delhi AQI today: Air quality worsens to 454 on Saturday, vehicular emissions largest contributor to PM2.5 pollution
content: Delhi AQI today: The air quality index (AQI) on Saturday, 28 November, deteriorated further, hovering in the 'hazardous' category at 454 at 6:51 AM. The reading was close to the seven-day peak of 449 recorded at 6 AM on 21 November.The national capital's lowest AQI reading was recorded at 3:01 PM on Friday, when it fell from 273 in the morning to 144, before worsening again in the evening. Around 7:30 PM, the AQI started hovering above 300 and has maintained an upward trend since then. Readings stayed in the 300-400 range before midnight, then rose above 400, according to data from AQI.in. Delhi's seven-day AQI peaked at 449 at 6 AM on 21 November. The seven-day period ended on 27 November, with the lowest reading recorded at 170 at noon on 26 November. Early morning readings generally hovered between 300 and 450 on several days during this period.At 6:11 AM on Saturday, Delhi's PM10 level stood at 428 micrograms per cubic metre, significantly higher than the World Health Organization's (WHO) 24-hour guideline of 45 micrograms per cubic metre. Carbon monoxide was reported at 3,395 parts per billion (ppb), while nitrogen dioxide measured 25 ppb and sulphur dioxide nine ppb. Ozone was recorded at two ppb. The temperature was 25°C, humidity stood at 30%, wind speed was 3.6 km/h, and the UV index was 3.1.According to AQI.in, Bettiah in Bihar reported the worst air quality on Saturday, with an AQI of 682, followed by Ghazipur at 558 and Saharsa in Bihar at 488. Srinagar's AQI also hovered in the hazardous category at 480.How AQI.in and CPCB classify air qualityFollowing the US AQI scale, AQI.in classifies air quality as follows:- 0-50: Good- 51-100: Moderate- 101-150: Poor- 151-200: Unhealthy- 201-300: Severe- 301 and above: HazardousAccording to PTI, which cites AQI data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), the classifications are different. The CPCB categorises AQI readings as follows: 0-50 as 'good', 51-100 as 'satisfactory', 101-200 as 'moderate', 201-300 as 'poor', 301-400 as 'very poor' and 401-500 as 'severe'.Vehicular emissions remain the biggest contributor to PM2.5 pollutionVehicular emissions emerged as the largest contributor to PM2.5 pollution in estimates recorded on Friday morning. Of the 57 monitoring stations in the city that recorded data on Friday, 36 were in the 'poor' category, while 17 reported AQI readings in the 'moderate' category and four were in the 'very poor' category. The monitoring station at Terminal 3 of the Indira Gandhi International Airport reported the worst air quality, with an AQI of 346.Between 1 AM and 9 AM on Friday, real-time source apportionment estimates for Delhi showed that vehicular emissions were the biggest contributor to PM2.5 pollution, accounting for 32% of the estimated load. This was followed by biomass burning at 22.8%, secondary organic aerosols at 14%, and secondary inorganic pollutants at 12.3%.Waste burning accounted for 10.7% of the estimated pollution load, followed by industrial emissions at 4.2%, mineral dust and ash at 1.8%, coal combustion at 1.5% and mixed combustion at 0.8%.

headline: Delhi Police testing app to flag dark spots, fix streetlight complaints in real time
content: NEW DELHI: The Delhi government is developing a mobile application to help police personnel identify and report dark spots in the city in real time, with complaints automatically routed to the agency concerned for redressal, The Hindu has learnt. The application, being developed by Geospatial Delhi Limited, is currently being tested by police personnel on the ground to assess its usability and address operational issues before its rollout. The initiative seeks to streamline a process that was earlier largely manual, involving monthly assessments by the police to identify poorly lit areas, followed by correspondence with different civic agencies to get the defects rectified. Deputy Commissioner of Police (PCR) Satyawan Gautam said the existing system often faced delays because of confusion over the jurisdiction of various agencies, including the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) and Delhi Development Authority (DDA). “Earlier, there was often confusion over which agency had jurisdiction over a particular location — whether it fell under the NDMC, MCD or DDA. Once a dark spot was identified, the police had to write to the respective agency through email, which made the process cumbersome and time-consuming. With the new application, officers will be able to report the issue directly from the location, with its latitude and longitude coordinates automatically captured and the complaint routed to the concerned agency,” he said. Their feedback will help address glitches and streamline the process before the platform is put into regular use. Mr. Gautam said the system was expected to make reporting and redressal faster and more efficient. The initiative comes amid concerns over the safety of public spaces in the Capital, particularly poorly illuminated parks and stretches frequented by women and children. The alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old girl inside Aastha Kunj Park in September had brought public-space lighting and security under scrutiny, prompting directions from Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu for safety audits and improvements in surveillance and illumination. On Thursday, a 10-year-old girl was disrobed inside a park in north-west Delhi’s Bharat Nagar. City dark spots Meanwhile, the latest streetlight assessment, dated November 26, identified 180 dark spots across 16 zones in Delhi. Of the 22,059 streetlights and poles assessed, 5,080, or nearly 23%, were found defective. Outer Delhi recorded the highest number of dark spots at 53, followed by Central Delhi with 35 and South Delhi with 19. Shahdara reported 14 while West Delhi had 11 and Northeast Delhi 10. North Delhi had nine, Southwest Delhi eight and Southeast Delhi seven. New Delhi and Dwarka reported no identified dark spots while Northwest Delhi had one. Rohini and Outer North reported two each. East Delhi and the Metro zone had five dark spots each. The distribution of defective streetlights, however, presented a different picture. Dwarka reported the highest number at 1,065 out of 3,797 streetlights and poles, followed by Southeast Delhi with 871 out of 1,718 and South Delhi with 683 out of 2,447. Outer Delhi reported 369 defective lights out of 555, while West Delhi had 343 out of 921. Shahdara recorded 323 defective lights out of 548, meaning nearly 59% of its assessed streetlight infrastructure was faulty. Outer Delhi had the highest proportion, with about 67% of its recorded streetlights and poles found defective. Southeast Delhi also had more than half its recorded streetlights and poles defective, at nearly 51%. In comparison, Central Delhi, despite having 3,410 streetlights and poles — the second-highest inventory among the zones — reported only 150 defective units, or about 4.4%. New Delhi had 68 defective lights out of 903, while East Delhi reported 130 out of 1,699. The application is expected to bridge the gap between identifying poorly lit locations and getting the responsible agencies to act on complaints. Real-time reporting and automatic jurisdiction mapping are intended to reduce delays in repairs.

headline: Delhi CM flags off Delhi-Bihar interstate bus service
content: Interstate bus connectivity between Delhi and Bihar is set to improve, with the governments of the two states signing a reciprocal transport agreement covering 18 routes to facilitate regular services throughout the year.The initiative is expected to benefit nearly 20 lakh workers and labourers from Bihar and Purvanchal living and working in Delhi, who often face difficulties travelling to their hometowns, particularly during festivals.The agreement was signed on Friday in the presence of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta. The Chief Minister also flagged off the Delhi-Bihar interstate bus service from the Maharana Pratap Inter-State Bus Terminal (ISBT) at Kashmere Gate. Bihar Transport Minister Damodar Rawat and Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh were also present.Under the agreement, the Delhi Transport Department has issued 216 permits to the Bihar Government for operating buses on 18 interstate routes. A quota of 12 permits each has been allocated to Delhi and Bihar for every route, facilitating organised bus operations between the two states.Speaking on the occasion, Rekha Gupta said, “The Delhi Government is continuously working to provide better facilities to every citizen living in Delhi or Bihar.”She said lakhs of people from Bihar contribute to Delhi's growth through their hard work, while students from the state also come to the Capital for education and employment. The improved connectivity would make travelling between the two states more convenient for these residents.Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said the initiative would provide relief to nearly 15 to 20 lakh people from Bihar and Purvanchal living and working in Delhi, particularly during Chhath, Diwali and Dasehra, when demand for travel to their hometowns rises sharply.He said the number of buses would be increased according to passenger demand and requirements. “The facility will further strengthen social and cultural ties between the two states," he said.Bihar Transport Minister Damodar Rawat said the agreement would provide direct bus connectivity from Delhi to 13 cities and regions in Bihar, including Patna, Gaya, Darbhanga, Madhubani and Bhagalpur. He thanked the Delhi Government and the Chief Minister for supporting the initiative.The decision to expand regular services follows the response to special buses operated during festive seasons. In 2025, a total of 210 corporation and public-private partnership (PPP) buses were deployed to facilitate passenger movement during festivals. During Diwali and Chhath this year, 155 buses operated on routes connecting Bihar with Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Jharkhand.To strengthen the service, the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses for interstate operations. It also plans to deploy another 150 buses under the PPP model. The expansion is aimed at ensuring that passengers have access to regular services throughout the year instead of depending largely on special festive arrangements.The 18 routes will connect Delhi with Araria, Bihar Sharif, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada, Patna and Purnia. Multiple routes have been identified for Patna, Gaya and Muzaffarpur, with buses passing through major cities and transport centres in Uttar Pradesh before reaching Delhi.

headline: Delhi HC seeks Satyendar Jain’s response to ACB plea challenging bail in corruption case
content: The Delhi High Court on Friday sought a response from Aam Aadmi Party leader Satyendar Jain on a plea filed by the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) challenging the order granting him bail in a corruption case linked to the Delhi Jal Board. Justice Sachin Datta issued notice to Mr. Jain on the Delhi government’s ACB petition and listed the matter for further hearing on December 22. The ACB has challenged the trial court’s September 3 order granting bail to the former Delhi Minister, arguing that the court failed to properly assess the evidence against him. The trial court had criticised the ACB for arresting Mr. Jain towards the end of the investigation, observing that “a sudden arrest at the tail end of the investigation, without strong reasons and without a change in circumstances, tends to invite criticism that it is arbitrary”. Mr. Jain was arrested in the case on August 18 and remanded to judicial custody the following day. Challenging the bail order, the ACB argued that the trial court had overlooked the alleged conspiracy involving public officials, a private technology provider and intermediaries. “The trial court failed to consider that the prosecution case is based upon a coordinated conspiracy in which public officials, a private technology provider and intermediaries allegedly performed complementary roles. Direct evidence of every conversation or payment involving the principal accused cannot be insisted upon at the stage of bail,” the agency told the court. While granting bail, the trial court had cited several grounds, including the “unexplained and extraordinary delay” of 27 months between the registration of the FIR in May 2024 and Mr. Jain’s arrest in August this year. The case relates to a tender awarded to M/s Euroteck Environmental Private Limited when Mr. Jain was the Water Minister. The ACB has alleged that the tender conditions were manipulated and the process made deliberately technology-centric to favour the company, restricting competition and giving an undue advantage to a selected private entity.

headline: When a child speaks up: DSLSA trains teachers on responding to abuse
content: New Delhi: A child growing unusually quiet, an otherwise regular student missing school, or someone confiding in a teacher about online abuse or sexual assault — recognising the signs is often only half the challenge. For Deepti Arora, an Education, Vocational Guidance and Counselling (EVGC) counsellor at a west Delhi school for 12 years, the bigger question has been what to do next: whom to report to, when to involve the police and how to initiate the process.These questions were at the heart of a training programme organised by Delhi State Legal Services Authority (DSLSA) Friday, where around 146 teachers-in-charge from schools across five district legal services authorities were familiarised with child protection procedures, reporting mechanisms and access to legal aid under Surakshit Bachpan Abhiyan and the NALSA (Child-Friendly Legal Services for Children) Scheme, 2024.The programme marks the campaign’s second phase, focused on equipping teachers to respond to abuse disclosures and connect children with legal aid. The first phase involved school outreach to sensitise staff on child protection.“We are trying to create a support system within schools so that children can approach teachers and counsellors themselves, knowing there is someone they can turn to and that their concerns will be addressed in their familiar setting,” said Judge Sunena Sharma, member secretary, DSLSA, explaining the objective of the programme.Across four sessions, teachers were familiarised with legal aid resources, coordination mechanisms and child protection laws. In one session, judicial officers Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan and Deepali Srivastava, among others, stressed the need for “immediate intervention”, explaining reporting procedures and access to free legal aid through Delhi’s 12 district legal services authorities.For Arora and several other participants, however, acting promptly often meant navigating layers of authority within schools, leaving them unsure of whom to approach and how to initiate a complaint. “I would always feel I had to report such incidents to my principal first. Fortunately, my principal has been supportive and helped take complaints forward so the police could begin an investigation. But not every teacher may have that support. Knowing now that we can approach the district cells directly and reach out through helpline numbers has taken away that doubt,” she said.The uncertainty, participants said, was compounded by the stigma surrounding child sexual abuse cases and apprehensions about getting drawn into lengthy legal proceedings. Dr Manju, another participant, said the complexity of legal procedures often made teachers hesitant to intervene.“Teachers, like anyone else, associate ‘court kachehri’ with endless complications. There is a hesitation about getting involved, especially when you are unsure how much you can help. Although laws such as the POCSO Act and other child protection measures are strictly followed, simplifying this for us, makes it less intimidating,” she said.One such session also focused on recognising warning signs and making children feel safe enough to speak. Participant Shweta Chaudhary flagged the dilemma teachers often face in assessing whether a complaint is “genuine”. Addressing this, Bharati Ali, board director of Help for Children in Need Foundation, said, “Speaking to a child in a comfortable setting can help them open up. If suspicions persist, teachers can approach the DLSA counsellor, who can speak to the child and, if necessary, involve the parents while maintaining confidentiality.”
